decisions.statement: `refuse_personal_access_token` (a route dependency) is on every route that grants or revokes access, creates an account with a typed password, issues the SCIM token, changes single sign-on or `advanced-settings`, and on leaving an organisation; the media-token URL can no longer mark a file confidential.
decisions.rationale: Guard: `test_session_only_routes.py` walks the route table for the whole class. `advanced-settings` was added after the register review because it sets the token lifetime cap and the mail relay (, asked to fix).
decisions.section: Security hardening of the whole product (fixes and guards)

decisions.title: P2, P4
decisions.statement: The scope of a token (organisations, projects) is applied centrally in `accessible_project_ids` (`rbac.restrict_to_session_scope`), and to the organisation list and record, memberships, reviews due and notifications; this amends the earlier "personal endpoints untouched by token scoping" decision ().
decisions.rationale: A redeemed reset link and switching two-factor off revoke the person's tokens; a routine password change does not (, reverses the recorded independence for recovery paths only).
decisions.section: Security hardening of the whole product (fixes and guards)

decisions.title: C1 to C5 (import)
decisions.statement: A person named in a bundle must hold a role in the target organisation, else they are unmatched exactly like an unknown address (also removes the registered-address oracle).
decisions.rationale: Replayed audit events are attributed to the importer with the original actor and time in the detail. An organisation setting `allow_imported_approval_state` (default allowed, ) returns imported records to drafts when off, through the modules' existing `template_reset` hooks run in `keeping_history()` (archived records and authorship kept), and the import audit counts records that arrived beyond draft. Bundles are bounded by entry count, per-entry size, JSON size and compression ratio, and a corrupt entry is a 400. An `image/*` claim must match the bytes (`trusted_content_type`); the email logo is a raster picture only.
decisions.section: Security hardening of the whole product (fixes and guards)

decisions.title: SC1 to SC3, M1, M2, S7, NEW-1
decisions.statement: SCIM `active` is parsed strictly; operations and names are type-checked (400, not 500); lists page in SQL; a platform administrator or deactivated account is not provisioned.
decisions.rationale: The MCP sign-in page mints a personal access token and discards the session token (: the token is scoped to the person's organisations and cannot manage the account). The server instructions say tool text is data. The identity provider client caps responses at 1 MiB, pins the connection to the checked address, caches discovery for 5 minutes and is rate-limited per address.
decisions.section: Security hardening of the whole product (fixes and guards)

decisions.title: G1 to G5, G7
decisions.statement: The demonstration generates its own secrets into an untracked file and refuses placeholders ().
decisions.rationale: The observability profile binds to loopback, has no anonymous access, requires `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, and Alloy reads containers through a read-only socket proxy. The backend port binds to loopback by default. Keys can be rotated (`APP_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS`, `scripts/rotate_secret_key.py`); an unreadable stored secret is counted, logged and checked at start-up. A TOTP code is accepted once and attempts are counted under a row lock. Passwords are 8 to 72 bytes and not on a built-in common list (`services.password_policy`).
decisions.section: Security hardening of the whole product (fixes and guards)

decisions.title: Audit completeness (H2 to H4)
decisions.statement: Comment add, edit, reaction and attachment removal on requirements, change requests and actions are audited (comment id and a body digest, never the body) and kept off the History and Activity pages (`AUDIT_TRAIL_ONLY_ACTIONS`); display name changes, second-factor enrolment, avatar removal, report run output deletion and requirements report downloads are audited; removing a comment attachment now…
decisions.rationale: deletes the stored object. Guard: `test_mutating_routes_audited.py` follows calls from every mutating handler to an audit write and requires a stated reason for each exemption. Audit rows are append-only for the runtime database role (`AUDIT_RUNTIME_ROLE`, `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL`, `services.audit_protection`); two roles, not a trigger, because the table owner can drop a trigger (). It is off until an operator provisions the role (`docs/deployment.md`).
decisions.section: Security hardening of the whole product (fixes and guards)

decisions.title: S3 to S6, NEW-2, NEW-3, C6
decisions.statement: The front end sends a Content-Security-Policy built at container start from checked values (`script-src 'self'` plus listed origins, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri`, `form-action`), HSTS behind an HTTPS proxy, a Permissions-Policy and cache headers; API JSON is `no-store`.
decisions.rationale: Actions are pinned to commit SHAs with Dependabot for actions, pip, npm and Docker; publishing is limited to `main` and to a `release` environment; CI gains Bandit (high severity), Semgrep (error severity, Python and front end), Gitleaks over history and tree, and a weekly OWASP ZAP baseline against the test stack, each failing on a high finding with no baseline (). `.gitleaks.toml` lists seven earlier commits whose fake test credentials cannot be rewritten; the sources were changed so the working tree is clean. Findings the first run raised were fixed in code (a weak hash used for a name, a world-writable directory, `text()` with a variable that is now a bound `set_config`); the DDL in disaster recovery keeps a reasoned `nosemgrep`. The converter's memory ceiling, queueing and restart policy were corrected and a person's conversions are rate limited.
decisions.section: Security hardening of the whole product (fixes and guards)

decisions.title: Logo band colour (login page: Login page
decisions.statement: `LogoBand` (a full-width band across the top of the card, the logo only; the title stays on the card, ) inside `LoginBrandHeader`, so `LoginPage` (including its two-factor step) and `OrgLoginPage` get it with no per-page code.
decisions.rationale: `GET /orgs/by-slug/{slug}/login-info` returns the resolved colour (a public presentation value; no private field added) and the public platform settings return the chosen one (null = top bar).
decisions.section: Logo band colour (login page, outgoing email, reports) (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: Reports draw a band only when a colour is chosen
decisions.statement: (, to veto; the plan left this to be decided).
decisions.rationale: Applying the default (dark) band to reports would hide every existing dark logo on white paper, an upgrade regression with no action to undo it. An organisation with a white logo sets a colour, which then covers reports too. The login page and email use the default, as the user asked.
decisions.section: Logo band colour (login page, outgoing email, reports) (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: Footer position of the signed-out pages: Setting and scope
decisions.statement: (, asked at the start; the recommended platform-only setting was declined).
decisions.rationale: `footer_position` on `server_settings` (not null, default `after_content`, so an upgrade changes nothing) and on `organizations` (null follows the platform), migration 0170. A plain validated string, not a database enum: `services.branding.FOOTER_POSITIONS` holds the values (`after_content`, `bottom_of_page`), so a further layout is a registry entry, not a migration. Resolved organisation, then platform, by `services.branding.footer_position`; an unknown stored value reads as the default. It applies on an organisation's own sign-in page (the login lookup returns the resolved value); every other signed-out page has no single organisation and uses the platform value. The footer's content stays the platform's company details in both cases (, to veto: the position is a presentation choice, the identity of the operator is not an organisation setting).
decisions.section: Footer position of the signed-out pages (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: Platform value is never cleared
decisions.statement: (): the update schema refuses `null` for it, as for the accent colour; an organisation clears its own with `null`.
decisions.rationale: Both are partial updates, so Server details, Platform branding and the organisation pages cannot overwrite it; the audit event names the field and no value. It travels in the organisation bundle and is re-validated on import (an unknown value imports as unset). A public presentation value on an unauthenticated lookup: no private field added.
decisions.section: Footer position of the signed-out pages (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: Footer position of the signed-out pages: Separator rule
decisions.statement: (, to veto; the request named only line ends).
decisions.rationale: A separator appears only between two groups on the same line, so no line begins or ends with one. It is drawn by the stylesheet in the gap before a group marked `data-joined`, which `AppFooter` sets after layout from the groups' vertical offsets (a `ResizeObserver`, re-measured when the company details load). The separator is out of flow, so marking a group never moves it to another line, which removes the mark-and-reflow loop a separator that takes width would cause. Before the first measurement, or with scripting off, none is drawn (the worst case is a missing separator, never a dangling one). The alternative, a pure-CSS flex row where each group carries its own separator, cannot hide the one that starts a wrapped line, so it cannot meet the rule. It applies to every page's footer, not only the sign-in page, because it is one component.
decisions.section: Footer position of the signed-out pages (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: Original email is an import option
decisions.statement: (): `PeopleChoices.keep_original_email`, off by default.
decisions.rationale: Off, the history detail keeps only the original person's name; on, it also keeps the address. Either way the stand-in row never holds the address.
decisions.section: Bundle import: imported people (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: The badge covers principal fields
decisions.statement: (): owners, assignees and reviewers go through `PrincipalBadge`.
decisions.rationale: Author and actor names elsewhere are plain text from many response schemas and show the stored name, "Imported person" is not appended; touching each would be a per-schema change for little value, since an imported person's name is already the bundle's. Raise it if a badge is wanted on those.
decisions.section: Bundle import: imported people (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: Event filter reduced to Change, multi-choice
decisions.statement: (): Created, Edited, Status changes and Deleted, several at once; the four metadata kinds moved into the Type list.
decisions.rationale: The `kind` parameter keeps all its values for links already shared.
decisions.section: Phase 59: History filters — Type as a two-level list, Change filter, capitalised Events (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: Type is a grouped multi-choice list; a heading is selectable
decisions.statement: (): one dropdown (`MultiSelectDropdown`, gaining `heading`, `indent` and `section` for any grouped list), `type` repeatable and a new `group` parameter.
decisions.rationale: Groups come from the registry: Records under the owning module's name (Core first), Metadata in a fixed order. A type of a chosen group shows ticked and unavailable, so the URL never holds a redundant pair.
decisions.section: Phase 59: History filters — Type as a two-level list, Change filter, capitalised Events (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: Metadata groups
decisions.statement: (, Q4): Links and files, Tags and places, Access, Structure and settings, Other.
decisions.rationale: Comments is not a group: discussion comments stay behind **Include discussion comments** (they are not entity events). A module declares its non-record event types through `ModuleDefinition.activity_metadata_types`; `*_link` and `*_definition` need no entry; an unclassified type is listed under Other so it is never unreachable. A test fails for a logged literal entity type that lands in Other.
decisions.section: Phase 59: History filters — Type as a two-level list, Change filter, capitalised Events (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: Website documentation update: Screenshots re-captured
decisions.statement: () at 1440×900 from the rebuilt stack after a reset and reseed with `seed_demo_data.py` (so the user's own test data is not shown): projects, project stages, project history, files, overview, project settings and modules, organisation overview, users, modules, details and files, server management (users) and organisations, preferences and notifications.
decisions.rationale: The sign-in page was captured in the logo band phase and is unchanged. Not re-captured: the module, report designer and compliance screenshots, whose pages did not change in this plan; their navigation rail predates the new order and is replaced when each is next captured.
decisions.section: Website documentation update (2026-11-11)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Decisions recorded
decisions.statement: (, 2026-11-04, in the plan's section 6): deployments are out of scope; elements are separate from project components, with a component mapping that only suggests allocations (Q1); separate from Module 6, linked by "Describes" (Q2); ports are a child list of an element (Q3); a baseline snapshots the architecture and there are no per-edit versions (Q4); roll-up is in the first version (Q5); the…
decisions.rationale: seeded type lists and shapes stand (Q6); the first of Modules 16, 17 and 18 to be built extracts the shared canvas wrapper (Q9); interchange is JSON in and out, Mermaid and Structurizr DSL out only (Q8); organisation-owned elements and sharing through collections (Q10).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 0: decisions and reading results (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Proposed shape for Phase 8
decisions.statement: (, pending User confirmation): the module owns its snapshot tables (`architecture_baselines`, `architecture_baseline_items` holding the serialised state of each element, connection, diagram and placement), with a nullable `baseline_id` linking to a stage baseline.
decisions.rationale: A new generic `ModuleDefinition` hook, called from `create_baseline_for_stage`, lets any module take its own snapshot when a stage is locked; a snapshot may also be taken manually. Reason: a polymorphic `BaselineItem` would change a requirement-bound core table and its export, while a module-owned snapshot keeps module data out of core and gives Module 6 the same hook for Design revisions.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 0: decisions and reading results (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Reading 2: proposed links
decisions.statement: `ChangeRequestProposedLink` belongs to a change request version and carries an outcome (merged, declined, skipped); there is no general store of suggested links.
decisions.rationale: It is not reused. Suggested allocations are computed at read time from the component mapping, and accepting one calls `services.link_authoring.create_link_for_artefact` (bulk accept is a loop in one transaction). Dismissing a suggestion is not stored in the first version (; a stored dismissal is added only when a person asks for it).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 0: decisions and reading results (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, open questions answered: Baseline storage
decisions.statement: `BaselineItem` becomes polymorphic, replacing the earlier proposal of module-owned snapshot tables (the Agent recommended the module-owned shape, to avoid changing a requirement-bound core table; the User chose the single shared table).
decisions.rationale: It stays generic: an `item_type` validated against the artefact-type registry (as `ArtefactLink.source_type` is), an `item_id`, and a JSON `snapshot`. `requirement_id` and `requirement_version_id` become nullable and are unchanged for requirement items, so existing baselines are untouched. This is also the shape Module 6 needs for Design revisions.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 0: open questions answered (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, open questions answered: Manual baselines
decisions.statement: `Baseline` gains a `kind` column (stage or manual) beside a nullable `stage_id`, with a check constraint: a stage baseline has a stage, a manual one has none.
decisions.rationale: Code that reads `stage_id` is reviewed for the null case, and the project export and import carry `kind` and the new item columns with a round-trip test.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 0: open questions answered (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, open questions answered: Snapshot timing
decisions.statement: Both: a snapshot is taken automatically when a stage baseline is written, and an architect can take one manually at any time.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 0: open questions answered (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, open questions answered: Snapshot owner
decisions.statement: The owning module serialises its records through a new generic `ModuleDefinition` baseline snapshot provider, called from `create_baseline_for_stage` and from the manual action.
decisions.rationale: Core stores and lists items only. Ports, placements and other child rows are included by the module, and a Restricted-classified or personal-data column is never serialised.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 0: open questions answered (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, open questions answered: Suggested allocations
decisions.statement: A dismissal is stored: a small table of dismissed (requirement, element) pairs with undo, an audit event per dismiss and restore, and a bundle entry (this reverses the earlier "no stored dismissal" default, which is withdrawn).
decisions.rationale: A dismissal is hidden while the mapping stays the same and is cleared if the element's component mapping changes.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 0: open questions answered (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Phases added or split
decisions.statement: The shared canvas is its own phase (Modules 16 and 17 reuse it); the editor is split into interactions and accessibility with export; baselines are split into a core change and the architecture snapshot with a compare view; the security review of the visibility resolver is its own phase before close-out.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture): plan restructured to 17 phases (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Component placement
decisions.statement: An element has no `component_id` column.
decisions.rationale: Its component and category come from the shared placement table, which also gives categories, the create form field and the list filter. Consequences: an element may sit in several components (this widens the earlier "one component" answer), an organisation-owned element is never placed, and component-based suggestions apply to project-owned elements only; a shared element is allocated manually.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture): plan restructured to 17 phases (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Element in use elsewhere
decisions.statement: Retiring keeps it visible to its users but out of pickers; deleting is blocked while another owner uses it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture): plan restructured to 17 phases (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Connection detail
decisions.statement: A diagram has a `connection_detail` setting, off by default: plain lines between connected elements (several between one pair collapse into one); on, typed, labelled and coloured connections.
decisions.rationale: This replaces the Agent's earlier idea of per-diagram connection type filters.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture): view toggles, connection detail and symbol library (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: View toggles
decisions.statement: A diagram can hold named toggles with a default state; an element or connection belongs to a toggle by hand, by rule (element type, domain, connection type, tag) or both.
decisions.rationale: The viewer's choice is not saved; exports use the saved defaults or the states named in the call. One toggle mechanism replaces separate filters, so a data flow can show firewalls and private endpoints only when wanted.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture): view toggles, connection detail and symbol library (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Hidden transit elements
decisions.statement: Hiding an element in the middle of a path joins its neighbours with a dashed bridged line that lists the hidden hops (depth capped at 12).
decisions.rationale: One resolver applies toggles, bridging, roll-up and line merging in that order, for the screen, the server SVG, reports and exports.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture): view toggles, connection detail and symbol library (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Symbol library
decisions.statement: SVG symbols are uploaded to organisation and project libraries (hide, restore and nested fallback as for the type vocabularies, the fallback being A small generic built-in set is seeded on a fresh install.
decisions.rationale: Vendor icon packs are never bundled. A symbol is a library entry, not an artefact type: it has no code, link, search or placement.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture): view toggles, connection detail and symbol library (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: One table per vocabulary, owned by a project or an organisation
decisions.statement: `TypeVocabulary` stores an organisation row plus a per-project override row (`name_override`, `display_order_override`), which cannot carry the extra columns these vocabularies need (shape, domain, colour pair, line style, directional, and later a symbol) without a second set of override columns.
decisions.rationale: The plan's table (`project_id` or `organization_id`, exactly one, enforced by a CHECK) is used instead. A project hides an organisation default with a `ProjectDefinitionSuppression` tombstone (`architecture_element_type`, `architecture_connection_type`) and adds its own row instead of overriding one. Names are unique per owner in the database, and a project also rejects a name its effective list already shows (ignoring case). A project's own rows follow the organisation's defaults in the list and are reordered among themselves.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 1: skeleton and vocabularies (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Nested projects (Phase 1)
decisions.statement: A project with no configuration of its own (no row and no hidden default) shows the nearest ancestor that has some, else the organisation's list (cycle-safe, capped at 50).
decisions.rationale: The first change in such a project copies the ancestor's rows and hidden defaults into it (`materialize_inherited`), so a change never edits the ancestor. Nothing is seeded for a project, so the fallback always applies at the start; this is the same effect as root-only seeding.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 1: skeleton and vocabularies (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Seeding and the existing-organisation backfill
decisions.statement: The plan said seeds run on a fresh install only.
decisions.rationale: Module state (the server default table) still seeds nothing on upgrade, but the migration backfills the default types into organisations that already exist, because the module is off for them and an organisation that switches it on later would otherwise find both vocabularies empty. Rows are invisible while the module is off, so this changes nothing for a deployment that never enables it. The backfill is idempotent (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 1: skeleton and vocabularies (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Connection types carry a line style, not a shape
decisions.statement: The plan's "as element types plus `directional`" is read as the same name, domain and colour fields, a `line_style` (`solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`) in place of an outline shape, and `directional` (`true` is one-way, `false` is two-way).
decisions.rationale: A connection type has no symbol. Element shapes are `rectangle`, `rounded`, `cylinder`, `hexagon`, `ellipse`, `parallelogram`, `folder`, `chip`; a seeded type takes its colour pair from its domain. `symbol_id` is added with the symbol library.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 1: skeleton and vocabularies (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: The diagram type is registered in Phase 5, not here
decisions.statement: The plan's status line said this phase registers three artefact types.
decisions.rationale: A registered type must have a summary, search, record-table, probe and generator entry that read a table, and the diagram table does not exist until Phase 5, so registering it now would need empty providers that the registry tests cannot tell from real ones. Phase 5 registers `architecture_diagram` with its table.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 2: elements, ports and connections (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Optimistic version is a counter the save quotes
decisions.statement: An edit, status change, port change or archive advances it; a save that quotes an older value is refused with 409, and the row is locked (`SELECT ...
decisions.rationale: FOR UPDATE`) while it is checked. A save that changes nothing does not advance it. Port edits advance the element's counter so an editor holding a stale copy is told. The counter is not carried in a bundle (an imported record starts at 1). An import quotes the record's current version, so a file is applied to the record as it is now.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 2: elements, ports and connections (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Status moves between any two states
decisions.statement: The plan said `draft` to `active` to `retired` with no approval gate.
decisions.rationale: With no gate there is no safety reason to forbid a move back (reactivating a retired element), so any move to a different status is allowed. The one rule is integrity: an element cannot be retired or archived while a child is neither retired nor archived. **Save and activate** applies (`activate` on both create payloads; the create path needs only the manage permission and no second person's approval is skipped); the review table in "Phase 16: one People page and Save and activate" gains a row when Phase 7 builds the form.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 2: elements, ports and connections (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Tree and reference rules
decisions.statement: A parent belongs to the same project and is not archived; a move may not create a cycle; depth is capped at 12 and a move counts the subtree it carries.
decisions.rationale: A connection joins two different, unarchived elements of its project; a port belongs to its end's element; changing an end's element without naming its port drops the old port. Deleting an element needs no children and no connection; deleting a port needs no connection using it; a type a record or port uses cannot be deleted (409), but hiding an organisation default stays allowed. The foreign keys to types and elements carry no `ON DELETE` clause (checked at the end of the statement), so deleting a project can remove its types, elements and connections in one statement; the service, not the database, enforces "in use".
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 2: elements, ports and connections (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Link types reuse two core defaults
decisions.statement: The plan listed "Allocated to / Allocates" and "Verifies / Verified by", but the core defaults already include "Allocated to / Has allocated" and "Verified by / Verifies" (unrestricted), and a seed with different reverse phrases is ignored with a warning.
decisions.rationale: The module therefore seeds only Constrains, Affected by, Concerns and Describes (each restricted to its ends) and uses the core phrases for allocation and verification: a requirement is "allocated to" an element, and an element or connection is "verified by" an action. A test pins the phrases and the restrictions.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 2: elements, ports and connections (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Risk's "Impacts" placeholder is left as it is
decisions.statement: Risk Management's "Impacts" seed (risk to requirement, design or `system_element`) names a type that was never registered; the plan's "Affected by / Affects" runs the other way (element or connection to risk) and is the architecture's link.
decisions.rationale: Retargeting "Impacts" at `architecture_element` would give two phrases for one relationship, so it is not changed here; if the User prefers one phrase, remove the other seed.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 2: elements, ports and connections (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Links panel creator and record paths
decisions.statement: Both types are listed in `not_creatable_from_links` for now: an element's creator is its form dialog and a connection needs two elements, and both come with the screens in Phase 7, which removes the element entry.
decisions.rationale: The frontend registers the record paths (`artefactPaths`, `artefactListPaths`, status labels) so a link, search hit or notification resolves; the pages those paths open are added in Phase 7, and the module has no navigation entry until then, so nothing offers the paths in the meantime.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 2: elements, ports and connections (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Two entry points, one subset rule
decisions.statement: `Viewer.of_user` applies every route in the plan (own project, owner access, organisation administrator, collection grants to the project or its ancestors with descendants, grants to a group the person belongs to).
decisions.rationale: The core hooks that see a project and not a person (the link graph, link validation, the global search, the summary providers) can only call `Viewer.of_project`, which applies the own-project and project-grant routes. It is always a subset of the person's own view, so a hook can show less than the person may open but never more. A test pins this for a project grant, a group-only grant and a project with no grant.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 3: collections, organisation tier and the visibility resolver (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: No list_for_organization
decisions.statement: Core resolves an organisation-qualified code (`ACME-ELM-001`) for any member of the organisation from that hook, which would show an organisation element that nobody shared with them.
decisions.rationale: An organisation-owned element is therefore not resolved by its qualified code in the code finder; it is reached through the organisation list, the project's shared list, the link finder and the search of a project it is granted to.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 3: collections, organisation tier and the visibility resolver (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Delete is blocked while shared
decisions.statement: An element cannot be deleted while it, or an ancestor, is in a collection that has a grant, while any connection (of any project) ends at it, or while a record outside its owner links to it (any link for an organisation element).
decisions.rationale: The reason is integrity: deleting would silently remove other projects' connections and links. Retiring keeps it visible to its users and out of the pickers (`elements/shared?open_only=true`), and a new connection to a retired shared element is refused; revoking the sharing lifts the block.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 3: collections, organisation tier and the visibility resolver (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: A group in use
decisions.statement: `PrincipalReference` for a grant is not mandatory: deleting a group removes its grants (access only narrows), unlike a restricted-audience field.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 3: collections, organisation tier and the visibility resolver (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Connection ends in a file
decisions.statement: The CSV writes an end the project owns by its bare code and an end another owner shares qualified by that owner's code (`PLAT-ELM-004`), because a bare code would name the project's own element of that number on re-import.
decisions.rationale: The parser resolves a qualified code through the resolver and refuses one the person cannot read. An organisation-tier import writes and reads organisation elements only.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 3: collections, organisation tier and the visibility resolver (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Built-ins are code, not files
decisions.statement: A built-in row has a `builtin_key` and no file; `symbols.BUILTIN_SVG` draws it on a 64 x 64 grid in `currentColor`.
decisions.rationale: The plan's `is_builtin` column is therefore a property (`builtin_key IS NOT NULL`). Reason: no storage or quota use, nothing to corrupt or relicense, and a bundle can carry a built-in by key alone. A built-in cannot be renamed (a bundle names it by key); it may be reordered, hidden per project, and deleted by the organisation administrator while unused, because no safety reason forbids a delete (Prefer the Flexible Reading) and the alternative leaves every picker with ten entries nobody can remove. The migration backfills the built-in rows (not any type assignment) for existing organisations, following the vocabularies' migration; it seeds no module state.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 4: symbol library (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, symbol library: One importer for uploads
decisions.statement: `symbols.prepare_symbol_upload` converts an EPS or PDF when the converter is configured, then accepts a vector drawing only (a raster does not scale on a diagram) and stores the *sanitised* copy (`services.report_svg.sanitize_svg`: allow-listed elements and attributes; entities, internal DOCTYPE subsets, external references and scripts refused or removed).
decisions.rationale: The sanitiser runs again whenever a symbol is read. `MAX_SYMBOL_BYTES` is 512 KB (): an icon is drawn at a few dozen pixels, and a larger limit invites a photograph inside an SVG and slow diagrams.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 4: symbol library (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Who may assign a symbol
decisions.statement: A project's element type or element: its effective library (the organisation's symbols it has not hidden, and its own, or its configuration source's).
decisions.rationale: An organisation-owned type or element: the organisation's own symbols only, since a project's symbol would reach people who cannot open that project (the rule the report images already follow). Hiding stops new use only; an assignment keeps working. A symbol an element type or element uses cannot be deleted (409); the row and its file go when it is not in use.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 4: symbol library (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Who may read a symbol
decisions.statement: `symbols.visible_symbol_ids`: an organisation symbol, by the organisation's members; a project symbol from its own project or a project that inherits its library, by a person who can open that project, and by whoever can read an element drawn with it (directly or through its type) under the visibility resolver.
decisions.rationale: Anything else is 404, indistinguishable from a missing symbol. The CSV `Symbol` column prints a name only for a symbol the reader may read.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 4: symbol library (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Hidden means the element or an ancestor is switched off
decisions.statement: A switched-off element takes its subtree with it; a rule or a manual member names the top.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Bridging follows directions and keeps one shortest path per pair
decisions.statement: A one-way connection is an arc source to target, a two-way one an arc each way; a chain of hidden elements is followed to 12, the line lists every hidden hop in order, and a pair reached both ways is one two-way line.
decisions.rationale: Keeping one path per pair of visible ends stops a dense hidden region from making the work grow exponentially.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: A line is dashed only when every connection behind it is rolled up or bridged
decisions.statement: A merged plain line that includes a direct connection stays solid.
decisions.rationale: With connection detail on, direct connections keep their own line and only rolled-up or bridged ones are grouped by pair, with a count.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: An element the viewer cannot read is never hidden, matched by a rule or bridged through
decisions.statement: It stays a locked node (its code only) so a bridged line can never reveal a middle element, and a toggle can never be used to probe whether a hidden element has a given type or tag.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Collapsed is stored and returned, not read by the resolver
decisions.statement: The plan says a connection with both ends inside one placed parent is hidden "until that parent is opened as its own diagram or marked expanded".
decisions.rationale: The resolver reports those connections per node (`internal_connection_ids`) and draws none, so "open as its own diagram" is the way to see them; the editor (Phase 8) decides what `collapsed` does to the box.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, diagram API: Whole-diagram version lock
decisions.statement: Moving a box, adding a toggle and editing the name advance the same counter, so a stale editor is told before it overwrites anything.
decisions.rationale: A save that changes nothing does not advance it. Layout save replaces the placements and notes (the editor owns undo); unplacing never deletes the element and deleting an element removes its placements by cascade.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, diagram API: Who can be placed
decisions.statement: An element the viewer can read: the project's own or one another owner shares.
decisions.rationale: A new placement needs an unarchived element and, for another owner's, one that is not retired (as for a connection); a placement already on the diagram is kept on every later save, so a revoked or retired element never makes a diagram unsaveable and shows as a locked placeholder.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, diagram API: Connections drawn
decisions.statement: The project's own, leaving out archived and (unless `include_retired`) retired ones, as the lists' "Open only"; an archived or retired element stays drawn, flagged by its status.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, diagram API: Toggle rules
decisions.statement: A rule stores vocabulary row ids, domains and tag names in the database (so a rename does not break it) and names the types by name in a bundle.
decisions.rationale: Rules are evaluated over every element the diagram involves (placed elements and connection ends), so a transit element that is not itself placed can still be switched off. A saved default state applies unless the request names `toggle_on` / `toggle_off`, which are never saved.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, diagram API: Server SVG
decisions.statement: Light-theme colours on a transparent background; every name, code, note and label is XML-escaped and stripped of control characters; a symbol is the one embedded markup and only its sanitised form (`symbols.symbol_svg`) is used, falling back to the type's shape; served with the same restrictive `Content-Security-Policy` as a symbol and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, diagram API: No import for diagrams
decisions.statement: The record table exports; `NOT_IMPORTABLE` says a layout is authored visually.
decisions.rationale: The project bundle carries the diagram itself.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 5: diagram API (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Create and edit share one field group
decisions.statement: `ElementFields` is the group both forms use; ports are entered in the create form (the API takes them with the element) and edited one change at a time on the element page through the same `PortList`, because a port has its own endpoints and no version.
decisions.rationale: `ConnectionFormModal` is one component for create and edit. An element or connection created from the list, an element's page or the Links panel runs through one hook each (`useCreateElement`, `useCreateConnection`), so quick links and tags are applied in every place.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 7: lists, detail pages, tree and settings screens (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Type vocabularies do not use ProjectTypeVocabularyPanel
decisions.statement: That panel is built around the override model (rename, reorder and disable an organisation type inside a project); the Architecture vocabularies are hide-only for an organisation default and carry more than a name (domain, shape or line style, colours, symbol).
decisions.rationale: `ArchitectureTypesPanel` is therefore the shared `DefinitionList` with an Edit dialog, and `DefinitionList` gained `isReadOnly` (grid layout), documented in the style guide's organisation-defaults pattern. The hide and restore interaction is the shared one (`confirmDelete`, `RestoreOrgDefaultsButton`). The 409 "still in use" conversion moved from a private function of `TypeVocabularyPanels` to `utils/blockedError.ts` so both use one implementation.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 7: lists, detail pages, tree and settings screens (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Sharing screen
decisions.statement: `CollectionsPanel` manages a collection's members and grants for a project or an organisation.
decisions.rationale: The plan asks for each route that grants access to be listed on an element; no endpoint returns that, and building one is a visibility-resolver change that belongs with the security review. The element's Sharing card therefore lists the collections the element is a direct member of (an owner's view) or says it is shared and read-only (a recipient's). An element also reaches people through a collection holding an ancestor; the card does not show that route. Recorded as a gap for Phase 15, not hidden.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 7: lists, detail pages, tree and settings screens (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Organisation elements have no page of their own
decisions.statement: They are managed in the organisation panel (create, edit, status, archive, collections).
decisions.rationale: Search finds an organisation element only through a project that can read it, which opens the project route, so no `orgArtefactPaths` entry is needed. An organisation element takes no tags, quick links or placements (they are project-keyed).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 7: lists, detail pages, tree and settings screens (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Element is creatable from the Links panel
decisions.statement: `not_creatable_from_links` loses `architecture_element`; `creatableRecordTypes.json` and the module's `linkedRecordCreators` follow, and the existing gate test (`test_creatable_record_types.py`) proves the `can_create` flag equals the endpoint for every person.
decisions.rationale: A connection stays excluded (it needs two elements) and so does a diagram (Phase 8).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 7: lists, detail pages, tree and settings screens (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Editing model
decisions.statement: Moves, resizes, additions, removals and note edits are local with an undo/redo history (100 steps) and are stored together by Save with the diagram's version.
decisions.rationale: Toggles and the connection-detail switch are settings, stored when changed; they advance the same version, which the hook keeps current. A save clears the undo history (the stored layout is the new baseline and notes take their stored ids). A reload merges the freshly read view into the unsaved layout (membership and geometry stay local, display data comes from the server), so nothing unsaved is lost. Lines and the boxes a switch hides are worked out in the browser (next entry).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 8: diagram editor interactions (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Hidden and unreadable boxes are kept
decisions.statement: A box a switch hides stays in the layout and is sent on Save; a box the viewer cannot read is drawn as a locked placeholder (code only) and is also kept.
decisions.rationale: Saving can therefore never unplace something the editor did not show.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 8: diagram editor interactions (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Lines are resolved in the browser
decisions.statement: The first build drew the lines of a box added in the editor only after Save, because the one resolver is on the server; the User rejected that (a box and its connections must appear together, and a round trip per edit is slow on a high-latency link, when the browser has the compute).
decisions.rationale: The editor now loads the diagram's model data (`GET .../diagrams/{id}/model`: the project's own elements, those shared with it and every connection end, their parents, the live connections as the viewer may read them, the connection types, and for each view switch the elements and connections it hides, with its rule already evaluated) and runs a TypeScript port of `resolve()` (`diagramResolver.ts`, shaping in `diagramLines.ts`) on every edit and every switch flip. Nothing computed there is stored or sent: Save sends only boxes and notes, and the server validates them (permission, version lock, one box per element, the element placeable by this viewer, finite boxes, notes belonging to the diagram), so a wrong line can never change data. The server still decides visibility (the model endpoint omits names, types, symbols and ports of what the viewer cannot read) and stays the authority for the first load (`GET .../view`), the SVG and documents.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 8: diagram editor interactions (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Kept equal to the server
decisions.statement: `frontend/src/modules/architecture/diagramResolverCases.json` holds 23 scenarios whose expected results the server's resolver produced; `test_architecture_diagram_resolver_cases.py` fails when the file is out of date with `diagram_resolver.resolve` (refresh with `UPDATE_RESOLVER_CASES=1`), and the `DiagramResolver` story runs the port over every case.
decisions.rationale: `test_architecture_diagram_model.py` feeds the endpoint's data through the Python resolver for every switch state and both connection-detail settings and requires the same lines, hidden boxes and internal connections as `GET .../view` (the test fails if the scenario stops reaching bridging, roll-up, merging, internal connections or hidden boxes), and pins the statement count flat as the project grows. The line shaping (labels, counts, hops) has its own stories. A change to the rule is made in both resolvers.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 8: diagram editor interactions (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Security review of the model endpoint
decisions.statement: Identified: leaking a name, type or symbol of an element the viewer cannot read (a locked entry carries its code only, a connection to it comes from `connection_outs`, which blanks the locked end; a backend test pins that the name appears nowhere in the response); leaking another project's or organisation's elements (candidates are the project's own plus `granted_element_ids`, the same set the…
decisions.rationale: shared list returns; the diagram is looked up within the project in the URL, another project's diagram is 404); a reader without access (the same `architecture_diagram` sub-component gate and project membership as `GET .../view`). Accepted: the `parents` map includes the parent id of a locked element, because a connection rolls up through it exactly as on the server; the id is already named by the connection the viewer may read, no name or type comes with it, and the view's roll-up already reveals the relationship. Not remediated further: a read of the model costs one pass over the project's elements and connections, the same order as `GET .../view`, which already loaded every connection.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 8: diagram editor interactions (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Server-writing actions save first
decisions.statement: Drawing a line between two boxes (which creates a real connection with the existing connection form, source and target preselected) and deleting an element store a pending layout before they run, so the reload after them cannot drop or resurrect a box.
decisions.rationale: Creating an element or a connection reads the model again so the new record's parent and ends are known.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 8: diagram editor interactions (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Shared canvas additions
decisions.statement: `resizable` / `onNodesResize` (React Flow's resizer on the selected node, reported once when it ends, a top or left resize counted as part of the resize and not a move), `onDropItem` with `GRAPH_DROP_MIME` and a node `caption`.
decisions.rationale: Nothing architecture-specific entered the core component.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 8: diagram editor interactions (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Keyboard operation
decisions.statement: Selecting, moving and the palette were already operable by keyboard.
decisions.rationale: Added: **Alt with an arrow key** resizes the selected node by 10 (minimum 80 by 40, reported once per press as a resize), **Delete or Backspace** asks the consumer to delete the selection (new generic `onDelete` prop; the canvas still deletes nothing, and a read-only canvas ignores the key and does not mention it), and the Selection card gained **Connect to**, a list of the other visible boxes that starts the same connection step as drawing a line (the only pointer-only action before). In the editor Delete takes a box or note off the diagram as an undoable local edit; deleting the element stays the separate, confirmed action. The canvas's spoken help mentions each key only when the page enables it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9: diagram accessibility and export (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Exports use the server's drawing
decisions.statement: The plan said PNG and SVG are made in the browser.
decisions.rationale: A browser renderer would be a third drawing of the diagram beside the screen and the server SVG, with its own line routing, label wrapping and symbol embedding to keep equal, which is the risk the plan names ("exports that differ from the screen"). Instead the editor asks the server for the saved diagram drawn for the switch states on the page (`GET .../svg` with `toggle_on`/`toggle_off`, the drawing a report shows) and saves it as SVG; the PNG is that SVG drawn on a canvas in the browser (`utils/svgToPng.ts`: loaded as an image from a Blob URL, never inserted into the page; opaque white background; scale 2, lowered to keep the longest side within 8192 pixels). Consequences, accepted: the file is the light-theme drawing, not the dark canvas; the export is of the **stored** diagram, so a pending layout is saved first (the same rule as drawing a line or deleting an element) and a failed or conflicting save cancels the export. File names are `DGM-001-name-slug.ext`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9: diagram accessibility and export (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Security review of the Mermaid and export paths
decisions.statement: Identified: a name, code, protocol or diagram title that ends the quoted label, starts a directive (`%%{`), or adds markup; a hidden or unreadable element named in the text; another project's or a non-member's read; a stored-script SVG drawn to PNG.
decisions.rationale: Remediated by design and pinned by tests: every user text is passed through one escape (control characters become a space; `# " < > & \`` become Mermaid entities), the title comment is a single line that cannot begin a directive, and a test feeds a hostile name, protocol and title and requires that every line after the header still matches the two shapes the exporter writes; the text is built only from the resolved view, which already applies the viewer's visibility (a locked node gives its code only), and a toggled-off element's code is absent from the output; the route uses the same `architecture_diagram` gate and project lookup as `/view` and `/svg` (another project's diagram is 404, a non-member gets 404), with `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `nosniff`; the PNG path draws the server's SVG, which escapes every text and embeds only the sanitised symbol markup, as an image (script does not run in an image). The statement-count test for the view and SVG now also covers the Mermaid route, so it reads the diagram in bulk. Verified that a sample covering every shape, arrow, label and escape parses as a valid flowchart with the Mermaid parser the docs site uses.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9: diagram accessibility and export (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Connection types are a tree of any depth, and a type may have several parents
decisions.statement: Chosen over a flat group label and over a two-level grouping.
decisions.rationale: A group is itself a usable connection type, which is how a hardware connection starts as "some form of comms" and is fixed as I2C or SPI after detailed design. Stored as a parent link table; filters by a type expand to descendants. Agent notes accepted by the User's choice: a type with several parents needs cycle and depth checks, every filter must expand descendants, and a migration seeds nothing, so existing organisations add their own groups.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 1: the User's first review of the built screens (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 1: Guidance is soft
decisions.statement: A domain filter with "Show all types", suggested types per element type, and warnings; no allowed-pair matrix.
decisions.rationale: Agent reasoning: a firmware service on a board legitimately uses an API, and a hard matrix refuses unforeseen legitimate pairs.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 1: the User's first review of the built screens (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 1: Attach points
decisions.statement: Eight per box; the nearest pair by default; a person can drag an end to another point and it is stored. : the anchor belongs to the drawn line, keyed by the diagram and the pair of placed elements, so a merged or rolled-up line has one anchor.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 1: the User's first review of the built screens (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 1: Editor and navigation
decisions.statement: Tabs Drawing and Configuration (view switches move to Configuration), "Add to diagram" as a menu button like the report blocks, and one System Architecture navigation entry with Elements, Connections and Diagrams tabs.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 1: the User's first review of the built screens (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, the connection type tree: Which parents are allowed
decisions.statement: A type's parents are rows of its own tier or, for a project type, an organisation default the project lists.
decisions.rationale: An organisation type can only sit under organisation types, because a project's type would reach people who cannot open that project; another organisation's id is refused as "not a type this owner can use" (tested). A link to a parent the project has since hidden is kept when the row is edited (hiding stops new use only), but cannot be newly chosen.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9a: the connection type tree (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, the connection type tree: Deleting a group
decisions.statement: The links go with it and its members become top-level types; a type a record uses is still never deleted (the existing 409).
decisions.rationale: Blocking the delete of a group with members was rejected as an unforeseen-workflow restriction.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9a: the connection type tree (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: Descendants everywhere a type is filtered
decisions.statement: The connection list filter (API, and the client-side filter on the page), the record-table export filter and the diagram switch rule (`matched_by_rules` takes the expansion computed once per call, so a view stays flat in the number of switches) all treat a group as itself plus everything beneath it.
decisions.rationale: There is no type filter in search or report fields today, so nothing to expand there; a future one must use `closure_of`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9a: the connection type tree (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, the connection type tree: Nested projects
decisions.statement: The links follow the types: a child project that changes an inherited configuration copies the ancestor's rows and re-points each copied link at the copy of its parent (an organisation parent is shared).
decisions.rationale: Tested; the ancestor is untouched.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9a: the connection type tree (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture, the connection type tree: Fresh-install seeds
decisions.statement: Groups Network, Serial bus, Power, Wired signal, Software interface and Data exchange, the earlier types placed under them, and two "Unspecified" types for the case where nothing is known yet.
decisions.rationale: Agent detail: the seeded type "Power" is itself the group (a name is unique within an owner), so there is no separate leaf.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9a: the connection type tree (2026-11-12)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Nothing is enforced
decisions.statement: There is no allowed-pair table and no server check of a connection's type against its ends: a firmware service on a board legitimately speaks an API, and an unforeseen legitimate pair would be refused (Prefer the Flexible Reading).
decisions.rationale: A test saves a software type between two hardware sensors. The guidance lives in the form only (`connectionGuidance.ts`, pure functions with stories).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9b: soft guidance for connection types (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture: The picker
decisions.statement: A type fits an end when either is `any` or the domains are equal; the picker offers the types that fit both ends, puts the types suggested for the two ends' element types first in a "Suggested" group, and shows a "Show all types" switch (with a count of what is hidden) when any are hidden.
decisions.rationale: A suggestion is listed whatever its domain, and counts as a fit for the pair: a type suggested by either end raises no warning. A new connection's type follows the guidance (the first suggested, else the first that fits) until a type is chosen, so an untouched default never keeps a type that does not fit in the list; an edited connection keeps its own type in the list. A type that fits neither end shows a non-blocking warning naming each end. An end whose element type is not in the project's list (an element shared from another owner) imposes no domain and suggests nothing.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9b: soft guidance for connection types (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Nested projects (Phase 9b)
decisions.statement: Suggestions follow their element type: a child project that changes an inherited element configuration copies the rows and their suggestions (same connection type ids).
decisions.rationale: When the child later copies the connection types too, its own element types are re-pointed at the copies; an element type still inherited from the ancestor keeps the ancestor's ids, which the picker ignores when they are not in the child's list (an unknown id suggests nothing). The copy and the remap are tested.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9b: soft guidance for connection types (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: State survives a change of tab
decisions.statement: The pending layout, selection and undo history live in the page (`useDiagramEditor`), and only the panel contents mount and unmount, so no state is lifted or duplicated.
decisions.rationale: The canvas remounts on return; the Configuration tab says when the drawing has unsaved changes. Save stays on the Drawing tab only.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9c: editor tabs and the Add menu (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Add menu
decisions.statement: The palette card is replaced by `DiagramAddMenu`, a `MenuButton` with the element types grouped by domain ("New software element", "New hardware element", "New software and hardware element"), then "Add existing elements" and "Add note" under "Other".
decisions.rationale: The old per-type tiles and their duplicate "New X" accessible names are removed (`DiagramPalette` deleted).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9c: editor tabs and the Add menu (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Draggable menu items
decisions.statement: A generic `ActionMenuItem.onDragStart` makes an item draggable; the menu stays open for the drag and closes at `dragend` (closing at `dragstart` would unmount the drag source and cancel the drag in some browsers).
decisions.rationale: It is a generic extension of the shared menu, not an architecture-specific branch; the drop-on-canvas path (`GRAPH_DROP_MIME`) is unchanged.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9c: editor tabs and the Add menu (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture, attach points: The rule
decisions.statement: A box has eight points: the middle of each side and the four corners.
decisions.rationale: A line uses the pair of points nearest each other (least squared distance, so no square root and both languages agree to the last bit). Boxes side by side have their facing corners exactly as close as their facing sides, so a tie goes to the sides, then to the fixed order top, right, bottom, left, top right, bottom right, bottom left, top left. One rule, two implementations: `diagram_points.py` (the server SVG) and `components/graphAttachPoints.ts` (the canvas, and the Selection card). `graphAttachPointCases.json` holds 16 shared cases, written by `test_architecture_diagram_points.py` and checked by a Storybook story running the TypeScript port; a change to the rule is made in both (as for the line resolver).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9d: attach points (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: An end can be left open
decisions.statement: A stored anchor has a source point and a target point, either of which may be empty.
decisions.rationale: Dragging one end therefore fixes that end only; the other stays automatic and becomes the point of its box nearest the fixed one. Forcing both to be stored would freeze the end the person did not touch at whatever happened to be nearest at that moment. Both empty is not stored (an empty list entry is refused; choosing Automatic for the last fixed end removes the anchor).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9d: attach points (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: Keyed by the drawn line
decisions.statement: The anchor joins the two placed elements a line is drawn between, so a merged or rolled-up line has one anchor for all it stands for, and an anchor applies to a line drawn the other way round with its ends swapped.
decisions.rationale: A save refuses a pair given twice in either direction, an end that is not placed on the diagram, a line to itself and a value outside the eight. An anchor whose line is not drawn at the moment (a view switch hides an end, or roll-up draws another pair) is kept and unused; one whose box is no longer placed is removed (by the layout save, by unplacing and by deleting the element).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9d: attach points (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture, attach points: Straight lines
decisions.statement: The canvas draws straight lines between points (it drew right-angled step lines before).
decisions.rationale: A step line leaves a corner at a right angle to a side, which reads badly from a corner point, and the server SVG has always drawn straight lines, so the screen and the document now show the same line. Parallel lines between the same pair are still separated only in the server SVG.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9d: attach points (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture, attach points: Dragging an end
decisions.statement: Dragging an end of the selected line to another point of the same box stores that point as an unsaved edit (one undo step; Save stores it with the layout).
decisions.rationale: Dropping an end on a different box changes nothing: a line's ends are its connection's elements. Dragging from a point to another box still only starts a connection and stores nothing. The keyboard route is two lists in the Selection card ("Line starts at", "Line ends at"), each Automatic or one of the eight points, with Automatic naming the point it would use.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9d: attach points (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: One page, one navigation entry
decisions.statement: The module has a single entry, "System Architecture", opening `/projects/:projectId/modules/architecture` (`SystemArchitecturePage`) with the shared `Tabs` Elements, Connections and Diagrams.
decisions.rationale: The backend manifest declares one entry with `nav_sub_components_any` (element, connection and diagram), so the entry is offered while any of the three is on, through the existing generic mechanism; `additional_nav_entries` is no longer used by the module.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9e: one System Architecture page (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: The tab is a query parameter on one route
decisions.statement: `?tab=elements|connections|diagrams` rather than three paths under a layout route, so each list keeps its own filters in the same address, the list-position and back-link mechanisms (which key on path plus query) work per tab, and `listBackTarget` with `?tab=connections` already returns to the right tab.
decisions.rationale: An address with no or an unknown tab is replaced by one naming the first enabled tab, so a saved position is always keyed per tab.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9e: one System Architecture page (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: A tab whose sub-component is off is not offered
decisions.statement: It follows the rule the navigation already applies (`disabled_sub_components`): an address naming a disabled tab opens the first enabled one.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9e: one System Architecture page (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: Each tab keeps its filters
decisions.statement: The shell saves a tab's filters (its query without `tab`) in `sessionStorage` as they change, per project and tab, and restores them on returning to the tab.
decisions.rationale: Storage is guarded; blocked storage opens a tab without filters.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9e: one System Architecture page (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: The lists stay ordinary ListPageLayout pages
decisions.statement: The shell hands each list `chrome` (the tab strip and the list column's tab-panel attributes) which the list passes to `ListPageLayout`'s `tabs` and `contentProps`, with the shared title "System Architecture".
decisions.rationale: A list rendered without the shell (stories) has no tab strip. The Elements tab still has its own List and Tree view tabs inside the list column, so that tab shows two tab strips; this is a known deviation from the style guide's one-level tab preference, kept because moving the view switch is a separate change to the Elements page (revisit when Elements gains a view control in the title row).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9e: one System Architecture page (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Earlier addresses keep working
decisions.statement: `/elements`, `/connections` and `/diagrams` redirect (replacing the history entry, keeping their query) to the matching tab; record pages stay at their own paths.
decisions.rationale: Every internal link to a list (`artefactListPaths`, back links, the delete redirects, the Sharing page) uses `architectureTabPath`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9e: one System Architecture page (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: Default tab and a remembered tab
decisions.statement: The System Architecture page opens on Diagrams.
decisions.rationale: The tab last chosen on the strip is kept per person across projects in this browser (`localStorage`, guarded), so the navigation entry reopens it. A link that names a tab (a back link, a search hit, the Links panel) opens that tab and never changes the remembered one; only a choice on the strip does. A remembered tab whose sub-component is off falls back to Diagrams, else the first enabled tab. Server-side storage was offered and not chosen.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 2: Opening zoom
decisions.statement: The shared canvas has `fitMaxZoom`; the editor passes 1, so a small diagram opens at 100% (box text at the size of the page's text) and a large one still fits.
decisions.rationale: The default of 2 is unchanged for other canvases.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: No list toggle in the editor
decisions.statement: The editor passes `showViewToggle={false}`; the Outline is its text alternative.
decisions.rationale: The shared canvas keeps the toggle for other consumers.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 2: Outline tab
decisions.statement: The editor tabs are Drawing, Outline and Configuration (`?tab=outline`).
decisions.rationale: The Outline tab keeps the toolbar and the Selection card beside it, so choosing a row, Connect to, removing a box and Save all work from it, and the selection is page state shared with Drawing. Given up: the Outline is not visible while drawing, and a row chosen in the Outline shows on the canvas only when Drawing is open.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 2: Diagram settings gear
decisions.statement: `DiagramSettingsButton` (the shared `SettingsPopoverButton`) beside Export holds the connection-detail switch, stored at once as before; it is marked when detail is on.
decisions.rationale: Configuration keeps the view switches only. `DiagramConnectionDetailPanel` is removed.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 2: Edit in a modal
decisions.statement: The Selection card's Edit element opens the same `ElementFormModal` as the element page.
decisions.rationale: Save stores the change with the element's version lock and audit event, then reloads the element list and merges the diagram view (`reload(false)`), so a pending layout edit is kept. A shared or unreadable box has no Edit.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 2: Ports from the diagram
decisions.statement: The Selection card lists the selected box's ports with the shared `PortList`; add, rename, direction, connection type and remove are stored at once (the element-page calls), a shared box is read-only.
decisions.rationale: The connection form shows a Source or Target port choice only when that element has ports (the choice used to appear as an empty "No port" select).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 2: Neutral seeded element types
decisions.statement: A fresh organisation is seeded with System, Subsystem and Component only (domain "any"); the software and hardware types, their suggested connection types and their type symbols are no longer seeded (`DEFAULT_ELEMENT_TYPE_SUGGESTIONS` and `DEFAULT_TYPE_SYMBOLS` are removed, so there is no half-used mechanism).
decisions.rationale: The built-in symbol library and the connection type groups are unchanged. A migration seeds nothing: migration 0172 still backfills its own historical list for an organisation that existed before it, and an existing organisation keeps whatever it has. The demo seed script adds Board, Sensor and Service to its organisation; the test helper `add_domain_types` does the same for tests that need domain types. The Add menu heading for domain-neutral types is "New element".
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: Setup entry in the Add menu
decisions.statement: The last entry, a gear labelled "Set up element types", opens the project's Element Types settings (leaving a diagram with unsaved edits asks first).
decisions.rationale: It is shown only to someone who may manage the types. The frontend had no way to read a module role, so `GET .../modules/architecture/capabilities` returns `{ manage_types }` using the same `architecture_admin` check the type endpoints enforce (open to any project member, discloses only the caller's own ability, audit not needed: a read). The endpoints still enforce the role; the entry is a convenience.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 2: Connection type picker
decisions.statement: The single-choice `TreeSelect` no longer draws radio inputs: each node is a full-width selectable row with a tick on the chosen one, announced as a radio inside a radiogroup, under the tree's chevrons and indentation; the clear row ("All types") is the same.
decisions.rationale: This applies to every single-choice tree (the connection type fields and the type filters). Multi-select stays checkboxes.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 2: Phases 9f to 9i (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: Outline elements as a tree or a table
decisions.statement: The Outline tab's Elements section uses the shared `ViewToggle` (List and Tree, remembered per person) so elements read in the same table form as the lines (element, type, nearest placed parent); the tree gains Expand all and Collapse all beside its per-branch chevrons.
decisions.rationale: Elements, Notes and Lines are shared `CollapsibleSection`s (remembered per person, with a count pill).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9j (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 3: Components control
decisions.statement: Elements stay placeable in the project's component and category tree (D18: one shared table for every type, so a project can slice any records by the same tree); it is separate from an element's parent and child elements, and the two can read as the same thing.
decisions.rationale: The header control (`RecordPlacements`, shared by every record type) now has a `(?)` explaining that, and is limited to 22rem instead of the full header width. Revisit if elements should declare `not_placeable`; that needs the User's sign-off.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9j (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 3: Working inside an element
decisions.statement: Opening the inside already existed as a Selection card button that nobody found.
decisions.rationale: The shared canvas gains a generic `onNodeOpen` (double-click; Enter is left to selecting so the keyboard flow is unchanged, and the Selection card button, now with a tooltip, is the keyboard route). The editor opens the element's inside diagram from it. A diagram with a scope and no boxes says that new elements created there become children of the scope element.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9j (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 3: Boundary boxes
decisions.statement: A diagram of an element's inside can draw each *outer* connection of that element (a connection with exactly one end inside it, the element itself or a descendant; the other end outside) as its own box, so two links to one outside element are two boxes.
decisions.rationale: A box is keyed by the outer connection, not an element, so it has its own table, `architecture_diagram_boundaries` (diagram, connection, box; both keys `ON DELETE CASCADE`; unique per diagram and connection). Offered from Add to diagram, in a group "Outside this element".
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9k, links from the parent layer (2026-11-13)
