decisions.title: System Architecture review round 3: Outline shapes
decisions.statement: Input, output, two-way and a plain circle.
decisions.rationale: The canvas has a generic `outline` option on its nodes (`pointed-right`, `pointed-left`, `pointed-both`, `ellipse`; nothing architecture-specific), the server SVG draws the same flags and the Mermaid export uses a trapezoid each way, a hexagon and a circle. The rule: a point on the right is an input (the flow runs into the scope), on the left an output. The circle is used when the viewer cannot read the element outside, since showing a direction there would disclose more than the box's code. The artwork is not the schematic port symbols of any one tool: it is a simple flag, awaiting the User's confirmation.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9k, links from the parent layer (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: Where a line meets a box
decisions.statement: `diagram_resolver.resolve` takes the boxes (`Boundary`: its id, the outer connection's scope-side element, the element outside, and the realising connections) and swaps the end of each realising connection that meets a box for the box: its end that is the scope-side element (when that element is not itself placed), or that lies inside the element outside.
decisions.rationale: One candidate is made per box, so a connection realising two outer connections is drawn to both; a connection whose two ends would both meet a box is left alone. Boxes are placed elements with no parent. The browser port (`diagramResolver.ts`) and `outerSide` follow the same rule through `diagramResolverCases.json`, which gained five cases and `scope` and `outer_sides` keys; the key of a direct line now includes its two ends so one connection drawn to two boxes stays two lines.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9k, links from the parent layer (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 3: Covered, never "missing"
decisions.statement: A box is Covered when any live connection realises its outer connection, Not covered otherwise, a neutral marker in the box's caption, the Selection card, the Outline's Outer connections table and the report.
decisions.rationale: No warning colour or wording.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9k, links from the parent layer (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: Creating the connection from a box
decisions.statement: Drawing a line from an inner element to a box, or its "Connect to" list, opens the New connection form with the ends set from the box's direction (an output starts at the inner element) and, once created, marks it as realising the box's connection; the form lets the person change the ends, and a refusal of the realisation is shown after the connection exists.
decisions.rationale: A locked box offers nothing (its outside element cannot be connected to). A line's Selection card offers **Realises** for a line that stands for one connection: its outer connections with Remove, and the boxes on the diagram to add. The connection's own page lists *Realises* and *Realised by* but does not edit them in this phase (setting is from a diagram of the layer above).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9k, links from the parent layer (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: Coverage report and the one MCP tool
decisions.statement: `AR1 Boundary coverage` (`reports.py`, slug `boundary-coverage`): for each element that contains others, or the one named by `element` (code or name), the outer connections with direction, the element outside, Covered or Not covered and what realises it; a second table lists the ones nothing realises (flagged as a gap table only so a summary pack can re-list it).
decisions.rationale: An outer connection is found from the symmetric difference of the two ends' ancestor chains, so the cost is the connections times the tree depth. An end owned by another project or the organisation is "Shared element", with no code or name. The module now declares `mcp_tools` (the report's tool, `architecture_get_boundary_coverage_report`) and `mcp_guidance.md`; the generated module-tools reference is updated. The wider MCP surface remains Phase 14.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9k, links from the parent layer (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 3: Bundles and templates
decisions.statement: A connection's bundle entry lists the codes of the outer connections it realises (`realises`) and a diagram entry its boxes (`boundaries`: the connection's code and the box), so no new key exists and template classification is unchanged; a template reset keeps only what points at a connection that survived.
decisions.rationale: An import re-applies each realisation through the same rule and drops, with a warning, one that no longer holds, and drops a box whose connection does not cross the imported diagram's scope.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9k, links from the parent layer (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 3: Performance tooling
decisions.statement: The diagram probe now builds a scoped diagram with a boundary box and a realising connection, which needs a PUT: `ScalingProbeApi` gained a generic `put` (the guard, the creation-permission test and the dataset test implement it); a probe's last `post` must still be the request under test, so the PUT calls come first.
decisions.rationale: The dataset generator scopes the first diagram and a few others (`_SCOPED_DIAGRAMS`) to an element with outer connections and writes boxes and realisations for them, bounded so the connection scan is flat at any size.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 3: Phase 9k, links from the parent layer (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Tags beside the version
decisions.statement: `RecordHeader` gains `tagsInline`: `tags` is drawn on the badge line after the version, never on a line of its own, and `RecordTags inline` draws the compact form: read-only chips for the tags and components, nothing for a record with neither, and one small "Tags and components" button for someone who may change them.
decisions.rationale: The empty "Not placed in a component" line no longer exists in the header. The option is generic; the three architecture record pages use it and other modules keep their layout until the User asks.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9l, header and editor height (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: A dialog, not a popover
decisions.statement: The button opens the existing full editor (`RecordTags`, unchanged) in a `Modal`, because the tag picker and the component picker each open a popover of their own and popovers do not nest.
decisions.rationale: Changes still save at once; the chips on the line re-read after each one.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9l, header and editor height (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Editor height
decisions.statement: The Drawing tab's canvas takes the window height left below it (`useFillViewportHeight`: page offset, a 16 px bottom gap, live on resize and when the content above changes), never under 300 px.
decisions.rationale: At 1280 x 720 the header, tabs and toolbar leave about 324 px; the Change state menu (the next phase) removes the transitions line and gives that height back. Wheel zoom is unchanged.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9l, header and editor height (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: One tree in the core
decisions.statement: `components/placementTree.ts` turns the project's components and categories into `TreeSelect` nodes (a component with its categories beneath it), and `PlacementPicker` (create form and record header) and `ComponentFilterField` (every list filter) now draw it with `TreeSelect`, replacing the flat `MultiSelectDropdown` lists.
decisions.rationale: A component alone and the same component narrowed to a category stay different places, so each is its own node and ticking one never ticks the other. `TreeSelectNode` gained `pathLabel` (`Hardware / Power`) so the trigger summary and the checkbox's accessible name keep the full path. Every record type benefits; nothing per module.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9m, components as a tree (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Add menu
decisions.statement: `AddElementsDialog` has the same Component and category tree as a filter; an element matches when it sits in any ticked place.
decisions.rationale: Placements are read in pages of 500 ids. Grouping the list by the element folder tree waits for folders (Phase 9q).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9m, components as a tree (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Selection card
decisions.statement: A box's project components are edited with the shared `RecordPlacements` (new `captioned` option: a visible "Components" caption with its help, as the card's other controls have), saved at once like ports.
decisions.rationale: The empty "Not placed in a component" text is removed from the shared component (`strings.placements.none` deleted); an empty record shows only the control.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9m, components as a tree (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: A shared box shows no components
decisions.statement: The plan said a shared box "lists it without controls".
decisions.rationale: The placements read answers 404 for a record owned by another project or the organisation (a component belongs to one project's tree, and that tree is not disclosed to another), so there is nothing to list. The card does not request it, rather than make a call that always fails.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9m, components as a tree (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: One transition map on the server
decisions.statement: `transitions.STATUS_MOVES`: `draft -> proposed | active | rejected`, `proposed -> active | draft | rejected`, `active -> retired`, `retired -> active`, `rejected -> draft`.
decisions.rationale: Every status change of an element, a connection and a diagram goes through `move_refusal` (409 for the same state or a move outside the map), and `ElementOut`, `ConnectionOut` and `DiagramOut` return `allowed_status_moves`, so the menu draws exactly what the server accepts. A later state is a map entry and a label. A configurable per-project state set is not built (no stated need).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9n, Change state menu (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Behaviour change recorded
decisions.statement: The earlier rule allowed any move, so a Draft could be retired at once.
decisions.rationale: It no longer can: a Draft is made Active (or Planned) first, or archived. Existing tests that retired a draft now create the record active.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9n, Change state menu (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: A Proposed child still blocks retiring its parent
decisions.statement: The existing rule is "children neither retired nor archived"; `proposed` is neither, so the rule needs no change and a proposed part is not orphaned from its parent's view.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9n, Change state menu (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Rejected, and the rename
decisions.statement: The first build called the second state `planned`; the User renamed it **Proposed** (put forward, not yet agreed) and added **Rejected** (considered and not adopted).
decisions.rationale: A Draft or a Proposed record may be rejected, and a Rejected record may be reopened as a Draft ( for the Proposed-to-Rejected and Rejected-to-Draft moves: a proposal is the likelier thing to be rejected, and a dead end with no way back would force a copy). Rejected is **out of use like Retired** (): `labels.INACTIVE_STATUSES` and the frontend `isOutOfUse` carry both, so "Open only" hides it, a shared rejected element cannot be newly connected to or placed, a record drawn from it is faded, the list inactive style applies, and a rejected child no longer blocks retiring or rejecting its parent. A new record cannot be created or imported as Retired or Rejected. The status was never committed as `planned`, so no data migration is written.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9n, Change state menu (2026-11-13)

decisions.title: One form, one save path
decisions.statement: A line's Selection card lists the connections behind it, each with an **Edit** button (named for its code) that opens the shared `ConnectionFormModal` the detail page uses, so a field added later reaches both.
decisions.rationale: Save quotes the connection's version (`PUT .../connections/{id}`, the same manage gate and audit event as the detail page), then re-reads the element and connection lists and the diagram with `editor.reload(false)`, which merges and keeps the pending layout. A refusal (a stale version, an end the person may not read) is shown in the dialog and the form stays open.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9o, edit a connection from the diagram (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Per connection, not per line
decisions.statement: A rolled-up or merged line stands for several connections, so the button sits on each row of the Selection card's table rather than on the line; this edits any of them and needs no new "pick one" step.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9o, edit a connection from the diagram (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: A shared connection is read-only
decisions.statement: A connection belongs to the project that created it, so a row whose `project_id` is not the diagram's project has no Edit button.
decisions.rationale: This only hides a control the server would refuse anyway (the owner's `architect` is the only editor).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9o, edit a connection from the diagram (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Client-side sort, not server sort/order
decisions.statement: The plan assumed the Elements, Connections and Diagrams lists page by `limit`/`offset`.
decisions.rationale: They do not: each loads its whole filtered set in one request (and the project-scope merge across nested projects is already in that response) and applies search, status, type and "Open only" in the browser. The style guide's own rule is that a list that loads everything sorts the loaded array and only a paged list sorts on the server, so the three lists sort with `utils/sortRows` and keep the sort in the URL (`useUrlSort`, `?sort=name&order=desc`). A server `sort` parameter would add an allow-list and a second implementation of an order the browser must reproduce anyway for the filtered rows. If a list is ever paged, it moves to the server then.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9p, sortable lists and the guard (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Export order is unchanged
decisions.statement: The plan had the record-table export honour the sort.
decisions.rationale: The shared export has never taken a sort for any type (a list's filters travel to it, its order does not), and the exported CSV is the import file, keyed by `code`, so row order carries no meaning. Adding a sort to one module's export would be a per-type exception to the shared mechanism; a person who wants a sorted file sorts it in the spreadsheet.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9p, sortable lists and the guard (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Code order uses digit values
decisions.statement: `sortRows` now compares with `numeric: true`, so `ELM-9` precedes `ELM-10` for every table that uses it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9p, sortable lists and the guard (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: The guard
decisions.statement: `scripts/check_sortable_columns.py` (pinned by `backend/tests/test_sortable_columns.py`, like the other style-guide checks; the repository has no separate CI step for them) fails a file that renders a `DirectoryTable` and contains no `sortable` column unless it is in `scripts/sortable_columns_baseline.json`.
decisions.rationale: The baseline holds the 26 files that remain (the plan counted 29 before these three lists were done); it only shrinks, and 9r empties it. It checks per file, so a second unsortable table in a file that has a sortable one is not seen. The rule was already written into `CLAUDE.md` and the style guide on 2026-11-13; this change adds the guard to both.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9p, sortable lists and the guard (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Home: Module 18
decisions.statement: A state machine diagram describes an element's behaviour, so it hangs off an element and reuses the shared canvas, codes, links, search, bundles and exports.
decisions.rationale: Module 6 is the Design record (rationale, revisions, approval) and has no canvas; Module 15 (Automations) creates records from a diagram and Module 16 (Workflow Capture) documents how people work, so neither fits. The User confirmed the shared canvas serving other modules does not change this: it makes the canvas a consumer concern, not an ownership one. Numbered Phase 17, built after 9u and before Phase 10.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17: state machine diagrams planned (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Wording clash found
decisions.statement: Phase 9n's "Change state" menu changes a record's status; a state machine's items are states.
decisions.rationale: Phase 17 renames the menu to "Change status" so one word means one thing.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17: state machine diagrams planned (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Notation: UML state machine, not Module 16's BPMN
decisions.statement: BPMN is a process notation; its events and gateways mean something different from a state's pseudostates, so reusing its shapes would mislead.
decisions.rationale: UML (the same as SysML state machines) maps onto Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2`. Each module draws its own notation on the notation-agnostic shared canvas; an earlier note that a BPMN event and a UML initial state were the same marker was wrong and is corrected in the plan.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17: state machine diagrams planned (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Name: state machine diagram
decisions.statement: The formal UML 2 and SysML name for the drawing, consistent with "Block diagram" in the Type choice and with the rule to prefer the established term of the field.
decisions.rationale: The code prefix is `SMD-001`, the artefact type `architecture_state_machine_diagram`; states stay `STE-001`. Renamed before any code, so no migration. Mermaid's `stateDiagram-v2` is the export syntax only.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17: state machine diagrams planned (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: What a folder is
decisions.statement: `architecture_folders` (owner project XOR organisation, `kind`, `name`, `parent_id`, `sort_order`) and a nullable `folder_id` on elements, connections and diagrams.
decisions.rationale: One tree per kind, any depth to a cap of 12, no cycle, a name unique among its siblings (ignoring case) and never containing `/` (the path separator). A CHECK keeps an organisation to element folders. A folder has no code, is not linkable or searchable and means nothing to the resolver, the roll-up or a report, so it is not a registered artefact type; a record reaches its folder only through its own `folder_id`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Deleting a folder moves its content up
decisions.statement: Records and sub-folders move to the parent, bumping each record's version; nothing is deleted with a folder.
decisions.rationale: A sub-folder whose name the parent already uses stops the delete with a message to rename one first
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Records name a folder by id on the API and by path elsewhere
decisions.statement: The three record types return `folder_id` and `folder_path` (names from the top joined by `/`), take `folder_id` on create and update (`null` clears it; a field left out keeps it), and the record tables, the CSV and the bundles use the path.
decisions.rationale: Routes are per kind (`/element-folders`, `/connection-folders`, `/diagram-folders`, with `/move-records`), so the kind's sub-component and manage permission gate each; the organisation's `/element-folders` need `architecture_org_admin`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: The folder filter is applied in the browser, with the filter sent to the export
decisions.statement: The three lists load their whole set (see Phase 9p), so the page filters by `folder_path`; the list's export receives `folder` and `subfolders` and applies the same rule on the server (`folders.filter_ids`), so the file holds what the page shows. "Include sub-folders" is on by default.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Bulk move is a selection on DirectoryTable, not a per-page checkbox column
decisions.statement: `DirectoryTable` gained a generic `selection` prop (a leading column of tick boxes with a select-all header box that skips unselectable rows); the three lists show "Move to folder" above the table while rows are chosen.
decisions.rationale: `RequirementsPage` keeps its own hand-written selection column; migrating it onto the shared one is a follow-up, not done here.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Where the tree sits
decisions.statement: The tree is a control in each list's filter panel (`FolderPanel`), which is where the page's other filters live and keeps the list column unchanged.
decisions.rationale: The three lists share one hook (`useFolderListControls`) and the organisation's elements panel uses the same panel and hook with its state kept off the page address (the administration tabs own it).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Other owners' folders
decisions.statement: An element another owner shares returns its `folder_path` (only the names on the way to that element, which the viewer may read) and a null `folder_id`; the Add menu groups candidates by owner (this project, the organisation, another project) and then by those paths, so a folder the viewer cannot reach through a readable element is never shown.
decisions.rationale: The "another project" group is labelled by project code only when the element carries one: the element answer has no project name, and adding one to a shared element would disclose more than the plan allows.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: A project's own element cannot use another owner's folder
decisions.statement: `folders.usable_folder` checks owner and kind; a foreign folder looks the same as a missing one (400 on a record, 404 on a folder call).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Bundles and templates
decisions.statement: The project bundle has `architecture_folders` (`{kind, path, sort_order}`, parents first), template **configuration**; the organisation bundle `architecture_org_folders`.
decisions.rationale: A record carries `folder` (a path). An import reuses a folder that already has the path, creates the rest (also for a record whose path the folder list lacks), and never drops a record for its folder; a path that cannot be created (too deep, blank name) is reported and the record is left at the top level.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Nested projects
decisions.statement: Folders are per-project content, not a vocabulary a child falls back to: no ancestor fallback.
decisions.rationale: Users and groups parity, time, Save and activate, human codes, search and MCP do not apply (no person field, no date, no lifecycle, no code, no searchable text, no tool); folder changes are audited as `architecture_folder` events (kind, field names, counts; no names) and appear in History under "structure".
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9q, folders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Every list sorts in the browser
decisions.statement: None of the 26 files pages (no `total`/`onLoadMore`; each loads its whole set and filters in the browser), so none needed a server `sort`/`order`; the plan's "server-side where its endpoint pages" matched no list.
decisions.rationale: A list page keeps the sort in the URL (`useUrlSort`: the Strategies, Guiding Principles, Future States and Open Questions pages, Decisions, Risks, the Organisations list, and the stakeholder lists when they are a page); a panel embedded in another page keeps it local (`hooks/useTableSort.ts`: `useTableSort`, or `useSortState` where the rows exist only after an early return), so it leaves the host page's parameters alone, the same rule the filters follow.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9r, the sortable-lists sweep (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Shared sort values
decisions.statement: The Strategies, Guiding Principles, Future States and Open Questions lists share one set of sort values per type (`modules/context_strategy/contextStrategySort.ts`) between the project page and the organisation panel.
decisions.rationale: A priority sorts by rank (low, medium, high), not alphabetically; a risk rating by its normalised score; a version by number. `RecordListView` (five stakeholder lists) sorts its fixed columns itself and takes a `sortValue` per caller column (`RecordColumn`), so a kind's own column opts in with `sortable` and a value.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9r, the sortable-lists sweep (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 4: Request lists
decisions.statement: `requestListState.sortRequests` already ordered by demand, score, dates and Pain Points; Code, Title, Status and Owner now sort too, with the existing rule that a request with no value sorts last in both directions.
decisions.rationale: The two request files were reported by the check only because their columns are built in `requestColumns.tsx`, so the check now also accepts a table that passes `onSort` (the columns are marked where they are built).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9r, the sortable-lists sweep (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: One list with no natural order
decisions.statement: `OrgUsageTable` is a fixed key-value table of six usage figures read in a set order, so a sort would only scramble it.
decisions.rationale: It is named with this reason in `NO_NATURAL_ORDER` in `scripts/check_sortable_columns.py`, which is the exemption mechanism the rule's "a stated reason in `docs/decisions.md`" needed. The baseline file stays, empty, so a new file cannot join it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 4: Phase 9r, the sortable-lists sweep (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: A column on the element, one note for every diagram
decisions.statement: The note shows on every diagram that places the element, as its name does.
decisions.rationale: A per-diagram override is not built (no stated need). Create and edit share the one `ElementFields` group (the form, the diagram's element modal and the organisation panel), with `help` on both the description and the note saying which is which.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9s, the display note (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 5: Drawn four ways
decisions.statement: The canvas draws it as a generic node `body` (`GraphCanvasNode.body`: plain text, line breaks kept, clipped with an ellipsis to the lines the box has room for, re-measured on a resize; a box with no room for a line shows none, so the note is never half-drawn).
decisions.rationale:
The server SVG wraps each paragraph and clips to the lines that fit, ending in an ellipsis (`diagram_svg._note_lines`); the PNG is drawn from that SVG; Mermaid writes each non-empty line as another `
` line of the node label, escaped like the name. A boundary box and a locked (unreadable) box carry no note.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9s, the display note (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Show notes is the viewer's switch
decisions.statement: In the diagram settings gear beside the stored Connection detail switch, kept in the page address (`notes=0`), never stored, never disabled (it changes only the viewer's screen) and not applied to exports, which use the default (shown).
decisions.rationale: The gear's marked state and spoken label say when notes are hidden.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9s, the display note (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Where the description is read
decisions.statement: The element page, the Selection card (read-only, collapsed to a few lines with "Show more" through the shared `ActivityNote`), the Outline's table view (new Display note and Description columns), the record table export and import (new `display_note` column; a note over the cap is a row error through the create and update bodies), search (opt-in field `display_note`, "Display note"), the report…
decisions.rationale: field list and both bundles.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9s, the display note (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 5: Four kinds, one table
decisions.statement: `leader_kind` is `none`, `element`, `connection` or `point`.
decisions.rationale: A check constraint allows a target column only for its own kind and requires both coordinates for a point. The foreign keys are `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so deleting the target leaves the note and its kind with an empty column; the view and the export read that as `none` (`diagrams.effective_leader_kind`) and a save that changes the note rewrites it as `none`, so nothing dangles and no trigger is needed. The target is a column, not a link row, because it is one fact of the note and is not a record a requirement, report or search names.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9t, annotation notes with leaders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Tones are a closed set in code
decisions.statement: `NoteTone`: neutral, info, success, warning, danger.
decisions.rationale: They are drawn from the theme's tokens on the canvas (`--color-info`, `--color-accent`, `--color-warning`, `--color-danger`) and from fixed light-theme colours in the server SVG, the same split as element colours. This is a rendering choice of the module, not a core enum a module extends, so the module boundary is not touched. The neutral tone replaces the earlier yellow of the server SVG note; the canvas draws a note dashed as before.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9t, annotation notes with leaders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: What a leader may name
decisions.statement: A new target element must be placed on the diagram in the same save, and a new target connection must belong to the diagram's project (one query for the lot), so a layout save cannot name another owner's record or one the viewer cannot read; a target a note already had is kept unchanged, so taking a box off the diagram or retiring an element hides the leader rather than failing the next save.
decisions.rationale: Both cases are tested, with a connection of another project and an unknown id. The leader never discloses a record's content: the view returns ids the caller could already read.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9t, annotation notes with leaders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 5: Hidden is not deleted
decisions.statement: A leader whose target is switched off, rolled up or removed from the diagram is not drawn, the Selection card says so, and the Outline lists the note with "Points at ELM-003 Firewall (not drawn)"; the leader returns with its target.
decisions.rationale: In the browser the canvas skips a leader whose node or line is not on it; on the server the SVG and Mermaid do the same, and a bridged or merged line carries a connection leader (the drawn line that stands for it).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9t, annotation notes with leaders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: One rule for the leader's ends
decisions.statement: A leader to a box joins the nearest pair of attach points of the note and the box; to a line's middle or a free point it starts at the note's nearest attach point.
decisions.rationale: These are the existing `nearestPair`/`nearestPoint` rules of the attach-point feature, so no second rule exists and the shared cases (`graphAttachPointCases.json`) still cover them; the server SVG test pins the resulting coordinates for the three kinds. A line's middle is that of the line as drawn: the browser draws parallel lines on top of each other and the SVG offsets them, so a leader to one of several parallel lines can differ by the offset between the two drawings.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9t, annotation notes with leaders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 5: Generic canvas, module storage
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvas` gains `tone` on a node, `leaders` (`GraphCanvasLeader`: a node, a line or a free point), `onLeaderTargetChange` and `onCanvasClick`.
decisions.rationale: A leader is a React Flow edge that is not selectable or focusable, with a small invisible end node for a line's middle and a visible, draggable one for a free point; dragging a leader's end onto a box names the box, and onto empty canvas names that position. Modules 16 and 17 can use it with their own ids; the canvas stores nothing.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9t, annotation notes with leaders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 5: The keyboard route
decisions.statement: The Selection card lists what a leader may point at (the drawn boxes and the connections of the drawn lines), offers **Point at a spot** (the next click on the canvas places the end; Cancel stops it) and an **Arrowhead** switch.
decisions.rationale: The click that places the end must not clear the note's selection, so the page ignores a deselection while it waits.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 5: Phase 9t, annotation notes with leaders (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture Phase 9u, part 2: Shared and organisation elements
decisions.statement: A comment on an element another owner shares is stored against the element's owner and is read by anyone who can read that element (the record-visibility rule), including the owner's team; a recipient project's comments are therefore visible to the owner.
decisions.rationale: Revoking the grant hides the thread again. This follows the user-stated rule that a recipient may read, link and place the element but not edit it; commenting is a read-level action here (recorded as the reading of "existing comment right", ).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 9u, part 2: comments, bundles, canvas layer and screens

decisions.title: Absolute coordinates at any nesting
decisions.statement: React Flow positions a child relative to its parent; the canvas converts, so the consumer (and the stored layout of a state) keeps one absolute coordinate system, which also lets the server draw without walking parents.
decisions.rationale: Moving a container reports it and every node inside it through `onNodesMove`; moving a child reports only the child; a resize from the top or left leaves the children in place and reports none of them. A child cannot be dragged out of its container (`extent: parent`); an unknown parent, a node's own id and a loop of parents are ignored.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17b: generic canvas additions for state machine diagrams (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture: What is stored when
decisions.statement: A state's or transition's content is stored at once by its form (the findings and a state's code come from the server); only the drawing (a state's position, size and nesting, a transition's attach points) is local until Save, with undo and redo, as in the block diagram editor.
decisions.rationale: A new state is created by its form, and Cancel creates nothing.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17c: state machine diagram editor and the merged Diagrams tab (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Nesting is a Selection card control, not a drop
decisions.statement: "Inside" in the Selection card puts a state in an ordinary state (never a marker, itself or one of its descendants), moves it into the frame below the name strip, grows every frame above it and carries its own children; it is the keyboard route too.
decisions.rationale: A state dropped from the palette on a frame that already holds states is created inside it. A plain state is not turned into a frame by a drop, so a stray drop never nests.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17c: state machine diagram editor and the merged Diagrams tab (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Keyboard routes for drawing a line
decisions.statement: The Selection card's "Add transition to" lists every state including the state itself (a loop), and "Line starts at" / "Line ends at" set the attach points (a marker offers its four sides only), so nothing needs a pointer.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17c: state machine diagram editor and the merged Diagrams tab (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Save and activate is not offered for a new state machine diagram
decisions.statement: A diagram with no states always fails the checks, so the button could only fail; the diagram is activated from Change state once it is sound, and a refusal shows the server's list of errors beside the menu (it is not mistaken for a stale save: only the stale-version message sets the conflict).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17c: state machine diagram editor and the merged Diagrams tab (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: PNG is drawn in the browser from the server's SVG
decisions.statement: The plan said "PNG and SVG from the server renderer"; the module has one PNG path (`svgToPngBlob`), so a second server-side rasteriser is not added.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17d: state machine diagram export, wording and docs (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Shared Export
decisions.statement: `useDiagramExport` and `DiagramExportMenu` are used by both editors; the block editor's own copy was removed, so the two cannot drift.
decisions.rationale: A pending drawing is saved first.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 17d: state machine diagram export, wording and docs (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: A suggestion is computed, never stored
decisions.statement: An element the project owns, placed in a component through the shared placement table, is suggested for each requirement of that component that is not archived and has no link to the element.
decisions.rationale: A retired or archived element is not suggested. A category under the component does not change the match: the requirement's component is what counts. An element another owner shares is not suggested (a component belongs to one project); it is allocated from the Links panel.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 10: allocation (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Any existing link between the pair ends the suggestion
decisions.statement: Whatever its type, so accepting never creates a second link and an allocation made by hand is not suggested again.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 10: allocation (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Accepting uses the generic link path
decisions.statement: `allocation.accept` calls `link_authoring.create_link_for_artefact` with the "Allocated to" type the project can use (400 when it is hidden or shadowed).
decisions.rationale: Each pair is its own savepoint, so a refused pair (an approved requirement in a project that needs a change request for links) is reported with its reason and the others still apply; one endpoint serves Accept and Accept all.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 10: allocation (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: A dismissal applies while the element has stayed in the component
decisions.statement: The plan says a dismissal is cleared when the element is no longer placed in the requirement's component.
decisions.rationale: Placements change through several core paths (the placement API, a category reassignment, a bundle import), and a hook in each would be a core edit for one module's table. The row instead carries its own time and `dismissal_applies` compares it with the earliest placement of the element in that component: a placement made later than the dismissal (the element left and returned) voids it, and an added category under the same component does not. The stale row is deleted the next time a person dismisses, restores or accepts that pair. Trade-off: a requirement moved to another component and back keeps a dismissal made earlier, because the element never left the component it now shares; accepted as rare.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 10: allocation (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Authority is the authority to change the requirement's links
decisions.statement: `require_link_authority` for requirements, the same check the accepted link needs, for Accept, Dismiss and Restore.
decisions.rationale: Reading needs project membership and the Elements sub-component. The plan names the Architect for acceptance; an Architect holds link authority through the role's permissions where the project grants it, and a requirements analyst with the Link permission can allocate too, which is the flexible reading. The view returns `can_manage` so a screen offers buttons only to someone they will work for.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 10: allocation (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: What the file leaves out
decisions.statement: Comments and pins, `*_email` keys (creators, archivers), an element's **owner**, requirement links, collections and grants, allocation dismissals and uploaded symbol files.
decisions.rationale: The plan says "round-trips losslessly"; this trades that for not putting personal data in a file any member who can see the elements can download, because the record exports apply the organisation's personal-data policy and explicit export permission to an owner column and a file would bypass it. If the User wants owners (and authorship) in the file, it needs the same policy check; recorded here as a known gap against the plan, not a silent narrowing.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 11: interchange and reports (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture, interchange and reports: Structurizr DSL
decisions.statement: Levels follow the element tree (system, container, component; deeper elements are components of their second-level ancestor with a `level` property); one relationship per connection with the protocol as technology and code, type and direction as properties; a connection to an element inside the source's own tree is counted, not written (Structurizr forbids it); one view per active diagram from…
decisions.rationale: `build_view` with the saved or named toggle states (system landscape, container or component view by the elements shown, a mixed diagram rolled up to its systems with a comment); only owned, live elements are named; every string is one cleaned, quoted line, so a name cannot start a statement.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 11: interchange and reports (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture, baselines, core: Manual baseline
decisions.statement: `POST`/`GET /projects/{id}/baselines`: any member lists; taking one needs project management for `requirement` and the provider's permission atom for a module type, each checked separately, with no server-administrator bypass (customer content).
decisions.rationale: Requirements are captured at their current version with no approval, lock or status change. The list returns counts per type only: a module's snapshot content is read through that module's own routes (Phase 13), since its visibility is the module's rule, and returning it here would be a second read path around the resolver.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 12: baselines, core (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture, baselines, architecture: What is captured
decisions.statement: Four types, one item per record: element, connection, diagram and state machine diagram (a state is inside its diagram, not an item of its own).
decisions.rationale: `ModuleDefinition.baseline_snapshots` carries four providers (`baseline_snapshot.py`), each gated by the manage atom of its type for a manual baseline. A stage baseline is written for whoever moved the stage; a component's own stage baseline captures nothing (`component_id` set), so the project-wide baseline is the only one that holds the architecture. (the whole-project reading follows the Phase 12 hook contract: a type whose records belong to no component returns nothing then).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 13: baselines, architecture (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture, baselines, architecture: One reader
decisions.statement: A record's snapshot is its project bundle entry (`export.export_project_data`) split by type, so ports, tags, places, boxes, notes, anchors, toggles, states and transitions carry the same portable keys as an export and cannot drift from it.
decisions.rationale: The four providers share one read per baseline, kept on the session (`db.info`) for the triggering context object. Archived records are not captured.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 13: baselines, architecture (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Classification (Phase 12's rule applied)
decisions.statement: Entries pass through `interchange.scrub` (now public): comments and pins, `*_email` keys and an element's owner object are removed, and `created_at`, `is_archived` and `archived_at` are dropped.
decisions.rationale: The owner is lost to the snapshot as it is to the interchange file (a person or group on a record that outlives it is personal data under the data classification policy); a change of owner is therefore not shown by a comparison. ; the trade-off against a complete record is for the User to revisit with the interchange file's (Phase 11).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 13: baselines, architecture (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: The rule already existed; nothing measured it
decisions.statement: The button sizes pattern says neighbours match, but `iconSizeViolations` and `orphanedControlViolations` check icon sizes and wrapping, not height.
decisions.rationale: `buttonHeightViolations` (`frontend/src/testing/buttonHeights.ts`) now reads the rendered height of the buttons in each horizontal flex row (a `.btn`, or a wrapper holding exactly one) and fails a line whose buttons differ by more than a pixel; `data-button-size-ok` opts out. It runs in the stories of both editors (toolbar and Selection card, wide and narrow, a node and a line selected) and in both Playwright specs. Run against the old toolbar it reports the 28px and 36px mix, so it is not vacuous.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 9v, toolbar sizes and a measured check (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 6: The toolbar is small
decisions.statement: Medium was tried first, since the pattern's "size follows the level" reads a whole-diagram toolbar as page level; at the editor's column width it wrapped the settings gear onto a second line and pushed the canvas past the window (the Playwright fits-the-screen step failed by 1.5px).
decisions.rationale: The toolbar sits in the page body on a dense working surface and most of it was already small, so the two menu triggers became small instead: `MenuButton` takes `size` (`md` default, so its other callers are unchanged) and the Add and Export menus pass `sm`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 9v, toolbar sizes and a measured check (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 6: The rule
decisions.statement: Help for a button, toggle or menu trigger is a tooltip on the control; a `(?)` is only the help of a caption (a form field, filter or settings row).
decisions.rationale: Written as the style guide's "Pattern: help on interactive elements", cross-linked from "Pattern: explain in help, not in the layout" and "Pattern: button sizes", and as one bullet in `CLAUDE.md`. The earlier "Instructions for a surface" bullet of "Pattern: field help" said to place a `FieldHelp` "beside the control it explains"; it now says the surface's caption.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 9w, help on the control itself (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 6: Limit of the check
decisions.statement: It reads indentation, so it sees a `FieldHelp` as a sibling of a button in the same parent, with or without a `{cond && ...}` guard; it cannot see a button reached through a helper component.
decisions.rationale: A new violation of that shape is caught in review, not by the script.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 9w, help on the control itself (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 6: One mechanism, on ItemRow
decisions.statement: `ItemRow` takes `revealActions`: the actions are hidden with `opacity` (so they keep their space and the row never changes size), shown on row hover and on `:focus-within`, and always shown under `@media (hover: none)`.
decisions.rationale: This adopts the request's hover reveal only with the keyboard and touch routes the plan required, so it hides no action from anyone who cannot hover. Written as the style guide's "Pattern: actions revealed on hover".
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 9x, comment threads as icon buttons (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 6: One shared set
decisions.statement: `SelectionActions` draws the row and `selectionAction` fixes each common action's icon, so the block diagram's and the state machine's cards use the same row and a new action reaches both.
decisions.rationale: `IconAction` (moved out of `CommentThreadView`, which now uses it) is the one small icon button with its name as `aria-label` and tooltip; it also renders a link for a destination and takes an optional `help` for a name that does not explain itself ("Open inside as diagram" keeps its explanation as the tooltip's second line, so nothing the text button's tooltip said is lost).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 9y, Selection cards as icon buttons (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 6: Accessible names are unchanged
decisions.statement: Every action keeps the name it had (`Edit element`, `Remove from diagram`, `Delete element…`, `Edit state`, `Comment on this box`), so the Playwright specs and stories that address controls by name still work and a screen reader user hears the same words.
decisions.rationale: The per-row Edit in a line's connection table (`Edit CON-001`), the "Stop realising" button and "Remove note" are the same `IconAction`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 9y, Selection cards as icon buttons (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: No action is rare enough for the overflow menu today
decisions.statement: The request says a rare or hard-to-picture action goes into one overflow menu.
decisions.rationale: Every action in the two cards is frequent and has an unambiguous icon (the one that is not obvious, Open inside, keeps its explanation in its tooltip), so all are icons. `SelectionAction.menu` and the "More actions" menu are built and covered by a story so the next rare action is one flag, not a new pattern. "Point at a spot" stays a text toggle: it is a mode with two states in the note's own field group, not a card action. Add port stays the port list's own control (`DefinitionList`), which follows its own pattern.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 9y, Selection cards as icon buttons (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 6: Add is immediate
decisions.statement: The Add to diagram menu and a drop create the state through the unchanged add endpoint, with a default name from `defaultStateName` (lowest unused "State n", compared without regard to case because the server refuses a repeated name; a marker takes its kind's label, with " 2", " 3" when taken).
decisions.rationale: The new state is selected and its name takes the focus. A refused add toasts and adds nothing; a second add is held while one is being stored, so two adds never quote one version.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 17e, state machine diagrams add directly (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Values are set in the Selection card
decisions.statement: `StateFieldGroup` is the one field group (name, kind, and for an ordinary state description, entry, exit, activity), used by the card (`StateSelectionFields`) and by `StateFormModal`, now edit-only and opened by double-clicking a state.
decisions.rationale: The card stores a state's content when the focus leaves its fields or **Save state** is pressed (moving between its fields stores nothing, so one edit is one write), with the version lock; a blank name is not stored. The old **Edit state** icon is removed because the fields are in the card; every other action is unchanged.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 17e, state machine diagrams add directly (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 6: Quick links and tags on create
decisions.statement: A state has no create form now, so it has no `QuickLinkField` or `TagField` there; tags (`RecordTags`) and links (a compact `ArtefactLinksPanel`) are in the Selection card from the moment the state exists, which is the same trip the quick-link rule exists for.
decisions.rationale: The create-and-edit field-group rule holds: one group serves both.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 6: Phase 17e, state machine diagrams add directly (2026-11-14)

decisions.title: Fix, in the shared layer so both editors are covered
decisions.statement: `useCanvasComments` now reads `pin` itself (the editors' copies of that code are removed): the linked thread is derived as open from the moment the comments load, nothing else opens a thread, and every close (Escape, a click outside, the marker, the close button, choosing another thread) removes `pin` from the address with a replace.
decisions.rationale: A link naming a thread that no longer exists is dropped. `GraphCanvas` gained a generic `onBackgroundClick` (a click on empty canvas outside comment mode, read-only too), which the layer uses to close the thread. The first `centerOn` fits the drawing explicitly and then moves, so the view is always fitted first and then moved; later moves keep the person's zoom. Pins are not counted in the fit (they sit outside the canvas nodes), which the Playwright step checks by comparing a diagram with a thread against one without.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18a, comment threads closed on load (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Add is immediate
decisions.statement: Both routes call one `addTransition` that posts the transition with empty event, guard, action and description, selects it and moves the focus to the Selection card: the event, or the guard when the source is a choice (, from the plan: lines leaving a choice are told apart by their conditions).
decisions.rationale: A refused add is a toast and nothing is added. The add endpoint already accepted empty values; `test_a_transition_is_created_with_no_event_condition_or_action_and_they_are_set_later` pins it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18b, transitions added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: One field group
decisions.statement: `TransitionFieldGroup` (ends, event, guard, action, description) is used by the card (`TransitionSelectionFields`) and by `TransitionFormModal`, now edit-only and opened by double-clicking a line.
decisions.rationale: The card's **Edit transition** icon is gone for the reason the state's was (its fields are in the card). The line has no record code, so it has no `QuickLinkField` or `TagField`, as before.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18b, transitions added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Shared draft hook
decisions.statement: The draft, changed-field diff and one-at-a-time commit that `StateSelectionFields` owned moved to `useSelectionDraft`, used by both cards, rather than copying it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18b, transitions added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Generic canvas extension (Phase 18b)
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvas` gained `onEdgeOpen` (double-click on a line, the same contract as `onNodeOpen`; a leader line is never opened), so Modules 16 and 17 can use it.
decisions.rationale: The keyboard route to the same fields is the Selection card.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18b, transitions added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Elements are added at once
decisions.statement: Dropping a palette type or choosing it in the Add menu posts the element through the unchanged create endpoint with a default name (`defaultElementName`: the type's name and the first number not in use among the project's elements, "Sensor 1"), inside the diagram's scope element, places it, selects it and puts the cursor in the Selection card's name (`ElementSelectionFields`).
decisions.rationale: A refused create is a toast and nothing is added. `NewElementDialog` is deleted; `ElementFormModal` stays for the Elements list, the Links panel and the organisation's elements.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18c, block diagram elements and connections added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Connections are added at once
decisions.statement: Drawing a line, the card's "Connect to" list and a boundary box's "Connect to" call one `addConnection`, which creates the connection with `defaultConnectionType` (the first type the ends' element types suggest, else the first top-level type that fits both ends by domain, else the first that fits, else the first type; the same rule the dialog used, now one function) and every other field empty…
decisions.rationale: selects its line when it is drawn and puts the cursor in the card's name. A boundary box's connection is still marked as realising the outer connection straight after. The Selection card edits a line that stands for **one** connection of this project in place (`ConnectionSelectionFields`); a rolled-up or merged line lists its connections, each with an Edit button that opens the dialog, because several records cannot share one set of fields.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18c, block diagram elements and connections added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: The one dialog left on creation
decisions.statement: A project with no connection type cannot create a connection, so `ConnectionFormModal` opens with a "Set up connection types" link (new `setupPath` prop).
decisions.rationale: It cannot be saved until a type exists.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18c, block diagram elements and connections added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: One field group per record
decisions.statement: `ConnectionFieldGroup` is extracted from `ConnectionFormModal` and is now the one set of connection fields for the create dialog, the edit dialog and the card; `ElementFields` already was for elements and gained `autoFocusName`.
decisions.rationale: The card's draft and commit are the shared `useSelectionDraft`, stored when focus leaves the group or Save is pressed. A save awaits the list and diagram reads before it returns, so a second save quotes the new version rather than a stale one.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18c, block diagram elements and connections added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: The Edit element icon and its dialog are removed from the block editor
decisions.statement: Two routes to one edit is the inconsistency the style guide forbids; a shared, locked or read-only box shows its description and display note as text.
decisions.rationale: Double-clicking a box still opens its inside.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18c, block diagram elements and connections added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Quick links and tags on create
decisions.statement: An element or connection added to a canvas has no create form, so `QuickLinkField` is not shown at creation; tags (`RecordTags`) and components are in the card from the moment the record exists, and links are made from the record's Links panel (the diagram page's own).
decisions.rationale: Omitting the quick links is the stated reason: a link needs a record that exists, and the record now exists first.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18c, block diagram elements and connections added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: The enumeration
decisions.statement: `canvasCreations.json` lists every creation on both canvases (state, marker, transition, element, connection, boundary link, note, existing element, view switch) with its path, and every dialog each editor page renders with its role.
decisions.rationale: `backend/tests/test_canvas_creations.py` fails for a handler that is missing or a dialog that is not listed, so a new creation cannot add a form without a recorded reason. The two dialog-first entries (adding existing elements, a view switch) are choices among records or configuration, not shapes drawn.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18c, block diagram elements and connections added at once (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: A label column on the state
decisions.statement: `VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, plain text, never markup (the server stores it, the browser and the SVG draw it as text).
decisions.rationale: It rides the existing state create and update payloads; no new endpoint, gate or permission. The limit is `SYMBOL_LABEL_LENGTH` and the field's `maxLength`; a longer value is refused by the API (422) and cut on import from a file from elsewhere.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18d, symbol labels and condition wording (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Only a marker carries one
decisions.statement: An ordinary state's name is drawn in its box, so a label there would never be seen: the API refuses one (400, "Only an initial, final or choice state can carry a symbol label."), and changing a marker to an ordinary state clears its label rather than refusing the kind change (the person has already chosen the new kind; keeping hidden text would reappear if the kind were changed back).
decisions.rationale: The card shows the field for marker kinds only, and clears it from the draft when the kind is changed to an ordinary state. The marker's name field is captioned "Name (Outline and exports)" so it is not mistaken for the drawn text (R4); the ordinary state's stays "Name".
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18d, symbol labels and condition wording (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: A label grows the drawn symbol, not the stored box
decisions.statement: The plan's "grow to a fixed larger size" is implemented as a render-time rule, `marker_frame` / `markerFrame`: a symbol with a label is drawn at least `LABELLED_MARKERS[kind].size` (initial 52, final 72, choice 96), centred on the stored box, and lines attach to that frame.
decisions.rationale: Alternatives: rewriting the box when a label is set or cleared. Rejected because the layout is saved separately and held locally with undo (a server-side resize would be lost by the local layout, and a clear would need to know whether the box had been resized by hand). A diagram with no labels is drawn exactly as before and nothing is rewritten. A marker is not resizable, so the stored box is always the unlabelled size. The text is wrapped to the symbol's text width over at most three lines and cut with an ellipsis; white on a filled symbol (initial dot, final disc), the page's text colour in the diamond.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18d, symbol labels and condition wording (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Generic canvas extension (Phase 18d)
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvasNode.markerText` (`text`, `width`, `lines`, `onFill`) draws plain text inside a marker; no architecture code in the canvas, so Modules 16 and 17 can label a gateway or event.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18d, symbol labels and condition wording (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Mermaid cannot carry it
decisions.statement: `stateDiagram-v2` has no text on `[*]` or `<<choice>>`.
decisions.rationale: The Mermaid export writes a choice's label in its comment line (`%% STE-003 Battery low?`) and the limit is stated on the export page; the SVG, PNG, bundle and CSV keep it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18d, symbol labels and condition wording (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Condition wording
decisions.statement: The transition field, its help, the Outline column, the Selection card's read-only label, the findings text, the help for the Kind and Add menus, the website page and the glossary read **Condition (guard)** (the help gives an example and says each line leaving a choice needs its own).
decisions.rationale: The glossary's **Guard** entry points to **Condition (guard)**. Stored names, the API, exports and the `guard` focus key keep `guard`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18d, symbol labels and condition wording (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: A per-person preference, not a diagram property
decisions.statement: The choice is kept in `localStorage` (`useSnapToGrid`, wrapped in try and catch, with an in-memory copy when storage is blocked), shared by both editors and open tabs, off by default.
decisions.rationale: It is not stored with the diagram, so it needs no column, bundle entry, template classification or migration and changes nothing another person sees; it does not move a box that is already placed. A server-side user preference (`useUiPreference`) was rejected: R5 asked for this browser, and a grid choice that follows an account across devices with different screens is not wanted.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18e, snap to grid (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: One generic canvas mechanism
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvas` takes `snapGrid` (size, 20 canvas units, fixed), `snapOn` and `snapInvertKey`.
decisions.rationale: React Flow snaps drags and arrow-key moves in absolute coordinates (so a nested state shares the top-level grid) and the canvas puts the edges a resize moved on the grid when the resize ends (`graphSnap.snapResize`; an edge it did not move stays, so a resize never moves an off-grid corner). An Alt+arrow resize steps by the grid while snapping. A free leader end snaps by its centre. The dot grid is drawn only while snapping applies; a canvas given no grid keeps its plain dotted background, and the two editors, which now give one, show no dots while it is off. `graphSnap.snapApplies` is the one rule: the setting, inverted while the invert key is held during a pointer gesture (a press that began on a box or a resize handle), never for a key-driven move.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18e, snap to grid (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Shift clashed with React Flow's box selection, and is now off
decisions.statement: The plan required proving Shift did not clash.
decisions.rationale: It did: React Flow turns any press made while Shift is held, including one on a box, into a selection rectangle and swallows it, so a Shift drag could not start. The canvas's selection is single by design (`multiSelectionKeyCode` is null and a batch of select changes keeps the last), so Shift box selection never worked as a feature; `selectionKeyCode={null}` turns it off for every canvas consumer. Alt stays reserved for the key resize, so the plan's fallback (return the choice to the User) was not needed. Overrule by asking for another invert key (`snapInvertKey` is a prop) and for box selection to be built properly with multiple selection.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18e, snap to grid (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: One shared RecordDiagramsCard on the element and connection pages, directly under the details card
decisions.statement: It replaces `ElementStateMachinesCard` (deleted).
decisions.rationale: One list: code, name, type, how the record appears and status, each row linking to its editor. An element's heading carries **New state machine diagram** (`NewStateMachineDiagramButton`), drawn once the project's modules are known and only while the state machine sub-component is on, since the create would be refused otherwise. A record on no diagram reads "Not on any diagram."; a failed read leaves the card out.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18f, a Diagrams card under the details (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Two reads, one bulk path
decisions.statement: `GET /elements/{id}/diagrams` and `GET /connections/{id}/diagrams` (`record_diagram_routes.py`, `record_diagrams.py`).
decisions.rationale: Placements, diagrams, ancestors and ancestor names are loaded in bulk, so the statements do not grow with the number of diagrams (`test_architecture_record_diagrams.py` compares two sizes). Archived diagrams are left out, as the diagram lists leave them out.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18f, a Diagrams card under the details (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Where a connection is "drawn"
decisions.statement: The diagram resolver is run over that one connection and the diagram's placed elements, so a line rolled up to ancestors follows the one rule the diagram itself uses: `drawn` when the line joins the connection's own ends, `rolled_up` when it joins ancestors, absent when both ends fall inside one box or an end is not drawn.
decisions.rationale: View toggles are a view state and are not applied, and bridging through other connections is not reproduced; a diagram that can draw the line lists it even while a toggle hides it. A boundary-box line of a scoped diagram is not listed as a drawing of the outer connection.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18f, a Diagrams card under the details (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: How an element appears
decisions.statement: `placed` (its own box), `inside` (only the nearest drawn ancestor, named with its code, is drawn; the name is blank for an ancestor the person may not read) or `describes` (a state machine diagram of the element).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18f, a Diagrams card under the details (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Visibility adds no new rule
decisions.statement: The element read goes through `records.read_element` (a hidden or another project's element is a 404, the same as its page); a diagram type whose sub-component is switched off for the project is absent, indistinguishable from none (a connection's read answers an empty list when block diagrams are off).
decisions.rationale: A diagram carries no per-viewer access of its own, so nothing else is filtered.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18f, a Diagrams card under the details (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: A generic canvas badge
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvasNode.badges` (`GraphNodeBadge`: icon, accessible name, optional count, `onActivate`, or `items` for several targets) is drawn by `GraphNodeBadges` as a real button on the node's top left corner.
decisions.rationale: It sits beside the clipped box, never changes the node's size, avoids the corner attach points and a comment pin (top right), and a press, double-click or key on it never drags, selects or opens the node beneath it. One item opens at once; several open a small `Popover` list. It is the sibling after its box in the DOM, so Tab reaches it next. Nothing in the canvas knows what a badge means, so a later workflow or glossary canvas can mark a sub-process or a linked term.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18g, a state machine badge and a round trip (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: The model carries the diagrams
decisions.statement: `ModelElement.state_machines` (id, code, name) comes from one bulk query in `diagram_model.build_model` for the readable elements, scoped to the diagram's own project (a state machine diagram another project made of a shared element is not the consumer's to list), archived ones left out, empty for a locked element and when the state machine sub-component is off for the project (the same gate as…
decisions.rationale: the Diagrams card). `test_architecture_diagram_model.py` pins each case and that the statements do not grow with the number of elements or diagrams. No new table, so no bundle, template, generator or migration change.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18g, a state machine badge and a round trip (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Keyboard and non-pointer routes
decisions.statement: The Selection card gains **Open state machine diagram** (an icon action; one entry per diagram in the overflow menu when there are several) and the Outline lists each element's diagrams (a table column and buttons in the tree).
decisions.rationale: All three go through one `openMachine`, which asks before leaving unsaved changes, as opening an element's inside does.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18g, a state machine badge and a round trip (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Round trip
decisions.statement: The way there carries `?from=<block diagram id>`; the way back carries `?select=<element id>` (`stateMachineLinks.ts`).
decisions.rationale: Neither is trusted: the state machine page reads `from` through the project's diagram API, so a diagram of another project or one the person cannot read is a 404 and is ignored; the block diagram page selects a `select` only when it draws that box, and the link's selection ends (the parameter is dropped) as soon as the person selects anything else, so clearing the selection does not bring it back. A new generic `RecordHeader returnTo` places the control beside the back link; `ReturnLink` ("Return to DGM-001 Main system") is the shared link, and with no usable `from` (a reload from the list, a pasted link) the page offers an **Open in diagram** menu of the block diagrams that draw the element (the Diagrams card's read), so the way back never depends on history. A diagram that only contains the element inside a drawn ancestor is offered too; nothing is selected there.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18g, a state machine badge and a round trip (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: One list of terms
decisions.statement: `ARCHITECTURE_TERMS` (`help.ts`) holds each label that is not a form field with its help text; `TermCaption` reads it for a read-only Selection card label.
decisions.rationale: Form fields keep passing `ARCHITECTURE_HELP.<key>`, and the same key feeds the list, so one text serves every surface. The glossary entries use the same wording in longer form.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18h, help for notation and domain terms (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Shared components
decisions.statement: `DetailCard` takes `help` (a `(?)` after the heading); `HelpHeader` is the one shape for a column header with help (a header is not a form field, so a plain `<th>` is not a field-help case, but a header naming a term needs the same affordance); `CollapsibleSection` already took `help`.
decisions.rationale: A port's direction and type selects have no caption, so each is wrapped in a `Tooltip`, as the style guide allows for a control with no caption.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18h, help for notation and domain terms (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 7: Guard against regression
