decisions.statement: `scripts/check_architecture_term_help.py` fails a listed term drawn as a bare `<th>`, `<dt>`, heading or title, or a field with a listed label that says `helpNotNeeded`, and fails a listed term no surface uses; `backend/tests/test_architecture_term_help.py` pins it with positive and negative cases.
decisions.rationale: This follows the field-help check (empty baseline) and is a static check, not a rendering test, because the rule is about source shape and runs in the backend suite with the other check scripts.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 7: Phase 18h, help for notation and domain terms (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: One shared pair of buttons and one key rule
decisions.statement: `EditHistoryButtons` draws Undo and Redo and installs `useHistoryShortcuts`, so the buttons and the keys cannot disagree; both editors use it in place of two hand-written buttons.
decisions.rationale: The match (`historyAction`) is by the character typed, either case: Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z on Apple devices; Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y elsewhere. The other platform's modifier is never accepted, so the Windows key is not taken. The platform is `utils/platform.isApplePlatform`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19a, Undo and Redo on the keyboard (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Where the keys are left alone
decisions.statement: In a text field, text area, select or editable region (the field keeps its own undo), while a `dialog`, `alertdialog`, `menu` or `aria-modal` element is open, in a read-only editor, and when there is no step to take.
decisions.rationale: `preventDefault` is called only when a step was taken.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19a, Undo and Redo on the keyboard (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Capture phase
decisions.statement: A first version on the bubble phase never acted: React Flow marks a key pressed on a box as handled before it reaches the document, so the `defaultPrevented` guard skipped it.
decisions.rationale: The listener is on the document in the capture phase, ahead of the canvas's own handling.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19a, Undo and Redo on the keyboard (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Rows are text rows, menus with more than one level are a tree
decisions.statement: `.menu-item` is restyled (no `btn` class, no border or fill at rest, a tint on hover and focus, danger as coloured text).
decisions.rationale: `ActionMenuList` builds a tree from the items: an item with `children`, or a run of more than one item with the same `group`, is a parent row (chevron, `aria-expanded`) whose rows sit in a labelled `role="group"` indented under a guide line, to three levels; it replaces the side flyout and its hover timer. The first parent starts open; a group holding one item keeps its name as a heading. `Popover menu` adds the tighter padding, a soft shadow and a caret toward the trigger. `MenuButton` and `ActionMenu` share it, so every call site changes together.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19b, the Add menu and the shared menu style (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Keys on every menu
decisions.statement: Up, Down, Home and End move through the visible rows (previously only a menu with a submenu had them); Right opens a parent and moves to its first row; Left or Escape closes the level the focus is in and returns to its row, Escape closing only that level first; Tab closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger (previously Tab was trapped inside the popover).
decisions.rationale: Child items now honour `disabled` and `onDragStart` like top-level ones (they ignored both).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19b, the Add menu and the shared menu style (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Consequence worth knowing
decisions.statement: A row inside a closed parent is not in the page.
decisions.rationale: Add block in the report designer, the list actions menu and the diagram Export menu now open one group first and show the others as closed rows; the specs and stories that chose a row in another group go through `chooseMenuRow` (stories, `testing/menuTree.ts`) and `clickMenuRow` (Playwright, `tests/menuTree.ts`), which open closed parents until the row appears. The report designer's long Add block list is now "Most used" open and "Other blocks" closed: one more click to reach a block in the second group. Flagged for the User: if that cost is not wanted for a long list, an option on `ActionMenuItem` for a group to start open could be added; it is not built.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19b, the Add menu and the shared menu style (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Comment mode and read-only
decisions.statement: Neither connects anything, so neither draws points (`visibility: hidden`; read-only already did).
decisions.rationale: Comment mode used to draw them, inert; that is the one visible change outside the new rule.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19c, attach points near the pointer (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Tone None
decisions.statement: `NoteTone` gains `none`: the note draws its text alone, with no fill, border, dashed edge or "Note" caption.
decisions.rationale: `tone` is a plain `String(16)` validated by `NoteIn`, so no migration. The word "Note" was the node's caption in `canvasNodes`; a none-tone note has none, and its text stays the accessible name (a control with no name is not acceptable). The canvas stays generic: `GraphNodeTone` `none` and `GraphCanvasNode.placeholder`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19d, notes with no tone and a Note mode (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Findable when empty or hovered
decisions.statement: A text-only note with no text would be invisible, so the editor draws a faint dashed outline while it is hovered, and while its text is empty (the stand-in "Empty note" is muted and italic).
decisions.rationale: The selection ring is unchanged. This is editing chrome only: the server SVG and Mermaid skip an empty none-tone note and draw no block for a filled one. An empty note of any other tone keeps its block, as before.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19d, notes with no tone and a Note mode (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Server drawing
decisions.statement: `diagram_svg._drawn_notes` is the one rule for which notes are drawn, used by the drawing and the document's extent, so a skipped note adds no empty margin.
decisions.rationale: A none-tone note's leader keeps the neutral line colour.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19d, notes with no tone and a Note mode (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Note mode
decisions.statement: A **Note** toggle beside **Comment** (`NoteModeToggle` over the shared `CanvasModeToggle`, which `CommentModeToggle` now also uses): a click on empty canvas places a note centred on the click, selects it and puts the cursor in its text; the mode stays on.
decisions.rationale: Only one of Note and Comment is on: turning one on turns the other off, and a comment started elsewhere (Pin to diagram) wins while it lasts. Add note in the Add menu remains the keyboard route and now also puts the cursor in the text. A click on empty canvas in Note mode does not deselect (it places a note), and an archived diagram's switch is unavailable. Only the block diagram editor has notes, so only it has the switch.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19d, notes with no tone and a Note mode (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Cursor placement
decisions.statement: `autoFocus` did not hold for a note added from the Add menu: the closing menu returns focus to its button after the new card mounts.
decisions.rationale: The note editor focuses its text one animation frame later instead; an element's name field was unaffected only because its creation waits for the server.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19d, notes with no tone and a Note mode (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: One routing mechanism
decisions.statement: A drawn line stores an ordered list of vertices (`{x, y}` in absolute canvas units, at most 16, each finite and within the coordinate limit the placements use) and a `smooth` flag.
decisions.rationale: Absolute units keep a box nested in another and the snap grid of the editors behaving as on the screen. The path rule is one pure function written twice and pinned together: `graphLinePath.ts` and `diagram_line_path.py`, with `graphLinePathCases.json` produced from the Python rule (`UPDATE_SHAPE_CASES=1`, the loop's mechanism) and compared by a story. Smooth is a Catmull-Rom curve written as cubic Beziers; a line with no vertices is always straight. Both sides round halves toward positive infinity (`Math.round`), because Python's `round` differs on values such as `20.005` and the two paths then differed in the last digit. Orthogonal routing is not built (no stated need).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19e, vertices on lines (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Where it is stored
decisions.statement: A block diagram line has no row of its own (it is the drawn line for an element pair, possibly standing for several connections), so `points` and `smooth` widen the anchors row (`architecture_diagram_anchors`), keyed as before by the pair.
decisions.rationale: The row's "something is set" check now counts vertices, so a line with vertices and automatic ends is stored. A transition is drawn once, so `points` and `smooth` are columns on `architecture_transitions`. Migration 0189 adds both with empty defaults, so no existing line changes; the down migration deletes anchor rows that held only vertices (they would break the old check) and drops the columns. A stored anchor is read for the opposite direction of its pair with its points reversed, as its attach points already were.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19e, vertices on lines (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Open ends follow the vertex
decisions.statement: With vertices an automatic end is the attach point nearest the vertex beside it (first for the source, last for the target), not the other box.
decisions.rationale: `routeAttachPoints` and `route_points` hold this, with four shared cases added to `graphAttachPointCases.json`. Without vertices the rule is exactly the earlier one.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19e, vertices on lines (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Named "Vertices", not "Route" or "Bend points"
decisions.statement: The plan called the section Route. "Route" is already a term on the Outline (Direct, Rolled up, Bridged, with its own help), so a second meaning would be misleading.
decisions.rationale: The first build used "Bend points", which the user rejected as informal under the Formal Wording rule; "vertex" is the geometric term CAD and vector drawing use for a point a polyline passes through (Inkscape and Illustrator say "node" and "anchor point"; "anchor" already means a line's stored route in this module). The Selection card section, the Outline column and the help term are "Vertices"; the term is in `ARCHITECTURE_TERMS`, so its help is the same on every surface. Code identifiers keep `waypoint` for the stored list (`LineWaypoint`, `clean_waypoints`); users never read them. The plan's "Routed" mark became a count column, which says more.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19e, vertices on lines (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Keyboard route
decisions.statement: `LineVertexFields`, shared by both Selection cards: X and Y fields per vertex (applied once on blur or Enter through a new `InlineTextInput commitOnBlur`, so one edit is one undo step), Add and Reset as icon actions, remove per vertex, and a Smooth curve switch that is unavailable with no vertex.
decisions.rationale: Added vertices go below the middle of the last segment (`suggestWaypoint`).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19e, vertices on lines (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Server drawings
decisions.statement: The block diagram and state machine SVG (and the PNG made from them) draw a routed line as one path, include the vertices in the image's extent, and skip the sideways offset used to separate parallel connections (the pair shares one route).
decisions.rationale: Mermaid has no routing; its pages say so.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19e, vertices on lines (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Challenge, not built
decisions.statement: Vertices are not removed when a box moves: they are absolute, so moving a box can leave a vertex far from the line it was shaping.
decisions.rationale: Following the box would need vertices stored relative to a box, which does not suit a line between two boxes; Reset vertices is the way back.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19e, vertices on lines (2026-11-15)

decisions.title: Own table, several per note
decisions.statement: `architecture_note_leaders` (`note_id`, `sort_order`, `kind` element, connection or point with exactly its target column, `start_point`, `points`, `smooth`, `start_style`, `end_style` none, arrow or dot), at most ten per note.
decisions.rationale: The migration moves each existing leader into a row with its kind and target unchanged and `leader_arrow` as an end style of arrow or none (start style none), then drops the note's leader columns; the downgrade writes each note's first leader back (a second leader, the start point, vertices and styles are lost). A leader whose target had already been deleted read as none and gets no row.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19f, leaders as drawn lines (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Deleting a target removes its leader
decisions.statement: The target foreign keys cascade, so the leader row goes and the note stays.
decisions.rationale: Before, the column was emptied and read as none; with several leaders per note an empty row has no meaning.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19f, leaders as drawn lines (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: One rule for start and end
decisions.statement: A chosen start point wins; an open start is the note point nearest the first vertex, else nearest what the line ends at.
decisions.rationale: A box end with vertices is the box point nearest the last vertex; with none, the nearest pair, as before. `diagram_svg._leader_run` and `GraphCanvasView` apply the same rule.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19f, leaders as drawn lines (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Layout save
decisions.statement: `NoteIn.leaders` replaces the single-leader fields; a leader keeps its `id` when it belongs to its own note (400 for another note's, a repeat or an unknown id); a new box target must be placed and a new connection must be this project's, as before.
decisions.rationale: Notes are flushed before their leaders.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19f, leaders as drawn lines (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: A setting of the diagram, on both diagram types
decisions.statement: `line_hops` (boolean, off by default, `server_default false`) on `architecture_diagrams` and `architecture_state_machine_diagrams`, so no diagram changes on upgrade.
decisions.rationale: It is stored, not a per-browser preference like snap to grid, because the exports must draw what the screen draws. It is changed through the diagram's own update (`DiagramUpdate.line_hops`, `StateMachineDiagramUpdate.line_hops`) with the version lock and the existing "updated" audit event (field names only); the block diagram's create payload also takes it. The editors set it from the settings gear (shared `LineHopsSetting`), not from the create and edit forms: it matters only once lines cross, which needs a drawing, and the forms are about the record's identity. This is a deliberate departure from "create and edit share one field group" (a field the edit form does not edit is not in the create form either).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19g, line hops (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: One rule, written twice and pinned together
decisions.statement: `graphLineHops.ts` and `diagram_line_hops.py`, with `graphLineHopCases.json` produced from the Python rule (`UPDATE_SHAPE_CASES=1`) and compared by a story, as the line path is.
decisions.rationale: It is a separate cases file from `graphLinePathCases.json` (the plan said to extend that one) because a path case is one line and a hop case is a set of lines with the paths of those that hop. Curves are flattened (16 steps per Bezier span, through `curveSpans`, now shared with `linePath`); only +, -, *, / and square roots are used (no `hypot`, `dist` or trigonometry) so both languages give the same numbers.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19g, line hops (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Where it is drawn
decisions.statement: The block diagram and state machine server SVG (and so the PNG, which is that document drawn in the browser) draw the arcs; `diagram_svg` now works out every line's geometry (`_edge_runs`, `_leader_runs`) before drawing so the hop rule sees the same points the lines are drawn with (after the sideways offset of parallel lines).
decisions.rationale: Mermaid has no hops, a limit stated on both pages. The canvas computes the hops from the same attach points and vertices as it draws, in `GraphCanvasView` (`GraphCanvas lineHops`), and draws a crossed line through the routed edge's `hopPath`; a plain line that gets a hop becomes a routed one (no handles, its label kept). While a vertex is dragged the line is drawn without its hop. The path ends within 3 pixels of where React Flow's own handle ends the line, because the hop path starts at the attach point.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19g, line hops (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Ordering across the screen and the file
decisions.statement: The id that decides is the line's id: the resolved line's id, a transition's id and a leader's id, the same strings on both sides.
decisions.rationale: A leader or connection not yet saved has a client-made key until the save, so a crossing involving one may swap which line hops once it is saved.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19g, line hops (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 8: Audit and result
decisions.statement: Moved to the shared row: `SplitButtonTrigger` alternatives and `ReportExportButton` formats (now `ActionMenuList` in `Popover menu`; the format list closes on choosing, as before, and the trigger shows "Exporting…"), `EntitySwitcher` links, the add-from-filter row of `MultiSelectDropdown`, the `GraphNodeBadges` list and the options of `UserAutocomplete`, `TagInput` and `QuickLinkField` (one…
decisions.rationale: `menu-item` class, with `aria-selected` as the highlight in `theme.css`, replacing per-option inline styles). Already conformant: `HeaderSearch`, `TreeSelect`, `ProjectNavSection`'s more list, `ResourceMenu` (a page navigation, not a popover). The full table is in the style guide's action menu pattern.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19h, menu sweep across the app (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Native selects keep the browser's list
decisions.statement: `FilterSelect`, `LabeledSelect` and `InlineSelect` wrap `<select>`, whose option list the page cannot style; replacing it would lose native keyboard, touch and accessibility behaviour for a look only.
decisions.rationale: They take no change.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 8: Phase 19h, menu sweep across the app (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: Limit 256
decisions.statement: `SYMBOL_LABEL_LENGTH` is 256 (schemas, bundle reader, Mermaid, the field's `maxLength`); `architecture_states.label` widens to `VARCHAR(256)` (0192; the downgrade cuts a longer label to 40).
decisions.rationale: The field is an auto-growing `TextAreaField` so a long label can be reviewed, shows "n of 256 characters" from 200 characters, and its help says a long remark reads better as a note.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20a, symbol labels: longer, whole words (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Whole words, the symbol grows
decisions.statement: `diagram_symbol_label.py` and `symbolLabelLayout.ts` hold one rule: lines break at spaces, after a hyphen, between full-width (East Asian) characters and at a typed line break, never inside a word; the symbol starts at its labelled base size (52, 72, 96) and grows by 4, to at most 320, until the text block holds with `LABEL_PADDING` (4 units, , 2026-11-16: a minimum distance between text and the…
decisions.rationale: inner edge of its symbol, and the same distance outside it) clear of the inner edge of the circle, the ring's disc or the diamond (`holds`: the block's nearest corner, measured at right angles inside the diamond's stroke, in integers so Python and TypeScript agree exactly). `TEXT_PERCENT` (56, 42 and 40 percent) only sets the width a line is first wrapped to. A word longer than the largest symbol is kept whole on its own line, `fits` is false and the field warns (a warning, never a clipped label). Alternative rejected: CSS wrapping with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` plus a line clamp, which is what split words.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20a, symbol labels: longer, whole words (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: A font-independent measure
decisions.statement: The server has no font and browsers differ, so widths come from a table of average glyph widths in thousandths of the font size (space, narrow, capital, wide, full width, other), integers only, so Python and TypeScript agree exactly; it is set wider than the glyphs of the system fonts (measured in the browser: the widest rendered label was 7% under it), so the real text keeps its padding.
decisions.rationale: `symbolLabelCases.json` (written by `test_architecture_symbol_label.py`, `UPDATE_SHAPE_CASES=1`) pins sizes, lines and widths for 13 labels on every kind, and `stateShapeCases.json` pins the base sizes, shares and the parametric drawings.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20a, symbol labels: longer, whole words (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: Labelled drawings are parametric
decisions.statement: `labelled_svg` / `labelledSvg` draw a marker at any size with its stroke width kept; the fixed `LABELLED_MARKERS` table is gone.
decisions.rationale: The canvas now takes the label as `GraphMarkerText.lines` (the consumer breaks them; `text`, `width` and the line limit are removed, no consumer other than the state machine editor and its stories used them) drawn with `white-space: pre`, so the screen and the server SVG show the same lines.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20a, symbol labels: longer, whole words (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: Padding outside a symbol
decisions.statement: Label position (20b) puts text at least `LABEL_PADDING` from the symbol's outer edge; the constant is shared for it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20a, symbol labels: longer, whole words (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: A per-symbol choice
decisions.statement: `architecture_states.label_position` (`VARCHAR(16)`, default `inside`, a check constraint to `inside`, `left`, `right`, `above`, `below`; a core enum is not involved, `LabelPosition` is the module's own).
decisions.rationale: Inside is the default, so no stored diagram changes. Only an initial, final or choice state may place its label outside (the API refuses a position other than `inside` on an ordinary state with a 400, and a kind change to an ordinary state resets it, as it clears the label). A bundle row carries it (`label_position`; an older file with none, an unknown value or a value on an ordinary state becomes `inside` on import, the same tidying the label gets); it is a record-table column named by its display label (`Label position`, export only, like the other state columns); it is not a searchable field (no free text); the audit event's `fields` list names it. The state machine diagram's template classification is unchanged (the states travel as configuration).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20b, label position (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Outside text is drawn beside the symbol at its plain size
decisions.statement: `diagram_symbol_label.beside_label` / `symbolLabelLayout.besideLabel` wrap the label to `BESIDE_MAX_WIDTH` (160 units, whole words, a longer word stays whole), measure it with the same width table rounded up to a whole unit, and place the text block against one side of the symbol's own box, `LABEL_PADDING` (4 units, , 2026-11-16) from its outer edge, centred along the side and aligned toward the…
decisions.rationale: symbol (left text right-aligned, right text left-aligned, above and below centred). The shared cases file holds 128 placements, written by `test_architecture_symbol_label.py` and read by the browser's copy. No size warning applies outside the symbol, so the field's word warning shows only for Inside.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20b, label position (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The node stays the symbol, the text overflows it
decisions.statement: Making the canvas node the union of symbol and text puts the side middles, which are where lines meet a marker, in the air beside the symbol, so every line to a labelled symbol would end away from it; a separate attach box would have meant a second geometry in `graphAttachPoints`, `diagram_points` and the cases between them.
decisions.rationale: Instead the canvas node is the stored box (the symbol), `GraphMarkerText.block` places the text relative to it, and the text takes pointer events, so a click or drag on the text selects and moves the symbol. Cost: the text lies outside the node's measured box, so the opening view would crop a label at the edge of a diagram; the canvas computes the most any label reaches beyond its marker (`labelOverhang`) and gives `fitView` that much plus 24 pixels of padding (the editors fit at a zoom of at most 1, so pixels are never fewer than canvas units). The server's SVG includes the text in the drawing's extent (`_reach`).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20b, label position (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: A line avoids the side the text is on
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvasNode.attachPoints` (a generic field: the points an open end may choose; a marker defaults to the four side middles) is set by the state machine editor to the side middles without the label's side (`markerAttachPoints` / `marker_attach_points`; a blank label covers no side), and the server's SVG uses the same list, so an automatic line never runs through the text.
decisions.rationale: An end a person chose in the Selection card (all four sides stay in its select) is used as given, and all four handles stay available for drawing a line.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20b, label position (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Visible text and accessible name differ on purpose
decisions.statement: The four Selection card buttons (`StateSelectionFields`, `TransitionSelectionFields`, `ElementSelectionFields`, `ConnectionSelectionFields`) read **Save** and keep their earlier names ("Save state", "Save transition", "Save element", "Save connection") through `aria-label`; the toolbar button of both editors reads **Save** and is named **Save diagram**.
decisions.rationale: A screen reader therefore never meets two controls named "Save" in one view, and the visible text is part of each name, so voice input that says "click Save" still works.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20c, Save wording (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: Wider than the request
decisions.statement: Only the state card was named, but the transition, element and connection cards had the same "Save <noun>" text and the same card shape; leaving three of four different would have been the inconsistency the round exists to remove.
decisions.rationale: The other buttons in both editors were searched for identical accessible names: none remain (dialog saves are in a dialog of their own, comment saves sit in a thread).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20c, Save wording (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: A note has an optional Title
decisions.statement: `architecture_diagram_notes.title` (`VARCHAR(120)`, empty by default; `enums.NOTE_TITLE_MAX`, the same limit in `NoteIn` and the field's `maxLength`) is drawn in bold above the text.
decisions.rationale: Rejected: "the first line is the title", because a hidden convention cannot carry field help, a limit or its own column.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21a, note title, line breaks and alignment (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Typed line breaks are kept . Cause verified at build
decisions.statement: Two defects, as the plan suspected: the server's `_wrap` split the whole text into words (`value.split()`), so every typed break and blank line was lost in the PNG and SVG; and the canvas label had no `white-space` rule, so the browser collapsed them.
decisions.rationale:
The SVG now wraps each typed line on its own (a blank line stays one empty line) and the canvas label is `white-space: pre-line` (the generic node, so any consumer's label keeps a break it was given). A line longer than the note still wraps between words. Mermaid writes the title in bold and the typed lines, joined with `
`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21a, note title, line breaks and alignment (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Alignment is Left, Centre or Right
decisions.statement: `text_align` (`VARCHAR(16)`, default `left`, a check constraint, `enums.NoteAlign`, `labels.NOTE_ALIGN_LABEL` and the frontend `NOTE_TEXT_ALIGN_LABEL`) applies to the title and the text.
decisions.rationale: **Full justification is not offered**: SVG has no justified text, so the exports could not match the screen, and the product's rule is that the two agree. Overrule to offer it with an approximation in the exports. Mermaid centres a node's text, so the alignment is not written there (stated in its docstring and the docs).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21a, note title, line breaks and alignment (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Generic canvas fields, nothing note-specific in core
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvasNode.title` and `textAlign` (`GraphTextAlign`) draw the heading and the alignment; a node with a title and no label is named by the title, and the accessible name and the list view read "title: label".
decisions.rationale: The module maps its note onto them (`canvasNodes`), so the module boundary holds. A note with only a title is not a placeholder; one with neither still is.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21a, note title, line breaks and alignment (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The empty rule follows the title
decisions.statement: The server SVG skips an empty note with no tone only when it has neither text nor title (`_drawn_notes`), and Mermaid writes a note with either.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21a, note title, line breaks and alignment (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 10: The Selection card
decisions.statement: `DiagramNoteEditor` has Title, Note text and Alignment above Tone; the title and the text apply when the field loses focus (one undo step each), the alignment and the tone at once.
decisions.rationale: The card's callbacks collapse to one `onChange(patch)` (`NotePatch`), so Phase 21b's size and Phase 20d's state machine notes add a field, not a prop. **A real defect fixed on the way:** the card's text field kept what was typed after an Undo or Redo (its draft was never re-read from the note); both fields now take the note's value again when it changes under the card.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21a, note title, line breaks and alignment (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 10: Notes are not searched
decisions.statement: A note is free text on a drawing, not a described property, so the module's search deliberately has no note field (`search.py`'s design notes); the new title follows that rule rather than opening a second reading.
decisions.rationale: Overrule to add a `notes` field to the diagram search provider.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21a, note title, line breaks and alignment (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Size is Automatic or Manual per note
decisions.statement: `architecture_diagram_notes.size_mode` (`NoteSizeMode`, check constraint, `labels.NOTE_SIZE_MODE_LABEL`, frontend `NOTE_SIZE_MODE_LABEL`).
decisions.rationale: The migration sets existing notes with no tone to `automatic` and every other note to `manual`, so a box a person sized does not change on upgrade; the stored width and height are never rewritten. An older bundle with no `size_mode` gets the same rule on import; an unknown value becomes `manual`.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21b, a note sizes itself to its content (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The stored size is kept under Automatic
decisions.statement: The drawn frame is computed (`drawn_size` / `drawnSize`, `noteFrame` in the editor), never stored over the Manual size.
decisions.rationale: Choosing Manual in the card stores the frame the note is drawn at now; choosing Automatic leaves the stored size for a return. Dragging a handle, or Alt and an arrow key, on an Automatic note makes it Manual at the size reached (`resizeItems`), so no handle is dead. A note with neither title nor text has no content frame and keeps its stored size (the placeholder).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21b, a note sizes itself to its content (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The API default is Manual
decisions.statement: `NoteIn.size_mode` defaults to `manual` (and so does the column), so a caller that sends a width and height keeps it; the editor's `newNote` is Automatic, which is where "new notes are Automatic" is applied.
decisions.rationale: Rejected: an `automatic` default, which would silently ignore the size every existing API caller and test sends.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21b, a note sizes itself to its content (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 10: One layout, two implementations
decisions.statement: `diagram_note_layout.py` and `noteLayout.ts` return the lines and the frame from the title, the text and the maximum width (320 units; a word wider than that stays whole and sets the width); `noteLayoutCases.json` (written by `test_architecture_note_layout.py`, `UPDATE_SHAPE_CASES=1`) is what both are tested against.
decisions.rationale: Widths come from the symbol label's width table at the note's font size (13, line height 16), the bold title 10% wider (`TITLE_PERCENT`), and a toned note adds 14 units for its caption. **Deviation from the plan's wording:** the table was not moved to a new shared module; `text_width`/`textWidth` and `wrap_label`/`wrapLabel` take a font size and a percentage instead, which gives the one table with no import churn.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21b, a note sizes itself to its content (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The server draws every note from the same lines
decisions.statement: The SVG and PNG now wrap a note's text with the shared measure at 13 units (it was an 11-unit font approximated by character count), with the frame from `drawn_size` applied once at the top of `render_diagram` (`_framed_notes`), so the leaders' attach points, the box, the text and the picture's bounds read one frame.
decisions.rationale: A Manual note that does not fit still ends its last line with an ellipsis, now measured with the same table. This changes how a Manual note's text is wrapped in the exports (closer to the canvas), not its box.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21b, a note sizes itself to its content (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Padding is measured from the frame to the text, border included
decisions.statement: `NOTE_PADDING` is 6 units; the generic `GraphCanvasNode.inset` sets the padding and the stylesheet subtracts the border widths (the 4-unit left border stays, inside the padding), so the stripe of a toned note is kept.
decisions.rationale: Every note carries the inset, Automatic or Manual, so the look does not change when the size mode does.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21b, a note sizes itself to its content (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The Selection card has a Size select
decisions.statement: Automatic or Manual, with help stating that a resize makes the note Manual.
decisions.rationale: Bundle (`size_mode` written, older bundles read by rule), baseline and template (a note travels in its diagram's bundle entry), perf (probe and generator populate it, the generator at random), demo seed (the Redundancy note is Automatic; edited, not run). Search, MCP, permissions and SOC 2 are not touched (a note is not searched, see Phase 21a).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21b, a note sizes itself to its content (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 10: One fit, two implementations
decisions.statement: `diagram_box_fit.py` and `elementBoxFit.ts` return the least width (the widest unbreakable word of the name, the caption, or the symbol, plus the insets), the name's lines at the drawn width and the least height (insets, the symbol at a fixed height of 40 plus a gap of 4, 16 per name line, 17 for the caption), on the symbol label's width table (the name measured at the bold factor, because the…
decisions.rationale: exports draw it bold). `elementBoxFitCases.json` (written by `test_architecture_box_fit.py`, `UPDATE_SHAPE_CASES=1`) is what both are tested against, at three stored widths. A box is never drawn below 80 by 40.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21c, an element box fits its symbol and text (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The drawn size is the larger of the stored size and the fit; the stored size is never rewritten
decisions.statement: `boxFrame` (editor) and `_framed_nodes` (server SVG, applied once at the top of `render_diagram` as for notes) are the only readers of a box's size, so the canvas node, a line's attach points, the free slot for a new box, a comment pin's anchor, a leader's suggested vertex and the exported drawing agree.
decisions.rationale: A symbol set on the element, on its type, or changed on the type later therefore never touches a stored layout. Boxes that were cut now draw larger to the right and down on existing diagrams and may overlap a neighbour (the alternative, rewriting stored sizes, was rejected, as in the plan); saving a layout stores the stored size, a deliberate resize stores the size reached.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21c, an element box fits its symbol and text (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The caption is the code and the type on both sides
decisions.statement: The screen draws "ELM-001 · Type", the export only the code; both measure the longer text, so the frame is the same.
decisions.rationale: A long type name therefore widens a box. **A locked box measures what it draws**, the code and "(not visible)" on the screen (`lockedBoxLabel`) and the code in the export, so its frames can differ by a few units (the one place the screen and the export differ).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21c, an element box fits its symbol and text (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The name is no longer cut in the export
decisions.statement: The SVG breaks the name between words with the shared measure and draws every line; the two-line limit and the ellipsis are gone for an element box.
decisions.rationale: A boundary box and a display note keep their own rules.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21c, an element box fits its symbol and text (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 10: Generic canvas inputs
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvasNode.minWidth` and `minHeight` are the least size a resize (a handle, Alt and an arrow key, the grid snap) may make the node, defaulting to 80 by 40; a node that gives them is `graph-node-fitted`, whose text is never squeezed (the room is reserved).
decisions.rationale: No core file names the module. The Selection card's size fields do not exist, so there is nothing to state a minimum on.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21c, an element box fits its symbol and text (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The picker uploads in place
decisions.statement: `SymbolPicker` (the one picker the type form, the element form and the Selection card share) shows **Upload a symbol** to a person the capabilities read says may change the library, otherwise nothing (not a disabled control).
decisions.rationale: The file goes through the existing upload endpoints into the library of the record's owner (the project, or the organisation for an organisation element or type), is chosen in the form's draft and is stored when the form is saved. The server's `architecture_admin` / `architecture_org_admin` check stays the only gate; the Playwright spec asserts `POST /symbols` still returns 403 for an Architect without the role. No new permission.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21d, upload from the symbol picker and a Gallery mode (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: An organisation capabilities read was needed
decisions.statement: Only the project had `GET .../capabilities`; an organisation element's or type's form had nothing to ask, and showing the control to everyone would have meant a refusal after the file was chosen.
decisions.rationale: `GET /api/v1/orgs/{org}/modules/architecture/capabilities` returns the same `CapabilitiesOut` (`manage_types`, true for `architecture_org_admin` or an organisation admin), open to anyone who may read the types, with a backend test. This is the one change X8's "no new endpoint" did not foresee; it adds no permission and no data.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21d, upload from the symbol picker and a Gallery mode (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 10: One upload, shared
decisions.statement: `useSymbolUpload(scope)` and `SymbolUploadField` are the upload and its refusal text for both the Symbols settings panel (changed in the same change) and the picker.
decisions.rationale: The picker's help says the file is added to the library for everyone in the project or organisation. The first upload in a child project that inherits a library still copies the inherited symbols down (the server's existing `materialize_inherited` step); the help states it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21d, upload from the symbol picker and a Gallery mode (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 10: Reload after an upload
decisions.statement: The picker remembers symbols it uploaded so they can be chosen at once, and callers reload their list through `useArchitectureReference().reloadSymbols` or their own `reload` (`onSymbolsChanged`).
decisions.rationale: A form saved after an upload that was then replaced by another choice leaves the uploaded symbol in the library; that is the stated behaviour (it is shared, and removed in the Symbols settings).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21d, upload from the symbol picker and a Gallery mode (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 10: A Selection-card side effect
decisions.statement: Opening the Gallery moves focus into a popover outside the card, which is the existing "leaving the card saves it" trigger, so pending edits in the card are stored when the grid opens.
decisions.rationale: Nothing new is stored that leaving the card would not store.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 10: Phase 21d, upload from the symbol picker and a Gallery mode (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: One mechanism, not a copy
decisions.statement: `architecture_diagram_notes` gains `state_machine_diagram_id` (CASCADE) and `diagram_id` becomes nullable, with a check that exactly one is set (`ck_architecture_diagram_notes_one_owner`).
decisions.rationale: `architecture_note_leaders` gains `state_id` and `transition_id` (CASCADE, so deleting a state or a transition removes only its leader and keeps the note) and the kinds `state` and `transition`; its target check needs the column of its own kind and no other. Existing rows are block diagram notes and are unchanged. A parallel table was rejected: it repeats the "second copy of one pattern" failure the style guide names, and the note card, the Outline section, the drawing and the bundle rows would each need a twin.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20d, notes in state machine diagrams (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Layout save carries the notes
decisions.statement: `StateMachineLayoutSave.notes` is the complete list when given (an annotation left out is deleted, a leader left out is deleted) and keeps the stored notes when left out (`None`), so a caller that does not know notes still saves a drawing.
decisions.rationale: The note replace logic is one function, `diagrams.sync_notes`, used by both layout saves; the owner passes how a new row names it and what its leaders may point at (`_check_leaders` for a block diagram, `state_machines._check_note_leaders` here). A block diagram refuses a state or transition target, a state machine diagram refuses an element or connection target, and a state or transition of another diagram is refused with 400; a note or leader id of another owner is refused; the diagram's `version` advances when notes change and not for an identical list.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20d, notes in state machine diagrams (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: The model carries the notes
decisions.statement: `StateMachineModel.notes` (the shared `NoteOut` with its leaders, which now also carry `state_id` and `transition_id`); the diagram's own list and detail reads are unchanged, so the cost of a list does not grow.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20d, notes in state machine diagrams (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Notes are not searched (as for a block diagram, 21a) and are not a record
decisions.statement: A note has no code and is not a registered type, so no summary, search provider, record table, link or tag applies; it travels inside its diagram's bundle entry.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20d, notes in state machine diagrams (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: Server drawing
decisions.statement: The SVG and PNG draw a note and its leaders with the block diagram's own functions (`_framed_notes`, `_leader_runs`, `_notes`); `_leader_run` takes a state's frame and a transition's middle as targets, by the same attach-point rule as for a box and a connection, and `state_machine_svg` computes its transition lines first, then the leaders, then the line hops over both (a leader hops like a…
decisions.rationale: connection leader does). A diagram with notes and no states is drawn, not reported empty, and the extent includes every note and leader point.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20d, notes in state machine diagrams (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: Bundles, templates and baselines
decisions.statement: A note and its leaders are `notes` in the state machine diagram's entry, written and read by the new `note_bundle.py` shared with the block diagram's bundle (the block diagram's inline code moved there): a leader names a state by name and a transition by its position in the diagram's list, the keys the comment pins already use, a leader whose target is not in the bundle is dropped with a warning…
decisions.rationale: and its note kept, at most 200 notes and ten leaders each are read (a bundle is not trusted to respect the API's caps), and an older bundle with no `notes` key reads as none. The template classification is unchanged (the diagram's entry is the unit), and a baseline snapshot is that entry, so a snapshot carries the notes.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20d, notes in state machine diagrams (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: Frontend: the note model is shared
decisions.statement: `noteModel.ts` holds the note and leader types and edits moved out of `diagramEditorModel.ts`, generic over any layout that holds `notes` (`addNote<L extends NotesLayout>(layout: L): L`), with the canvas mapping (`canvasNoteNodes`, `noteLeaderLines`), `moveNotes` and `resizeNotes`, so the block and state machine editors keep the rest of their own layout.
decisions.rationale: `DiagramLeaderEditor` takes the "Points at" options from its page (`targets`) instead of boxes and connections, and `NotesOutlineSection` is the Outline's Notes section for both. The state machine editor adds `StateMachineNoteCards` (the leader summary, the target list and the vertex suggestion for states and transitions), the Add menu's **Add note**, the Note mode toggle with Comment (never both on, Escape leaves), canvas leader drawing (`onConnect` and `onConnectEmpty` from a note), and removal of a selected note or leader by the Delete key at once (no confirmation, since Undo restores it; a state or transition is still confirmed). `mergeModel` drops the leaders of a state or transition the server no longer has, so a reload after a delete never keeps a leader the next save would refuse.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20d, notes in state machine diagrams (2026-11-16)

decisions.title: One rule over the whole drawing
decisions.statement: `graphLineAnchors.ts` (browser) and `diagram_line_anchors.py` (server), held equal by `graphLineAnchorCases.json` (16 cases written by `test_architecture_line_anchors.py`, `UPDATE_SHAPE_CASES=1`): each automatic line, in the order given, takes the pair of attach points with the fewest uses and then the least distance (so the facing sides while free, the nearest free pair after); ends a person…
decisions.rationale: fixed and lines with vertices are placed first and never moved, and still count as uses; lines left on the same two points get lanes 16 units apart along the normal of the canonical direction (the lower-ordered end to the other), so a line each way takes its own side. Only +, -, *, / and square roots, so both agree exactly.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20e, lines never overlap (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: Order is the order given, not the id
decisions.statement: Ids are random, so placing by id would let a new line steal a point from an older one and make existing lines jump when one is added.
decisions.rationale: Callers pass lines in creation order (the model's order on both sides), and a test pins that adding a line moves no earlier automatic line. The cost: the browser and the server must pass the same order, which they derive from the same model.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20e, lines never overlap (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: Loops get slots
decisions.statement: `selfLoop(box, slot)` / `self_loop(box, slot)`: slot 0 is the top right (unchanged), 1 the bottom right, 2 the bottom left, 3 the top left, then further out each round; the label runs outward from the curve (`align`).
decisions.rationale: `graphSelfLoopCases.json` carries the slots.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20e, lines never overlap (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: A saved drawing redraws
decisions.statement: Nothing is stored for an automatic line, so a diagram saved before this change is drawn with the new assignment on its next view (browser and exports).
decisions.rationale: Only lines that shared a point or a path move; a diagram with no such lines looks the same. Stated in the release notes.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20e, lines never overlap (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: The rule
decisions.statement: With snapping off the stored position is the drop position, rounded only to a whole canvas unit, whatever the symbol's kind; the invert key counts only while it is down at the start of the gesture.
decisions.rationale: Stated in the style guide's "Snap to grid" entry.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20f, a symbol stays where it is dropped (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: Fix in the shared canvas
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvas` takes `deleteKeyScope` (`"canvas"` by default, so other consumers are unchanged; both editors pass `"page"`).
decisions.rationale: With the page scope one capture-phase document listener hears a plain Delete or Backspace wherever the focus is, with a selection, and calls the consumer's `onDelete` once; the in-canvas handler is then skipped so the key is never counted twice. It is left alone in a text field, a select, a dialog or an open menu (the rule the Undo and Redo keys use, now written once in `utils/keyboardTargets.ts`, which `useHistoryShortcuts` also reads), for a key held with Shift, Control, Command or Alt, and on a line's vertex handle (which removes only the vertex). `historyShortcutBlocked` keeps its name and meaning.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20h, the Delete key (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A newly added symbol does not take the focus away from its name
decisions.statement: The plan said a newly added symbol should take the focus so the key reaches the canvas.
decisions.rationale: The name field holds the focus on purpose after an add at once (the person types the name), and a Delete key in a text field must edit the text, so the two cannot both hold. The key now reaches the selection from everywhere else, and **Escape in a text field of the Selection card returns the focus to the selected symbol or line** (`utils/canvasFocus.ts`, `DetailCard onKeyDown`), so the keyboard route is: type the name, Escape, Delete. Leaving the field is what stores a name, so nothing is saved earlier or later than before. Escape is left to an open dialog or menu.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20h, the Delete key (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 9: What the key does
decisions.statement: State machine editor: a state or a transition asks first (the confirmation names what goes with a state and needs its code; Cancel keeps everything), a note or a leader is removed at once and Undo restores it.
decisions.rationale: Block diagram editor: a box, note, boundary box or leader is taken off the drawing at once as **Remove from diagram** does (an undoable edit of the unsaved drawing; the element is never deleted by the key, because deleting an element is the card's **Delete element** with its typed confirmation). A selected connection has no drawing-only form to remove, so the key shows a message saying a connection is deleted from its own page, rather than doing nothing silently. One delete of a note, leader or box is one Undo step; a state or transition delete is a record delete and is not in the history (the stated exception for records created at once).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20h, the Delete key (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: Where the key is named
decisions.statement: The tooltips of the card's **Delete**, **Remove from diagram** and note-removal buttons add "Keyboard: Delete or Backspace with the item selected" (the canvas's spoken help already said so); the style guide's graph canvas entry and the two docs website editor pages state the rule.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20h, the Delete key (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: One term, in the interface and the API
decisions.statement: **Validation**, with **error** and **warning** for each result.
decisions.rationale: The model response field `findings` is `validation`; `FindingOut`, `FindingSeverity`, the checks module's `Finding` and `findings_by_diagram`, and the activation refusal's `findings` attribute became `ValidationIssueOut`, `ValidationSeverity`, `ValidationIssue`, `validation_by_diagram` and `issues`. No alias is kept (an alias is a second spelling to maintain), so this is a breaking change for a client that reads `findings` of a state machine diagram: every reader in the repository (the editor, its stories and fixtures, the Playwright spec, the backend tests, the bundle test) changed together. Searched at build: the MCP server and skill, the perf scripts, the seeds and the architecture reports do not read the field, and every remaining "finding" in `mcp-server`, `perf`, `backend/scripts` and the website is the Engagements module's own or an unrelated English use.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20i, Validation (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: One component for both editors: not needed
decisions.statement: The block diagram editor has no diagram-wide results to list: its soft guidance (suggested connection types, the domain warning) lives in the connection form and is shown there, so a second host would be invented.
decisions.rationale: `ValidationButton` is module-local (`validationIssues.ts` holds the counts and wording); it moves to the shared components when a second editor has issues to list.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20i, Validation (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A test pins the term
decisions.statement: `test_architecture_validation_term.py` fails for the old word in any Python or Markdown file of the backend module and, when the repository root is visible, in any frontend file of the module; the model response is asserted to have no old key.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 9: Phase 20i, Validation (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A list of rows, not a narrower table
decisions.statement: `ConnectionSummaryList` and `ConnectionSummaryRow` (`modules/architecture/ConnectionSummaryList.tsx`) draw each connection in the shared `ItemRow`: the code with the type and protocol on the first line, the two ends on the second, and the row's actions at its end.
decisions.rationale: The code is one unbreakable unit while the row wraps as a whole, so a narrow card shows no clipped column and no split code. The caller supplies the formatted code and the actions, so the list holds no permission or navigation logic.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 11: Phase 22a, compact connection rows (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: One component for every narrow list of connections
decisions.statement: Searched at build: the Selection card and the element page's Connections card listed the same summary in two shapes; both now use the shared list, with the element page showing each connection's own name too (`showName`).
decisions.rationale: The Outline's connection table stays a table, because the Outline tab is a wide area; the boundary box's "Realised by" list is a bullet of code and name, not this summary.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 11: Phase 22a, compact connection rows (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 11: Behaviour kept
decisions.statement: The code is still a link to the record page and Edit is still an icon action named "Edit CON-001", shown only for a connection of this project on a line that stands for several; the next phase changes what a row does when chosen.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 11: Phase 22a, compact connection rows (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A second level of selection, not a new line
decisions.statement: The page keeps `{ edgeId, connectionId }` (`DiagramEditorPage`); it is derived against the canvas selection, so it applies only while that line is selected.
decisions.rationale: `setSelection` ends it for any other selection and keeps it when the same line is selected again (the canvas does so after a save redraws it). It is not in the undo history, not in the URL (`?select=` names the line) and the generic `GraphCanvas` gains nothing. A saved edit keeps the choice; a connection moved to another pair is no longer in the selected line, so the card falls back to the line's list.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 11: Phase 22b, choosing one connection of a merged line (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The card shows the chosen connection with a way back
decisions.statement: `ChosenConnection` in `DiagramSelectionPanel`: a heading naming it by code (through `useRecordCode`) that takes the keyboard focus, so a screen reader announces the change (no live region), **Back to the N connections**, **Open**, then the same in-place fields a single-connection line shows (`ConnectionSelectionFields`, `RecordTags`); a connection of another project, or a read-only diagram, shows…
decisions.rationale: the read-only summary row instead. The line's own attach point and vertex fields stay below, with a note that they apply to all N connections, since they belong to the pair of boxes. Back returns the focus to the row that was chosen.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 11: Phase 22b, choosing one connection of a merged line (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The record page is an Open icon action
decisions.statement: In the card the code is text, not a link: `ConnectionSummaryRow` takes `onChoose`, which makes its two lines one button (`.item-row__choose`), and each row has `Open CON-001` (a real link) beside the existing `Edit CON-001`.
decisions.rationale: A line of one connection shows the Open action too. The element page's Connections card is unchanged (its code stays a link).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 11: Phase 22b, choosing one connection of a merged line (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: Meaning and scope
decisions.statement: Straight is segments through the vertices; Curved is one bowed arc between the ends that needs no vertices (through them when there are any); Spline is the curve through the vertices that the smooth switch drew.
decisions.rationale: A line's own choice overrides a diagram default, and the choice applies to connections, note leaders and state transitions in both editors.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23d, Straight, Curved or Spline (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: Named "shape", not "style"
decisions.statement: *Line style* already means solid, dashed or dotted on a connection type (`LineStyle`, `ConnectionType.line_style`, its form's **Line style** field), so a second field of that name would have made one word mean two things on the same screen and in the same API.
decisions.rationale: The stored field, the API, the types and the interface say **Line shape**.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23d, Straight, Curved or Spline (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: No alias, no nested-project fallback question
decisions.statement: `smooth` is removed from the API and the types outright, as the earlier Findings rename was: the module has no external client, and a bundle written before shapes still reads `smooth: true` as a spline (`bundle_line_shape`), so no export is lost.
decisions.rationale: The diagram default is a field of one diagram, not a project-scoped definition table, so the nested-project fallback and the organisation-defaults-a-project-can-hide rules do not apply; the module-availability, save-and-activate and field-help rules are unchanged.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23d, Straight, Curved or Spline (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: One rule
decisions.statement: `diagram_line_path.py` and `graphLinePath.ts` hold `LINE_SHAPES`, `effective_shape`, `bow_span`, `shape_spans`, `line_path` and `line_middle`, pinned by `graphLinePathCases.json` (16 cases, including both bow directions, the cap, a zero-length line and fractional numbers); only `+ - * /` and one square root are used so both agree to the last digit.
decisions.rationale: Curved with no vertices is one cubic span with its control points at a third and two thirds of the chord, moved left of the direction of travel by a quarter of the length (at most 60 units), so it leaves the chord by three quarters of that at its middle. With vertices Curved is the Spline, as the request says. The label of an unrouted Curved line and its segment handle sit on the arc. The hop rule takes the shape and flattens the arc like any span (two new shared cases); a zero-length line is straight.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23d, Straight, Curved or Spline (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: The canvas stays generic
decisions.statement: `GraphCanvasEdge.lineShape` and `GraphCanvasLeader.lineShape` are the shape drawn; the editor resolves a line's own shape against its diagram's default (`effectiveShape`) before it reaches the canvas, so the canvas holds no default and no diagram concept.
decisions.rationale: A Curved line is drawn by the routed edge even on a read-only canvas.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23d, Straight, Curved or Spline (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: One control
decisions.statement: `LineShapeSelect` (a `LabeledSelect` over a label map keyed by the shape type, the help describing every option one per line) is the per-line **Line shape** field, which leads with **Diagram default (Straight)**, and the diagram's **Default line shape** in both settings gears beside **Line hops**; the stored default changes through the same version-checked edit as Line hops.
decisions.rationale: The Smooth curve switch and its help are removed. The per-line field sits in `LineVertexFields` so connections, transitions and leaders share it. The gear's accessible name gains ", line shape X" only when the default is not Straight, so existing names and tests are unchanged.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23d, Straight, Curved or Spline (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: Exports, bundles and tables
decisions.statement: The server SVG and PNG draw all three shapes with the same resolution; Mermaid leaves shapes out, as it does vertices.
decisions.rationale: The project bundle carries the diagram's default and each line's own shape (a transition's, an anchor's, a leader's); an unknown value reads as none and a diagram's missing or unknown default as straight. The template classification is unchanged (the keys are the same). The diagram record table gains a **Line shape** column (it imports); the state machine table has no column for line hops either. The performance generator and probe populate the column (profiles version 14); the demo seed gives the GPS link a Curved shape and a leader and a transition a Spline.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23d, Straight, Curved or Spline (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The scope is the title's tooltip
decisions.statement: The shared `Tooltip` wraps the title in `DiagramEditorPage`: "Inside" with the element's code (through the record-code rule) and name, or "System context" with its help text, on one hover or focus.
decisions.rationale: The header's subtitle is the purpose alone, and is absent for a diagram with none.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23e, scope in the title and a diagram switcher (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: A chevron switches diagram
decisions.statement: `DiagramSwitcher` (`modules/architecture`) passes the shared `EntitySwitcher` a loader of the project's live diagrams of the kind and links each to its editor, labelled by code and name.
decisions.rationale: Both editors have it; a block diagram lists block diagrams and a state machine diagram lists state machine diagrams. No core file changed.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23e, scope in the title and a diagram switcher (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: One field, one panel
decisions.statement: `SymbolPicker` is a button showing the chosen drawing and name.
decisions.rationale: It opens `SymbolPickerPanel`: **Search** first (it takes the focus through the popover's own focus management and is hidden in the Upload view), then the symbols, then the view buttons **List**, **Gallery** and **Upload**.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23f, the symbol picker's views are inside it (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A route belongs to a connection once it is set
decisions.statement: A connection's route is a row of the existing `architecture_diagram_anchors` table with a nullable `connection_id` (deleting the connection deletes the row), not a new table: it has the same fields, the same save, comparison, bundle and template handling, and a second table would have meant a second copy of each.
decisions.rationale: The pair's uniqueness became a partial unique index for pair rows and a second one holds one route per connection per diagram. A pair row must still set an end or a vertex; a connection's route may set nothing, which is a line of its own with automatic ends. This supersedes Y2's "the anchors belong to the pair" for a routed connection only.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23b, a route per connection (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: Which edits are per connection
decisions.statement: `routedConnectionOf` (`diagramEditorModel.ts`) says so in one place for the canvas drag, the card's fields and the vertex list: the line drawn for one connection on its own route; else the connection chosen in a merged line's card; else the only connection of a line that shares its two boxes with another line (Connection detail on, two connections between one pair: before this a drag moved both…
decisions.rationale: lines onto each other); else the pair. A first edit starts from the route the line has now, so nothing jumps. The connection stays selected: the page reuses the "just added connection" selection, which follows the connection to its new line and ends at any other selection.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23b, a route per connection (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A routed connection is its own line in the resolver
decisions.statement: `resolve(..., routed={connection: (box, box)})` takes a connection that stands alone between exactly those two boxes out of the merge, and reports `routable` (the connections behind a line that can be routed) and `own_route`.
decisions.rationale: A route whose boxes the connection no longer joins (moved to other elements, or rolled up to another pair) is ignored and the connection merges as before; the row stays and applies again if the boxes match again. A bridged chain and a line to a boundary box are never routable (several connections, or no element pair, lie behind them). `ViewEdge` carries `routable_connection_ids` and `route_connection_id`; the Python resolver, the browser port, and the shared cases (`diagramResolverCases.json`, five new scenarios) keep the two equal. The merged line's id (`source-target-first connection`) changes when its first connection is routed; the page follows the connection, not the id.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23b, a route per connection (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: Use the shared route
decisions.statement: An own route that sets nothing is kept (it is the way to say "a line of its own, automatic"), so giving a route up is an explicit action: **Use the shared route** (an icon action in the Route heading, with a tooltip) removes the row and the connection joins its pair's line again.
decisions.rationale: Undo and redo cover both.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23b, a route per connection (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 12: Bundles and templates
decisions.statement: The project bundle writes a connection's route with `connection_code` in the diagram's `anchors`, and the import maps it to a connection of the same import only; an unknown code, a repeated connection or a bad point is dropped with a warning like any other anchor.
decisions.rationale: It is part of the diagram's template record, so a template copies it. The export reads no extra rows. The performance generator does not create connection routes (a nullable column; a pair's routes are generated and the export reads both kinds in the same statement).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 12: Phase 23b, a route per connection (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The cause was the rule, not the data
decisions.statement: A Curved line with no vertices was one cubic bowed to the left of its stored direction by a quarter of its length (at most 60 units), whatever the boxes looked like, so it bowed even where straight was right and to whichever side the connection happened to be stored.
decisions.rationale: The fixed bow (`bow_span`, `bowSpan`, `BOW_RATIO`, `BOW_LIMIT`) is removed.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24a, Curved leaves a box outward (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A Curved line leaves and arrives along an outward direction
decisions.statement: At each end the tangent is the way from the box's centre through the attach point (a side's normal).
decisions.rationale: The two control points lie that direction from each end by 0.4 of the chord, kept between 24 and 120 units (`HANDLE_RATIO`, `HANDLE_MIN`, `HANDLE_MAX`), so boxes facing each other in line give a straight line (the control points lie on the chord), offset boxes give a gentle S and a line that must turn back gets a rounded bend with room to turn. A zero-length line, or one with no directions at all, stays straight. An end with no direction (a leader's free end or an end on a line's middle) arrives along the chord, so only the known end bends the line.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24a, Curved leaves a box outward (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A corner takes the least-bent of three candidates
decisions.statement: For a corner the candidates are the centre-to-corner diagonal and the two side normals it lies on; the one with the smallest angle to the straight line toward the line's next point (the nearest vertex, else the other end's attach point) is used, a tie going to the diagonal and then the vertical side.
decisions.rationale: Outward direction alone would have made every corner leave at 45 degrees, itself a source of needless bending. The cost is that two lines leaving one corner leave the same way, which is intended.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24a, Curved leaves a box outward (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: With vertices, Curved passes through them as Spline does and its end tangents are outward
decisions.statement: Only the first and last spans change: they take the outward direction with handles one third of the span's length, so the curve does not overshoot a nearby vertex.
decisions.rationale: Spline is unchanged (Catmull-Rom with free ends), so the two shapes now differ both with and without vertices.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24a, Curved leaves a box outward (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: One function chooses the direction in both languages
decisions.statement: `outward_direction` and `line_directions` (`diagram_points.py`) and `outwardDirection` and `lineDirections` (`graphAttachPoints.ts`) are pinned by `graphAttachPointCases.json` (every case now carries the directions; corners in each octant, a wide box, a corner met by its own target, a vertex deciding the direction).
decisions.rationale: `linePath`, `lineMiddle`, `segmentMiddles`, `shapeSpans` and the hop rule (`HopLine.directions`) take the directions as a `LineDirections` (`line_path(..., directions)` on the server); `GraphCanvasView` computes them where it builds each routed edge (`edgeDirections`) and the server SVGs where they build each run (`_edge_runs`, `_transition_entries`, `_leader_run`, which now returns the directions as a fourth element), only for a line drawn Curved. The generic canvas gained no prop: the directions come from the boxes it already holds.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24a, Curved leaves a box outward (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 13: Nothing stored changes
decisions.statement: Existing diagrams keep their `line_shape` values and vertices.
decisions.rationale: A Curved line's label, comment pin and segment handle sit on the curve's middle (`t = 1/2`), as before. No bundle, template, probe or seed change.
