decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24a, Curved leaves a box outward (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A domain is a vocabulary row, not an enum value
decisions.statement: `architecture_domains` is the module's fourth vocabulary (`OwnedNamedMixin`: a project or the organisation owns a row, a name unique within the owner, a sort order).
decisions.rationale: It has an organisation list and a project list, a project hides an organisation default through `ProjectDefinitionSuppression` (kind `architecture_domain`) and restores it, and a child project with no domain configuration of its own shows the nearest ancestor's, else the organisation's; the first change copies the inherited rows (`materialize_inherited`). This is the explicit nested-projects decision the project rules ask for. A domain that a type is in or a toggle rule names is never deleted (409); hiding stops new use only, so a type already in a hidden domain keeps it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24b, domains are a vocabulary (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A type is in zero or more domains; none means every domain
decisions.statement: Link tables `architecture_element_type_domains` and `architecture_connection_type_domains` (the pattern of the suggestions and parents).
decisions.rationale: `any` stops being a value: the form says "Any domain" for none. A link is validated to a domain in the owner's tier or one the project lists; one a row already has is kept after a hide.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24b, domains are a vocabulary (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 13: One fit rule
decisions.statement: Something fits an end when either side has no domain or the two share one (`domainsFit` in `connectionGuidance.ts`; the server applies the same reading to toggle rules).
decisions.rationale: It drives the connection picker's soft filter and warning (the warning now names the domains: "REST API is in Software, but the source element (Board) is in Hardware"), the Add existing elements Domain filter (a type in none matches every filter), and **Add to diagram**, which lists a type under each of its domains in the domains' order and a type in none under "New element" (an entry's key includes its domain, so a type listed twice has two keys). A toggle rule's `domains` became `domain_ids`; a rule matches a type with any listed domain, and a type in none matches no domain rule (as `any` matched none before).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24b, domains are a vocabulary (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: Existing data is converted in migration 0199
decisions.statement: An organisation with a type in `software` or `hardware` (its own or in one of its projects) or a toggle rule naming one gets the Software and Hardware rows it uses; each such type is linked; a rule's `domains` values become `domain_ids`; `any` becomes no link; the `domain` column is dropped.
decisions.rationale: Nothing is created for an organisation that used neither, and a migration seeds no defaults; a fresh organisation is seeded with Software and Hardware, and its seeded connection types are linked to them (the neutral element types and Ethernet and Network are in none). The downgrade writes back the first linked domain named Software or Hardware (else `any`) and the matching rule values; a custom domain is lost, as stated in the migration. Migration 0172's backfill now adds the `domain` column when it is missing, because a database built from the current models no longer has it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24b, domains are a vocabulary (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A domain has no colour
decisions.statement: The seeded colours still come from the seed key of the domain a seeded type was made for; a type keeps its own colour pair.
decisions.rationale: Taking a type's default colour from "its" domain is ambiguous with several domains and the type's own colour already covers it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24b, domains are a vocabulary (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: Bundles carry domains by name
decisions.statement: The project and organisation bundles gain `architecture_domains`, `architecture_project_domains` and `architecture_hidden_domains` (template configuration, so a project from a template copies the list and the hidden defaults) and each type row carries `domain_names`; a toggle rule carries `domain_names`.
decisions.rationale: A bundle written before this (`domain: "software"`, a rule's `domains`) still reads as the one domain of that name, `any` as none. An import links by name: a project's own rows first, then the organisation's (a default the project hides still names the domain a type was in), and creates a missing name in the owner's tier with a warning so the type keeps its meaning.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24b, domains are a vocabulary (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A project that copies its domains keeps types and rules consistent
decisions.statement: Link and rule ids name rows, so when a child project first changes its domains (or its types) the inherited domains are copied and every link of the project's own types and every toggle rule of its diagrams that named an ancestor's domain is moved to the project's domain of the same name (`DomainVocabulary.heal_links`); the inherited type vocabularies are copied at the same moment so no type of…
decisions.rationale: the project points at the ancestor's domain. Hidden organisation defaults stay valid.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24b, domains are a vocabulary (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The Domains section is a settings page of its own, not inside the type panels
decisions.statement: The plan said "a Domains section in the element types and connection types panels' settings".
decisions.rationale: The two panels share one `ArchitectureTypesPanel`, so the domains are a third `kind` of it (rename, reorder, add, delete or hide, **Add organisation defaults**) listed as **Domains** beside Element Types, Connection Types and Symbols, in the project and the organisation settings. A type's form takes its domains from a multi-select (`TreeSelectField`, "Any domain" when none).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24b, domains are a vocabulary (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A setting of the diagram, off by default
decisions.statement: `show_connection_names` on `architecture_diagrams` (migration 0200, `NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, so no stored diagram changes on upgrade).
decisions.rationale: It is stored, not a per-browser preference, because the exports must draw what the screen draws; it is changed through the diagram's own update (`DiagramUpdate.show_connection_names`) with the version lock and the existing "updated" audit event (field names only), and the create payload also takes it. It is set from the settings gear beside Connection detail, not from the create and edit forms (the same deliberate departure from "create and edit share one field group" recorded for Line hops). It is independent of Connection detail. Block diagram only: a state machine diagram has no connections.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24c, connection names beside a line (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 13: What is drawn
decisions.statement: One named connection draws its name; with Connection detail also on, the type and protocol follow on a second line.
decisions.rationale: A connection with no name adds nothing (the code is not a name). A line that merges several connections (parallel connections while detail is off, a rolled-up or bridged line) draws up to three names, one per line in code order, then "+N more" and, with detail off, its count ("×5") so a merged line keeps the count it showed before. A rolled-up or bridged line follows the same rule over the connections behind it, as the viewer may read them.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24c, connection names beside a line (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: Two presentation limits the plan did not state
decisions.statement: A name is one line of text, so its whitespace and line breaks are collapsed; a name longer than 60 characters is cut with an ellipsis in the label (the full name stays in the Selection card, the Outline and the lists).
decisions.rationale: The SVG does not wrap a label line (the existing type and protocol text is not wrapped either), so without a limit one 200-character name would run far across the drawing. The canvas still wraps a long line. Code order is the number inside the code (`CON-9` before `CON-10`), compared by length then text on both sides.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24c, connection names beside a line (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: One rule, two implementations, pinned by cases
decisions.statement: `diagram_edge_label.edge_label` (server: the view's label, so the SVG, PNG and Mermaid exports and the API) and `edgeLabelText` in `diagramLines.ts` (the browser's port, so the editor shows a line's label before it is saved) give the same text for `diagramLabelCases.json`, which `test_architecture_diagram_edge_label.py` regenerates with `UPDATE_SHAPE_CASES=1` and a story runs through the port.
decisions.rationale:
The canvas draws a label with a line break as its existing multi-line line label; the server SVG writes one `` per line (the last line's baseline where the single line sat, earlier lines above, each XML-escaped); Mermaid joins the lines with `
` after escaping each (a name cannot end the label or add markup).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24c, connection names beside a line (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The setting is not per line
decisions.statement: A person wants every line named or none (the same reasoning as Show notes on elements); a line's route and shape are already per line.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24c, connection names beside a line (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: Where the protocol is set today
decisions.statement: A connection's Protocol is free text on the connection itself (up to 200 characters): the connection form, the Selection card of a line and the connection's page; the Connections list has a Protocol column.
decisions.rationale: A line draws it only while the diagram's Connection detail is on and, before this change, only on a line of one connection. A connection added at once from the canvas or the API had none unless typed, which is why a diagram of such links showed no protocol.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24d, a connection type's Default protocol (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A column of the vocabulary row
decisions.statement: `default_protocol` on `architecture_connection_types` (migration 0201, `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, up to 200 characters, trimmed on save; an empty string clears it).
decisions.rationale: It is a column of the vocabulary row, so it takes the two tiers, hiding, the nested fallback and the copy of an inherited configuration with no new mechanism (`copied_columns` reads the table's columns), and travels in the project and organisation bundles and the template copy with the type (an older bundle without the key imports as empty). The nested-projects check: no new table, so nothing to resolve; the nested test pins that a child inherits and copies the default.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24d, a connection type's Default protocol (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: It pre-fills; it is not a fallback
decisions.statement: The create and edit dialogs and the Selection card fill Protocol from the chosen type.
decisions.rationale: A type change replaces the Protocol only while it is empty or still equals the previous type's default (`protocolAfterTypeChange`), so a typed protocol is never overwritten; a new connection's dialog follows the type's default until the person sets the protocol or the type. A connection added at once from the canvas takes the default of the type it is created with. The value is stored on the connection, so lists, exports and diagrams read the connection and nothing else; changing a default later leaves existing connections alone (no backfill, tested).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24d, a connection type's Default protocol (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The server applies it when the client sends no protocol
decisions.statement: `ConnectionCreate.protocol` is optional: left out, the create takes the type's default; an explicit empty string means none (tested), so the MCP tools and API clients behave like the form without each reading the type.
decisions.rationale: An update never applies a default (tested). The list CSV import sends the cell's value, so a blank cell stays blank and the exported CSV is still the import file; a bundle import copies the stored value and never applies a default.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24d, a connection type's Default protocol (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A merged line shows the shared protocol
decisions.statement: With Connection detail on, `Type ×N` is followed by ` · protocol` when every connection of the line has the same non-empty protocol (`2 connections · protocol` when the types differ); different or empty protocols add nothing.
decisions.rationale: The rule is the one label rule of the previous phase (`diagram_edge_label.detail_text` and its port `edgeLabelText`, `diagramLabelCases.json` regenerated with four new cases), so the canvas, the SVG, PNG and Mermaid exports agree. A merged line with detail off keeps its count only.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24d, a connection type's Default protocol (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The panel takes the width it is given
decisions.statement: Both minimums removed (`min-width: 0`), the view buttons wrap.
decisions.rationale: **It opens where it does not cover its field (E3):** a `matchAnchor` popover opens below while at least 240px of room is there (`MATCH_ANCHOR_USABLE_ROOM_PX`) and scrolls inside, instead of flipping above whenever above is roomier; with less room it takes the roomier side as before.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24e, the Selection card's content fits the card (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The same fault in the other matchAnchor popover
decisions.statement: `MultiSelectDropdown`'s option label, a flex item that could not shrink, ran out of the bubble for a long unbreakable label (505px in a 278px bubble); fixed with `min-width: 0` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`.
decisions.rationale: There are only these two `matchAnchor` users. A shared check, `popoverFitViolations` (`testing/popoverFit.ts`), and `expectContainerFits` (`testing/containerFits.ts`) assert that nothing runs out of its container, used by the picker, dropdown and Selection card stories.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24e, the Selection card's content fits the card (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: System Architecture review round 13: The ports' cause
decisions.statement: `PortList` uses the shared `DefinitionList` grid with a `max-content` column for the direction and type selects, so the row was 475px wide whatever the card (it overflowed at every width tested, including a 454px card).
decisions.rationale: **A control group in a card wraps (E6):** a list with `renderExtra` measures its own container (a container query, because the card is narrow in a wide window) and, under 34rem, becomes one flowing row per item with the extra controls on the line below; the extra column's selects may shrink. This is in the shared `DefinitionList`, so any list using `renderExtra` gets it and none is special-cased (the add row is now wrapped in a `definition-grid__row` like the others). The audit of the card at 320, 390, 520 and 1280 pixels for an element, a line, a note and a leader (and in the state machine editor a state and a transition) found no other overflow.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24e, the Selection card's content fits the card (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: The Selection card scrolls inside itself
decisions.statement: `DetailCard` takes `maxHeight`; both editors pass the drawing's height (`canvasHeight`).
decisions.rationale: The heading stays, the content scrolls in a focusable group named "Selection content" (a `group`, not a `region`, so the many specs that find the card by the region name "Selection" keep matching one element), `overscroll-behavior: contain` keeps the page still at the ends, and the `SelectionActions` row (class `selection-actions`) is sticky at the top of the scrolling content. A short card keeps its natural height (the cap is `max-height`, not a height). A focused field is scrolled into view by the browser inside the card.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24e, the Selection card's content fits the card (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: Title and Save on the heading line
decisions.statement: The User asked for the Selection card to be titled with the selected item and to carry its Save button beside the title, as an edit dialog's header does, so Save is easier to reach.
decisions.rationale: `DetailCard` takes `title` (the visible heading; the card stays named "Selection" for assistive technology and for every test that finds it by that name) and exposes its heading line as a mount point (`detailCardSlots`); `CardHeaderAction` draws its children there through a portal and in place outside a card; `SelectionSaveButton` is the one Save of the element, connection, state and transition cards (primary, disabled until a field changes, accessible name unchanged: "Save element" and so on). The draft and its commit stay with the fields (`useSelectionDraft`); leaving the fields still stores, so pressing Save in the header after typing stores once. The first line of each card that repeated the item (the bold code and name, `A → B`, `Leader 1`) is removed, its muted extra (the type, "Loop") kept; `DiagramLeaderEditor` no longer takes `index`. A note's and a leader's changes are saved with the drawing by the toolbar's Save, so they have no Save on the card. A line is titled by its connection (one connection, or the chosen one of a merged line) or by its two ends.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) review round 13: Phase 24e, the Selection card's content fits the card (2026-11-17)

decisions.title: A tool is a proxy to the screen's own endpoint
decisions.statement: `build_mcp_tool_manifest` already checks each path and method against the real routes, so the Architect role, the module and sub-component gates, the visibility resolver (a shared element is read through collection grants, a foreign end is a locked placeholder), the version lock and the audit event all apply unchanged.
decisions.rationale: No tool reaches a record by a path the route does not.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 14: MCP tools and agent skill (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Tools declared
decisions.statement: Reads: element and connection types, elements (with filters), shared elements, connections, block diagrams (record and resolved view), state machine diagrams (record, the whole model in one call, Mermaid), states.
decisions.rationale: Changes: elements and ports; connections including the realisation list; state machine diagrams with their states and transitions (create, edit, status, archive, restore, delete). Status changes use the server's own move map; there is no approval gate in this module, so none of the tools is an approval action.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 14: MCP tools and agent skill (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: Block diagrams are read only
decisions.statement: A block diagram is a drawing (placements, routes, notes, anchors); an agent that wrote a layout would be guessing coordinates, and the structure it needs is in the elements and connections.
decisions.rationale: `get_diagram_view` returns what the diagram shows. A state machine diagram is structure, so it is editable. Recorded as a choice, not a restriction for safety: a layout tool can be added without a core change.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 14: MCP tools and agent skill (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: Links use the core tools
decisions.statement: Allocation, constraint, risk and decision links are ordinary artefact links, created with `create_artefact_link`; declaring a second way would give two routes through the link rules.
decisions.rationale: Realisation between connections has its own endpoint and its own tool.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 14: MCP tools and agent skill (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: Deletion is declared, with archive named as the reversible choice
decisions.statement: A delete of an element, connection, port, state, transition or diagram is offered because the screen offers it; the route's own refusals (children, connections, a stale version) stand, and each description and the guidance say to archive when the record may be needed again.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 14: MCP tools and agent skill (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Left to people
decisions.statement: Collections and grants (they widen who can read an element), the type, domain and symbol vocabularies (shared with the organisation's defaults, and symbols are file uploads, which the declarative proxy cannot send), folders, and the JSON import (it creates records in bulk and a type row).
decisions.rationale: Each is a reasoned omission, not an oversight.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 14: MCP tools and agent skill (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: Why the missing wheels mattered
decisions.statement: Without a wheel pip compiles the package on every image and CI build; the slim image has no compiler or headers, so the build fails (`psycopg2-binary`, `pydantic-core`), and adding a toolchain would slow every build and enlarge the image.
decisions.rationale: Newer releases of the three packages ship 3.15 wheels, so upgrading them is the fix.
decisions.section: Dependency and image updates from the Dependabot pull requests (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: Pre-commit hook selects the pinned Node
decisions.statement: With `.nvmrc` on 26, a commit from a shell or editor still on Node 24 was refused with "active Node is v24, but .nvmrc pins Node 26".
decisions.rationale: `.githooks/pre-commit` now runs `nvm use` for the pinned major when nvm is installed and only refuses if that does not give the pinned major, so the lockfile check still runs under the Node CI uses and is not skipped.
decisions.section: Dependency and image updates from the Dependabot pull requests (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: System Architecture: Demo seed re-run
decisions.statement: The User asked for the demonstration organisation to be seeded again because testing had edited it and the website screenshots would show those edits (and again after the layout change below).
decisions.rationale: The organisation "Solstice Robotics" was deleted through the organisation deletion route and `seed_demo_data.py` run again in the test stack; nothing else was removed. The architecture block of that seed already covers every feature built since (folders, display notes, notes with several leaders, bend points, curved lines, line hops, comments, domains, default protocols, a state machine, allocation, a baseline and a shared organisation element).
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 16: seeds, completeness and close-out (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: System Architecture: E2E seed
decisions.statement: One fixed, read-only fixture is added for Gamma: the project "Eta-1 Flight System Architecture" holding a software service, a hardware board (two organisation element types, each in its own domain), one connection, a diagram placing both and a three-state machine, browsed by `seeded-architecture.spec.ts`.
decisions.rationale: It is read-only because every other architecture spec builds its own disposable organisation (a spec that edits a named fixture is not repeatable). System Architecture is enabled for Gamma only. The function was checked against a throwaway organisation, and the fixture was added to the live Gamma organisation by the same function so the new spec ran against it.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 16: seeds, completeness and close-out (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: Plans that reuse the module's parts
decisions.statement: Module 6 now says baseline storage is built and only a provider is left to write.
decisions.rationale: Module 16 (workflow capture) drew its editor directly on React Flow and said so in its boundary rule; that conflicts with the enforced rule that only `GraphCanvasView.tsx` imports the library, so its boundary, decision D2 and phase 5 now name the shared `GraphCanvas`. Module 17 (glossary) planned to add React Flow as a first dependency behind a new wrapper; it now draws through the existing canvas and adds no package. Neither plan's design otherwise changes.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 16: seeds, completeness and close-out (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: Demo diagrams laid out for reading
decisions.statement: The seeded state machine had states 60 units apart with labels about 140 wide, so labels sat over each other and over lines, and the final state sat where three lines crossed.
decisions.rationale: States now sit 220 or more apart with every line running between facing sides (explicit attach points, two vertices for the return from the battery choice), the final and choice labels sit below their symbols, and the notes sit in free space. The block diagram follows the same rule (sensors in a column, the flight controller and radio in a row, the interface boundary box at the end of the radio's upload, the interrupt line routed below both boxes, comment markers off the boxes); the ground station is no longer placed on it, because the boundary box stands for it. The organisation was seeded again to confirm the seed itself gives these drawings.
decisions.section: Module 18 (System Architecture) Phase 16: seeds, completeness and close-out (2026-11-18)

decisions.title: Image scan
decisions.statement: Trivy failed `scan-backend`, `scan-backup` and `scan-converter` on five HIGH findings (`msgpack` 1.1.2, `setuptools` 70.3.0, `urllib3` 2.7.0).
decisions.rationale: All were copies vendored inside the `python:3.15-slim` base image's own pip, not application dependencies, so no requirements file could fix them. Upgrading pip (26.2.2 to 26.3) cleared `msgpack` and `urllib3` but not the vendored `setuptools`, and 26.3 is the newest release. The fix is to ship no pip in the backend (and so backup) and converter images: the backend removes it after installing the requirements, the converter removes it as nothing there installs packages, and the profile stage (developer-only, never published) restores it with `python -m ensurepip`. Trade-off: a derived image that `pip install`s a module package (the entry-point route in `docs/modules.md`) runs `python -m ensurepip` first; `docs/modules.md` says so. Verified by building the images and re-running the pinned Trivy gate: all three exit 0.
decisions.section: First pull-request CI run of the architecture module: image scan, lint and Storybook failures

decisions.title: Steps the failed backend job skipped
decisions.statement: The job stopped at `ruff`, so the converter, backup-image, promtool, mypy and perf-anonymisation steps never ran.
decisions.rationale: Run locally, the converter tests, promtool, mypy and the anonymisation check passed (the one anonymisation finding was an untracked, git-ignored `.DS_Store`). The backup-image tests found two failures that predate this change: `docs/schemas/backup-manifest.schema.json` was out of date with the pinned pydantic (it now emits `ComponentKind` and `propertyNames`), so it was regenerated with `dr_stats.py --manifest-schema`; and the flamegraph path shortening in `perf/run_profile.py` named Python 3.15 while its test used 3.12, so it now matches any 3.x minor version and a base-image bump needs no edit. All 183 tests in those two files pass in the backup image.
decisions.section: First pull-request CI run of the architecture module: image scan, lint and Storybook failures

decisions.title: Second CI run, Storybook
decisions.statement: `SelectionCardFit`'s "The Title Names The Selection And Save Sits Beside It" failed again on CI after the first fix (the card still showed the element 1 s after Enter on the line) while passing locally, including under CPU load with coverage.
decisions.rationale: The cause is not proven; the working hypothesis is that after an edit in the card the line does not take the focus, so Enter does not reach it. `selectLine` now looks the line up and focuses it afresh on each attempt, asserts that it took the focus and that the card shows it, and retries for up to 5 s, so a recurrence names the step that failed. `ReportLayoutDesigner`'s "Blocks With Problems Cannot Be Saved And Show Them In The Inspector" (Run preview button not found after choosing the Preview tab) failed once on CI in a file this branch does not change, and passes locally on every run; it is **not** changed, and is to be investigated if it recurs.
decisions.section: First pull-request CI run of the architecture module: image scan, lint and Storybook failures

decisions.title: Third CI run, Storybook
decisions.statement: `RunningBandEditor`'s "Bold And Italic Wrap The Selection" failed on CI with `***Draft*** copy` for `**Draft** *copy*`.
decisions.rationale: After a Bold or Italic press, `useTextSelections` puts the selection back on the marked word on the next animation frame; the story chose the next words immediately, and on a slower runner that frame ran afterwards and replaced the choice, so Italic wrapped the word that was already bold. A person cannot act within one frame, so the story now waits for the restored selection before choosing the next words. No product code changed.
decisions.section: First pull-request CI run of the architecture module: image scan, lint and Storybook failures

decisions.title: CodeQL alert on the pull request: py/overly-large-range in diagram_svg.py
decisions.statement: The only open code-scanning alert (the review comment on the pull request; there were no open Dependabot alerts) flagged the character class that removes characters XML 1.0 cannot carry from a person's text in the server SVG.
decisions.rationale: The class was correct in effect, but it held a range of control characters and raw U+FFFE and U+FFFF bytes in the source. It is now a table of code points (`_XML_FORBIDDEN`) applied with `str.translate`, which removes exactly the same characters, reads as what it is and needs no suppression. `test_architecture_diagram_svg_text.py` pins every removed code point, the characters that must survive and the escaping; the 24 other architecture test files that draw an SVG still pass (341 tests). The Mermaid and state-machine exporters keep their own, differently shaped patterns, which the scan did not flag.
decisions.section: First pull-request CI run of the architecture module: image scan, lint and Storybook failures

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Who writes it
decisions.statement: `ProtectedRoutes` writes the requested address when this tab has had no signed-in person (a followed link, or a stored token that is no longer valid at load); `AuthProvider`'s unauthorised handler writes the current address when a session ends; `ForcedPasswordChangePage` writes it before the change ends the session.
decisions.rationale: A deliberate sign-out (`logout`) clears it and writes nothing, so the next person to sign in on a shared tab is not taken to the previous person's page.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 1: return to the page after signing in (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Stage notifications open Delivery status
decisions.statement: Delivery status gains a settings (gear) link to project administration, Stages and phases, shown only to a person who may change them Moving a stage and setting its dates are already on that page.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 2: notification targets, review (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Access changes open the affected organisation, project or standard
decisions.statement: Access changes open the affected organisation, project or standard.
decisions.rationale: which needs the organisation or standard id as the notification's entity. A revoke may leave the person unable to open the project; the detail page then states that access was removed , so the click never ends on an empty error.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 2: notification targets, review (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: A message with no page of its own opens the notification detail
decisions.statement: Compliance assignments, target dates, project reviews and a new standard version open the project's Compliance page ; standard-level reviews and standard access grants open the Standard
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 2: notification targets, review (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: One declared target kind per type, resolved in the browser
decisions.statement: A stored notification that lacks newer data falls back to the detail page; module kinds are declared on the module's registration, never in a core file.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 2: notification targets, review (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: One address for every surface
decisions.statement: The bell, the notification list, the instant email and each item of the daily digest open `/notifications/:id` (`NotificationOpenPage`).
decisions.rationale: The page loads the notification, marks it read and navigates (replacing itself in the history, so Back returns to where the person was) to the page `resolveNotificationTarget` names, or shows the full message. The bell and list previously resolved the page themselves; they now share the page, so a notification cannot open different pages depending on where it was clicked. The cost is one request on click. The digest's footer link to the list is unchanged; each item gains its own link.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 3: notification targets, fixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Target kinds are an ordered list per type, chosen by data
decisions.statement: The register gave one kind per row, but `permission_granted` and the review types have several cases (project, organisation, standard) that only the notification's data tells apart, so a type declares an ordered list and the first kind whose data the notification carries wins.
decisions.rationale: A notification stored before its data existed matches no kind and shows its message, never a wrong page. Core's table is `services/notification_targets.py`; the API lists `target_kinds` on every notification, so the frontend holds no second type-to-kind table.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 3: notification targets, fixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Module boundary
decisions.statement: Compliance's 14 types are members of core's enum, so Compliance declares their kinds (`ModuleDefinition.notification_targets`, placed before core's for a type both declare, which is how a standard grant opens the standard) and the two kinds only it can open (`notification_target_kinds`, resolved by `TierAModuleDefinition.notificationTargets`).
decisions.rationale: Risk's types carry `target_kinds`. No core file names a module's page, and no per-module value was added to a core enum or map.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 3: notification targets, fixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Subject availability
decisions.statement: `GET /notifications/{id}` returns `subject_available`: false when the notification names a project the person cannot open (`link_nesting.can_open_project`, which applies a token's project scope) or an organisation they no longer belong to.
decisions.rationale: The detail page then states that access to the page has ended, so a revoked-access notification never ends on an error. A record that was deleted is not detected (no generic existence check across types); the record page answers not-found. Another person's notification, and one a scoped credential may not reach, answers 404.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 3: notification targets, fixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Data added at creation
decisions.statement: Organisation-level grants and accepted invitations carry `entity_type="organization"` and the organisation id (a grant on a project keeps its project id and no entity, so the project is opened); a grant on a standard carries `compliance_standard` and the standard id; a standard-level compliance review carries the standard instead of the review (a project-level review keeps `compliance_review`).
decisions.rationale: Stored rows without the data fall back to the message.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 3: notification targets, fixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Delivery status gear link
decisions.statement: A settings icon links to project administration, Stage and phase settings, shown when the person may lock stages (`can_lock`, the permission the page already uses to show manager controls).
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 3: notification targets, fixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Incidental fix
decisions.statement: `org-policies.spec.ts` waited for the "Published policies" menu, which a page with one policy does not draw (a menu of one has nothing to switch between), so it failed whenever its policy was the only one; it now uses the menu only when present.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 3: notification targets, fixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: One policy file, three outcomes
decisions.statement: Permissive and file-level copyleft (MPL, EPL) pass, the latter flagged for its notice; library copyleft (LGPL) passes only for a package named in the policy with a reason (`svglib`, `psycopg2-binary`, both used unmodified and replaceable); GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL, Elastic and unknown fail.
decisions.rationale: `GPL WITH exception` still fails for a dependency, because an exception does not remove the copyleft that would reach the product. An operating-system package may be GPL or AGPL only as a separate program or build tool (Ghostscript, poppler and the URW fonts in the converter container, GCC and GnuPG as build tools), with its reason in the policy.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 4: licence audit and dependency licence guard (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Evidence for unclear metadata
decisions.statement: Licence is read from the declared SPDX expression, then a short licence field, then a single classifier; anything else is `UNKNOWN` and fails until a named override records its evidence.
decisions.rationale: Fourteen overrides exist, each checked against the packaged licence file. `resvg_py` is MIT (its packaged `LICENSE`), which closes the plan's "verify upstream" item.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 4: licence audit and dependency licence guard (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Python is resolved in a throwaway environment, and the guard gates licences, never versions
decisions.statement: Transitive Python versions float between image builds, so a drift check on them would turn CI red when an upstream releases.
decisions.rationale: The offline check compares the committed inventory with the lockfiles exactly (npm) and with the pinned direct requirements (Python); `--live`, run in CI, installs each requirements file afresh and fails if anything that resolves now has a disallowed licence. A new but allowed transitive package is printed as a reminder to regenerate.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 4: licence audit and dependency licence guard (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Output location
decisions.statement: Under `frontend/public/licences/`, because the Licences page of the next phase must read it as a static asset on first open and the front-end image build context is `frontend/`.
decisions.rationale: The files are sorted and carry no timestamps; licence texts are stored once by hash.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 4: licence audit and dependency licence guard (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Limits stated, not hidden
decisions.statement: 106 packages have no licence text: platform-specific optional builds of the documentation site's tools that are not installed on the generating machine, plus two Python packages whose distributions ship no licence file; their SPDX identifier is recorded and the page can show the standard text.
decisions.rationale: The base images' own operating-system packages are not enumerated; each image carries its copyright files.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 4: licence audit and dependency licence guard (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Separate from the policy model
decisions.statement: The group reads the static files phase 4 generates (`/licences/third-party-notices.json`, and `third-party-texts.json` only when a licence text is opened, because it is 1.4 MB).
decisions.rationale: They are not rows in the policy tables: no author, version, audience or acceptance applies, and the build, not an administrator, keeps them current.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 5: Licences in the Policies area (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: The Policies page always exists
decisions.statement: It no longer redirects to the front page when nothing is published, and the footer link on every page (signed in or out) is permanent.
decisions.rationale: With no policy readable the page opens on the product licence. This changes the old behaviour that a deployment with no policies showed no trace of the page; the two server-policy e2e steps that asserted the redirect now assert the Licences content.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 5: Licences in the Policies area (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Product licence text
decisions.statement: One constant, `PRODUCT_LICENCE` in `LicencesPanel.tsx`: the GNU General Public License, version 3, with links to the licence text and the upstream source repository.
decisions.rationale: It describes the licence in force today; the licence decision is a later phase and changes this constant, the `LICENSE` file and the package metadata together.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 5: Licences in the Policies area (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Library table
decisions.statement: Held in the browser (1,628 rows, searched by name or licence, sorted on any header, 100 rows per "Show more"), with a detail dialog per row and the licence text on request; a sort is local (`useTableSort`), not in the URL, because the table sits inside another page.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 5: Licences in the Policies area (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Signing is a reviewed repository entry, checked by our own script
decisions.statement: A third-party CLA application would be a vendor with write access to the repository (vendor policy), and a hosted signature store is a second source of truth.
decisions.rationale: The check reads the signatories from the pull request (adding the entry is the signature) and the maintainer and automation lists from the base branch, so a pull request cannot exempt itself. Authors come from the GitHub API login, not commit emails.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 6: licence model (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19, licence model: Package metadata
decisions.statement: `license` is set in `frontend` and `docs/website` `package.json` and their lockfiles' root entries.
decisions.rationale: The two Python projects declare no package metadata (they are tool configuration only), so none is added: adding a `[project]` table would turn them into installable packages. `backend/tests/test_cla_check.py` fails when `LICENSE`, the `package.json` files, the Licences page constant and the commercial summary disagree.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 6: licence model (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19, licence model: Licences page
decisions.statement: `PRODUCT_LICENCE` now names the AGPL and links the commercial licence.
decisions.rationale: AGPL section 13 asks a host that modifies the product to offer its users the modified source; the page's source link is the place a host changes, stated in the website's Licensing page.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 6: licence model (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Stays in Settings
decisions.statement: Messages, Policies, the Workflow group (stage workflows, link types, navigation labels), project statuses, and every module vocabulary and scoring section.
decisions.rationale: The user confirmed these after being asked whether "shared with projects" pulled them in.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 7: Org Resources, review (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Consequence to preserve
decisions.statement: The Reports group mixes a permission gate (`manage_org_report_layouts`, grantable to users and groups) with administrator-only configuration fields.
decisions.rationale: After the move each section keeps its own gate, so a person with only the layout permission sees layouts, packs and snippets and not the configuration. Phase 9 pins this with a test comparing permissions before and after.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 7: Org Resources, review (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Rename, not a second field
decisions.statement: `orgOverviewSections` is now `orgResourceSections` (same `OrgAdminSectionDef` shape).
decisions.rationale: The nine existing sections (Strategy, Future State, Guiding Principle, Personas, Stakeholders, Stakeholder Groups, Request inbox, Compliance by standard, Outstanding) therefore appear on Org Resources in this phase, not phase 9, because the field they are declared in moved; phase 9 moves the core groups and the two `orgAdminSections` record lists. The Overview is dashboards only.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 8: Org Resources page and extension point (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Same menu rules as the admin pages
decisions.statement: The page reuses `adminMenu.ts` (`buildAdminMenuEntries`, `resolveAdminSection`), so a module can group sections, a bare group address opens its first section and an unknown address returns to the page.
decisions.rationale: Redirects keep the query string and hash because a section's filters live in the URL.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 8: Org Resources page and extension point (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Collision rule
decisions.statement: A section whose key is reserved for a core group, repeats another section's key, or uses a group key equal to a section key (or the reverse) is dropped with a console error; `CORE_ORG_RESOURCE_GROUP_KEYS` is empty until phase 9 adds core groups.
decisions.rationale: A story fails if two installed modules collide.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 8: Org Resources page and extension point (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Sub-component filter
decisions.statement: The sub-component state endpoint is administrator-only, so for a member the filter cannot apply and the section is offered; its own endpoints decide what the person may do (the behaviour of `OrgAdminPage`).
decisions.rationale: No section declares a sub-component today. If one must be hidden from members, a member-readable state endpoint is the follow-up; this is recorded rather than built because no section needs it yet.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 8: Org Resources page and extension point (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Navigation highlight
decisions.statement: Organisation overview and Organisation resources are highlighted on their own pages (`alsoActiveOn`); the Overview entry was never highlighted on `/orgs/:id/overview` before.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 8: Org Resources page and extension point (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Access unchanged, pinned
decisions.statement: Layouts, packs and snippets keep their own gate (`manage_org_report_layouts`, which a custom role can grant); the configuration is offered only where `GET .../advanced-settings` (administrators) can be read, and saving sends only the five report fields, which the endpoint applies as a partial update (so the sign-in, email and token settings are untouched).
decisions.rationale: A story covers the hidden configuration for a non-administrator and one asserts the exact five-field payload.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 9: Org Resources, move sections (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Empty state removed
decisions.statement: Core always contributes Reports, so the page can no longer be empty; the string and its story were replaced by one asserting that Reports and Tags remain when every module is off.
decisions.rationale: Core sections follow the modules' so the landing section is a record list where a module contributes one.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 9: Org Resources, move sections (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Project members table: Role cell width
decisions.statement: `MultiSelectDropdown` gains `summaryMaxLength` and `summaryCount`; the members table shows the role names while they fit 28 characters and otherwise "N roles", with the names in the tooltip.
decisions.rationale: (request), threshold
decisions.section: Project members table: last role not clearable, role summary collapses (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Existing codes never change
decisions.statement: The counter is per type, not per prefix, so `DEC-001` to `DEC-005` is followed by `ADR-006` and no number is reused.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 10: record code prefixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Actions follow too
decisions.statement: The Actions generator has its own counter and a literal `ACT`; it now resolves the prefix as well, and the action bundle reads any prefix when it carries a code across (it only accepted `ACT-n`).
decisions.rationale: A requirement is outside the mechanism: its code is built from component and category prefixes.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 10: record code prefixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Code parsers
decisions.statement: Parsers that assumed a fixed prefix or four digits: the Architecture connection-end import cell looked for `-ELM-`, so a shared element under an overridden prefix would not have been found (now splits on the owner code's one hyphen); `label_title` and the frontend `splitArtefactCode` accepted three or four digits.
decisions.rationale: The phase text asked for more than four digits, which would also split a standard named `ISO-27001`; `ISO-9001` was already split wrongly. One reading of the label now exists (`code_rules.split_record_label`, three or more digits, a compliance clause label `<standard> v<version> · <clause>` is never split) with the frontend twin held to it by shared vectors (`artefactCodeCases.json`, read by a story and a backend test).
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 10: record code prefixes (2026-11-19)

decisions.title: Platform review 2026-11-19: Bundles and templates
decisions.statement: The project bundle carries the project's own overrides and the organisation bundle the organisation's; an organisation merge adds only types the target has not set; an entry that no longer fits (type not registered, prefix taken) is skipped with a warning, never failing the import.
decisions.rationale: A project made from a template copies the template's own (a person who does not want that does not set them on the template). A project import numbers its records afresh with the destination's effective prefix. **Found on the way (fixed):** the organisation bundle did not carry the project code policy or "always show the project code", so an import silently reset them; both now travel.
decisions.section: Platform review 2026-11-19, Phase 10: record code prefixes (2026-11-19)

standard.name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (Security and Confidentiality)
standard.description: The 2017 Trust Services Criteria (revised 2022) for Security (CC1 to CC9) and Confidentiality (C1), as assessed in docs/soc2/trust-services-criteria-mapping.md.

criteria.name: Commitment to integrity and ethical values
criteria.control: Company-level code of conduct and ethics policy
criteria.status_note: Organizational action required — Company must adopt and communicate

criteria.name: Board/governance oversight independent of management
criteria.control: Governance structure for the security program
criteria.status_note: Organizational action required

criteria.name: Management establishes structure, authority, and reporting lines
criteria.control: Named information security owner; defined roles for server admin, org admin, engineering, ops
criteria.status_note: Application-level roles exist and are enforced in code (`backend/app/services/rbac.py`); Company-level org chart is a placeholder

criteria.name: Commitment to competence
criteria.control: Hiring, training, and role-appropriate skill requirements
criteria.status_note: Organizational action required

criteria.name: Enforces accountability
criteria.control: Individual accountability for actions is enforced at the system level via per-user audit logging
criteria.evidence: `backend/app/services/audit.py` (`log_event`, records `actor_id` on every mutating action); `LoginEvent` table for authentication events
criteria.status_note: Technically implemented; Company-level performance/accountability process is a placeholder

criteria.name: Obtains/generates quality information to support internal control
criteria.control: System generates structured audit events and login history usable for control monitoring

criteria.name: Internally communicates information necessary for internal control, including objectives and responsibilities
criteria.control: Policies are documented (this package); formal internal communication/training program
criteria.status_note: Documented, but not yet formally communicated/attested by staff — Company action required (the product can record per-person acceptance of published policies once the Company publishes this set there and requires it)

criteria.name: Communicates with external parties (customers, regulators) regarding matters affecting internal control
criteria.control: Customer-facing status/incident communication process; public documentation of the product's security posture
criteria.evidence: [README.md](../../README.md), [enterprise-integration.md](../enterprise-integration.md) describe technical behavior; formal customer notification process
criteria.status_note: Organizational action required

criteria.name: Specifies objectives clearly enough to identify/assess risk
criteria.control: Product requirements and architectural goals are formally documented

criteria.name: Identifies and analyzes risk to objectives, across the entity
criteria.control: Formal, recurring risk assessment process and risk register
criteria.status_note: Process documented as a policy; no risk register or completed assessment exists yet — Company action required

criteria.name: Considers the potential for fraud in assessing risk
criteria.control: Fraud-risk consideration folded into the risk assessment methodology; technical fraud-relevant controls (e.g. self-approval prevention) exist in the product
criteria.evidence: [policies/risk-assessment-policy.md](policies/risk-assessment-policy.md); e.g. a change request's submitter cannot approve their own request (enforced in `backend/app/routers/change_requests.py`, tested in `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/change-request-approval-separation.spec.ts`)

criteria.name: Identifies and assesses changes that could significantly affect internal control
criteria.control: Architectural/security decisions are logged as they're made, including their risk rationale
criteria.evidence: `docs/decisions.md` (ongoing record of every architectural and security decision, including hardening passes)
criteria.status_note: Practice exists and is evidenced; not yet formalized as a standing process independent of engineering activity

criteria.name: Performs ongoing and/or separate evaluations of whether controls are present and functioning
criteria.control: Automated test suites run on every push/PR and function as continuous control evaluation for application-level controls (RBAC boundaries, auth, workflow guarantees); periodic security review passes
criteria.evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; backend pytest suite (~95% line coverage, published per run and failing below 93.2%); Playwright E2E suite; `docs/decisions.md`'s hardening-pass sections

criteria.status_note: A follow-up review found and fixed two endpoints (`deactivate_org_user`, `archive_org_user`) that scoped the caller's role correctly but not the *target* of the action to the same organization — see [policies/access-control-policy.md](policies/access-control-policy.md)

criteria.control: Physical data center security

criteria.status_note: Carve-out to subservice organization — Company must name the provider and reference their report

criteria.name: Discontinues logical/physical access when no longer required

criteria.name: Implements controls to protect against threats from outside system boundaries
criteria.control: TLS termination and network exposure are the deployer's responsibility (the app serves plain HTTP internally by design); CORS origin allow-list; SSRF guard on org-configured OIDC endpoints; per-account lockout on the 2FA challenge step after repeated failed codes
criteria.status_note: The first-factor password check has a progressive delay per account and per source address, the second factor a lockout, and the unauthenticated routes shared limits across workers; the client address is the connecting one (`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`). The front end sends a Content-Security-Policy and HSTS behind an HTTPS proxy. TLS termination remains the operator's — see [policies/access-control-policy.md](policies/access-control-policy.md) Known Gaps

criteria.name: Restricts the transmission, movement, and removal of information to authorized users/processes

criteria.status_note: Authorization-checked endpoints serve files, and the backend reaches the bundled object storage with a single bucket-scoped identity (no other bucket, no bucket listing), and the unauthenticated filer/master APIs are loopback-only; pinned by tests against the live storage service and the compose files. Known limit: the identity can create and delete its own bucket

criteria.name: Prevents or detects and acts upon unauthorized/malicious software
criteria.control: Endpoint/host-level malware protection, dependency vulnerability scanning
criteria.evidence: CI `dependency-scan` job (`pip-audit` for the backend and mcp-server, `npm audit --omit=dev` at high for the frontend and Playwright) and a Trivy scan of every production image before it is pushed (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`); fixable HIGH/CRITICAL findings fail the build
criteria.status_note: Dependency, image, static-analysis (Bandit, Semgrep) and secret (Gitleaks) scanning is automated and gating, and a weekly OWASP ZAP baseline runs against the test stack (`.github/workflows/dynamic-scan.yml`); actions are pinned to commit SHAs. Open: the documentation site's `braces` advisory has no patched release, so that audit is reported, not gating; host-level malware protection and the third-party Compose images are outside this scan — see [policies/change-management-and-secure-development-policy.md](policies/change-management-and-secure-development-policy.md). **Note (modular feature system):** the modular feature system's third-party discovery sources (Python entry points, `EXTRA_MODULES_PATH`) are gated behind `ALLOW_EXTERNAL_MODULES`, default `false` — a deliberate, documented mitigation layered on top of this still-open gap (a plugin-loading mechanism that can auto-import and run third-party code materially raises the stakes of having no automated scanning), not a closure of it; see [policies/vendor-and-subprocessor-management-policy.md](policies/vendor-and-subprocessor-management-policy.md) point 7 and its Known Gaps entry. **Note (module system follow-up, 2026-09-07 — Tier C / Module Federation):** a Tier C frontend module raises these same stakes further still, not merely in the same way as point 7's backend module — it runs with **no sandbox at all** (same origin/DOM/cookies/component tree as the host), where a backend module is at least bounded by the backend process's own authorization checks and Tier B (the modular feature system's *other* dynamic frontend option) is bounded by an iframe sandbox. Gated by the same `ALLOW_EXTERNAL_MODULES` flag, not a second one; see [policies/vendor-and-subprocessor-management-policy.md](policies/vendor-and-subprocessor-management-policy.md) point 8 and its Known Gaps entry 5.

criteria.name: Detects and monitors for configuration changes and vulnerabilities that could introduce risk
criteria.control: Container health checks; optional Prometheus/Loki/Tempo/Grafana Alloy observability stack; disk-usage monitor with alerting

criteria.control: Incident classification process

criteria.evidence: [policies/data-classification-and-confidentiality-policy.md](policies/data-classification-and-confidentiality-policy.md); `backend/app/services/rbac.py`; `backend/app/models/encrypted_type.py`; `backend/app/services/record_policy.py` (personal data in record exports and imports); [system-description.md](system-description.md) §7
